News.title: ‘It’s the Wonka event all over again’ – Xmas market is slammed for looking ‘nothing like promised’ with just FIVE stalls
News.content:
Next

A CHRISTMAS market has been branded as “rubbish” and a “rip-off” after visitors complained it looked “nothing like promised” with only five stalls.

Visitors have called out the AI material used to promote the event, with one saying “it’s like the Wonka event all over again“.



Cornwall’s Kernow Christmas Market has faced backlash from locals after the festive event was found to look nothing like it was advertised.

AI promotional material presented images of a market hall space decorated with Christmas trees, baubles, wreaths and fairylights, but the reality is what one visitor branded as “awful”.



Held at Pool Market in Redruth, the event saw stallholders pay Cornwall’s Winter Wonderland to take part, which already drew criticism after it was not ready on the opening day as planned.

Both Cornwall’s Winter Wonderland and Kernow Christmas Market were supposed to run from Friday, November 20 to January 3, according to CornwallLive.

However, the “winter wonderland” aspect was cancelled on Sunday, November 22 due to “high wind speeds” in the area.

In addition to the already turbulent start to Cornwall’s festivities, one visitor claimed the market was “nothing like promised”, closing at 4pm instead of the advertised 8pm.



Dozens also said that the festive-looking entrance shots advertised on social media were “nothing like promised” when it came to the reality, with one hailing it as “AI slop”.

Another user took to Facebook to say “it’s like the Wonka event all over again”, referencing a spectacularly bad “Willy Wonka experience” that led to police being called in Glasgow back in 2024.

Inside, images show only a handful of stalls in a larger warehouse space, with limited Christmas decorations.

One visitor commented on Facebook: “I was absolutely disgusted when we walked into the supposedly Christmas market” and that there were “no decorations, no lights. Nothing!”

They also said that vendors were reportedly charged £300 to run a stall at the Kernow Christmas Market, and that they should “get a refund”.



Kernow Christmas Market said on its Facebook: “We know things weren’t quite how everyone expected, and we completely understand the disappointment.

“Unfortunately, the Cornish weather and a number of last-minute challenges have caused delays, but we’re determined to make improvements ready for next weekend!

“Kernow Christmas Market is organised and operated by Pool Market, running alongside Cornwall Winter Wonderland.

“The team at Pool Market are a more traditional, long-standing team who don’t have access to social media, so Cornwall Winter Wonderland kindly helps with advertising, social media and booking stalls on their behalf.

“However, the organisation, layout and running of the actual Christmas market remain the responsibility of Pool Market.



“Now that Cornwall Winter Wonderland is getting up and running, their team will be lending a hand with decorating and improving the market ahead of next weekend!

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We want to create a much more magical Christmas atmosphere for everyone!”

Cornwall’s Winter Wonderland has also confirmed its full event will open today, including both the Ice Rink and the Kernow Lodge.

News.title: Horror moment girls, 4 & 8, on suspended swing are injured as spotlight collapses in front of shocked parents at circus
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horror moment two girls are injured after a spotlight collapses and falls on them in front of shocked parents at a circus.

The children, aged four and eight, cheated death when the heavy lighting rig crashed into their swing as they dangled 25ft above a stage.



The terrifying ordeal occurred in Tomsk, Russia, when the youngsters were given a ride during an intermission in the travelling troupe’s performance.

Shocking footage caught the moment the huge lighting rig collapsed before hitting their swing.



Screams rang out as circus workers panicked while trying to lower the swing and the two petrified children.

By a stroke of luck, the girls were not thrown out of the swing nor electrocuted by the crashing lighting rig.



One witness called Sergey Kulikov said: “The girls are alive.

“I called an ambulance; the younger one was taken to hospital with a strap around her neck and complaining of pain in her arm.



“We were all very frightened.”

The grandfather of one of the victims said they were “frightened but alive” after the girls were rushed to hospital.

“They were taken away by ambulance,” he said.

“They are both in the hospital now.

“There is some redness on their faces.



“They were struck by a wire or a rope.”

The four-year-old girl was described as “frightened,” suffering haematomas to her head and shoulder.

The child was kept in hospital under medical observation, said a REN TV source.

A criminal investigation has been launched into the children’s ride by the Crimean-based Orion Circus as part of their show called Wild Carnival.

One report said: “For an additional fee, children were being given rides on suspended swings beneath the circus tent’s cupola.



“At that moment, the structure holding the lighting equipment broke loose and struck the swings…

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The Investigative Committee has opened a criminal case regarding the provision of services that fail to meet safety standards.”

News.title: Brit, 40, ‘repeatedly sexually assaulted girl after getting into her bed & shower’ as he faces 10 years in Majorcan jail
News.content:
‘PREDATOR’ SNARED Brit, 40, ‘repeatedly sexually assaulted girl after getting into her bed & shower’ as he faces 10 years in Majorcan jail







Next

A BRIT who allegedly sexually assaulted a schoolgirl when she was as young as five is facing ten years in jail if convicted.

The lawyer, 40, who works as a tax advisor on Majorca, is accused of repeatedly sexually assaulting the child when she was aged between five and nine.



He allegedly sexually abused the girl after getting into her bed and interrupting her showers.

The Brit man has been warned ahead of his trial in Palma he faces ten years behind bars if found guilty.



Prosecutors alleged the abuse happened “on numerous occasions” over the course of four years, between 2012 and 2016.

They said the alleged victim had been admitted to hospital several times after repeated attempts to take her own life.



The child has experienced “a situation of chronic stress over time”, according to the indictment.

Prosecutors said her relationships with other people had been affected by the alleged abuse.

The man has been charged with continuous sexual abuse and sexual assault.

The second charge refers to an incident in 2016, when the man allegedly went into a bathroom where the girl had been showering and sexually assaulted her.



Prosecutors are demanding a 10-year prison sentence and decade-long restraining order for the man if he is convicted.

They also want the man to pay £25,000 compensation to his alleged victim.

He will testify tomorrow, representing himself under the supervision of a lawyer.

The alleged victim’s mother is also expected to take the stand, as well as police and forensic experts.

The trial is expected to last two days at Palma’s Audiencia Provincial Court.



It comes after a Swedish man was arrested on suspicion of sexually assaulting multiple children at a hotel on the same island last month.

He is accused of approaching several children before “hugging and touching them” without their consent.

The man attempted to touch a five-year-old boy who was sat with family in the hotel’s entertainment area, cops said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hotel staff allegedly witnessed the man approaching multiple children.

His arrest came as cops arrested another man on suspicion of a rape in the toilet of a nightclub in the Playa de Palma resort.

News.title: We live in UK’s iconic ‘triangle village’ – but we’re locked in bitter row over plans to change our unique homes forever
News.content:
SHARP DIVIDE We live in UK’s iconic ‘triangle village’ – but we’re locked in bitter row over plans to change our unique homes forever







Next

RESIDENTS of an iconic triangular village are battling plans for 200 new homes – because they fear it would change shape.

Locals of Failand in Somerset are fighting developers who want to build the homes on the edge of the distinctive community as they say it won’t be a triangle anymore.



The ‘Failand Triangle’ is currently made up of 350 homes between Clevedon Road, Weston Road, and Flax Bourton Road.

But the new homes would see the village spread beyond its distinctive triangle shape.



Hill Residential first submitted an application in December last year and the developers have now appealed to the government planning inspectorate claiming the council was stalling on a decision.

The triangle was originally known as the Sixty Acre Plantation, but development around the edges began in the postwar period.



The interior of the “Failand Triangle” began to be filled out from the 1970s onwards.

But development has not spread beyond the triangle as it is surrounded by the green belt.

More than 250 locals pleaded with the council to turn it down – but the decision will now be made at a six-day inquiry listed for April next year.

Maria Payne, councilor for Wraxall and Failand Parish Council said: “The triangle is what defines the settlement of the village of Failand.

“You are completely breaking the boundary off the triangle. The local plan is very clear that the boundary shouldn’t be broken.”



Sandra Roberts, 61, said: “I was brought up here and it’s been known as the triangle.

“When I was in the village school we used to go on runs and it used to be how many times we used to go around the triangle and that’s how it’s always been.

“You get a lot of wildlife and see deer there.



“It just doesn’t feel the right fit for here. The traffic is so much now and Flax Bourton is a rat run.”

Another local Charlie Barker, 23, said: “It would destroy the whole village. We don’t want it. There’s not enough infrastructure for it anyway.

“I’ve seen in various places near here there’s been similar developments that have gone up.

“What are you going to do? Stick a little driveway on the side of the road here and then there’s going to be a big a housing estate in the field, it’s going to be ugly.

Another local, known as Mrs Baker, 60, said: “It’s always been known as the Failand triangle.



“We look out from our living room window and we see wild rabbits a lot over there. Their natural habitat will be destroyed – and the whole area will change completely.”

But North Somerset Council said they had verbally agreed to extend the application deadline until the end of July.

It said: “However, despite several requests, the appellant refused to confirm the agreed extension of time in writing.”

Hill Residential is set to argue at the planning inquiry that the land it wants to build on is “grey belt” and it will deliver much needed housing.

Their statement of case states: “It will deliver substantial benefits and the need for the scheme is compelling.”



Although North Somerset Council accepts that the greenfield site is technically “grey belt,” its lawyers will propose that it is not in a sustainable location and so should still be turned down.

Its statement of case argued: “The proposal, due to its position in open countryside and poorly connected to essential services, facilities and infrastructure, would be in an unsustainable location and constitute inappropriate development in the green belt.”

A spokesperson for North Somerset Council said: “The Council opposes this development because it represents inappropriate development in the green belt and would be in an unsustainable location, with poor access to schools, shops and other services.

“The developer has appealed to the Planning Inspectorate and the scheme will be considered at a public inquiry in April 2027.”

Hill Residential were approached for comment.

News.title: New ban on ‘rip-off’ tourist fares and ‘blaring music’ is coming into force this WEEK in major crackdown
News.content:
Next

A NEW ban on pedicabs that charge “rip off” fares and “blare out” loud music is coming into force in London this week.

The major crackdown comes after some people were charged up to £500 for a 10-minute ride.

As of Friday (November 27), drivers must also undergo enhanced DBS (Disclosure and Barring Services) checks.



There will also be a clampdown on firms who operate pedicabs, with drivers only allowed to charge a £5 base fare and up to £1 a minute for each ride across the capital.



Drivers will also be required to hold a full driving licence or valid theory test certificate.

They must also meet English language requirements, while under the new rules operators of the vehicles must keep records and carry out fire assessment risks on premises.

All pedicab vehicles will have to display a valid licence from February 2027.



Sadiq Khan, the Mayor of London, said: “After years of campaigning, I’m pleased that TfL will be regulating pedicabs across the capital to ensure they meet proper operational standards.

“Pedicabs should be a fun way to explore London – but too often people face rip-off fares, blaring music and unsafe behaviour.

“We’re bringing in these new rules so that both customers and drivers can benefit from an industry that is more safe, reliable and professional.

“This will play an important role in supporting our vital night-time economy and enabling more people to enjoy all that our great city has to offer as we continue building a safer, fairer, greener London for everyone.”



The regulations coming into effect on Friday also require drivers to undergo enhanced criminal checks.

News.title: Burnham slammed after letting TikTok star recreate Hugh Grant’s famous Love Actually dance inside No10 in ‘cringe’ video
News.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham has been slammed for letting a TikTok star do Hugh Grant’s famous Love Actually dance inside No10.

Influencer Luke Hamnett, who has around 1.3 million followers, was invited into Downing Street to give the PM a softball interview for his podcast.



Mr Hamnett filmed himself copying the scene from the film, in which Grant’s Prime Minister dances through Number 10 to “Jump” by the Pointer Sisters.

Critics have accused the PM of avoiding tough questions from political reporters and cosying up to social media stars instead.



In the interview, Mr Hamnett told Mr Burnham: “I really, really do think you’re doing a really good job, and I won’t just blow smoke up your a—, I’m genuinely just saying that I think you’re doing a great job.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said being relatable does not mean treating the public like children who need entertaining.



She added: “When I was a new MP, we had to hand in our phones as we stepped into 10 Downing St, so it’s jarring to see a Labour PM turn it into a bit of a joke.

“Hugh Grant could dance through No 10 in Love Actually because he was pretending to be Prime Minister. Andy Burnham actually IS the Prime Minister.



“At a time when Trump, Xi and Putin are projecting power on the world stage, and people across Britain are anxious about the future, this looks extremely unserious. Being relatable doesn’t mean treating the public as though they are children who need entertaining.”

Mr Burnham has favoured sitting down with influencers and Instagram stars, and took just two questions from journalists at the UK-EU summit.

Before becoming PM, he also held an “Ask Me Anything” session on Reddit, inviting users to send in their questions.

Reform chairman Lee Anderson said: “I’ve never heard of ‘Live, Laugh, Luke. But I have heard of Annoying Andy who doesn’t understand that most people are just trying to live, work, and pay the heating bill.

“If the Prime Minister has got time to be prancing about doing Love Actually dances for TikTok, it tells you everything you need to know about this government’s priorities.”



TaxPayers’ Alliance campaigns director William Yarwood said Downing Street was becoming an influencer circus “while hardworking taxpayers are left wondering who’s footing the bill.”

He added: “Number 10 must reveal how much money is being spent on these influencer spectacles and stop using taxpayers’ cash to bankroll political PR.”

News.title: World-famous TV wine expert dies aged just 46 after devastating diagnosis only months ago
News.content:
Next

A WORLD-famous wine expert who shot to fame in a hit documentary has died aged just 46 following a devastating cancer battle.

Ian Cauble, a celebrated Master Sommelier and father-of-two, died on Thursday, just months after being diagnosed with a rare and aggressive form of lymphoma.



The beloved TV star had been receiving hospice care at his home in Napa, California, after the disease spread despite treatment.

His death, has sparked an outpouring of grief across the wine industry, with devastated friends and colleagues paying tribute to his infectious enthusiasm and generosity.



Cauble leaves behind his wife, Mercedes Lam, and their two young children, Charlotte and Hayden.

The wine guru received his shock diagnosis in late spring 2026, leaving him just months to battle the deadly disease, the Daily Mail reported.

Read more California news FAMILY MURDER Wife & daughter arrested 4 years after man’s SEVERED HEAD found in trash bag

Friends launched a GoFundMe campaign on November 7 to support his family as his condition deteriorated.

The fundraiser, which has attracted more than $370,000 in donations by Monday, revealed that doctors had determined his cancer was no longer treatable.

“Although Ian and his medical team did everything possible to treat it quickly, the cancer spread to other parts of the body and is now past the treatment phase,” organizers wrote before his death.

The money raised will reportedly help cover medical bills and provide financial security for his widow and children.



Cauble became an international sensation after appearing in the acclaimed 2012 documentary SOMM, which followed four aspiring wine experts attempting to pass one of the world’s toughest professional exams.

The grueling Master Sommelier qualification requires candidates to identify wines through blind tastings and demonstrate extraordinary knowledge of the industry.



Although Cauble failed the examination during filming, he eventually passed in 2012, becoming just the 197th person worldwide to earn the prestigious title.

His remarkable knowledge and charismatic personality helped turn the documentary into a cult favorite.

But it was his kindness and passion for introducing others to fine wine that friends remembered most following his death.

The team behind the SOMM films shared an emotional tribute on Instagram.

“Ian Cauble brought passion to every day, every minute, every second. He changed our lives forever. He accomplished so much and he never hurt anyone along the way. We will miss our friend so much,” they wrote.



Documentary director Jason Wise also shared a heartbreaking farewell on X.

“He changed my life so much, but all I can think about are the little moments – crazy late nights and early hangovers, all the trouble we got in around the world, the flights we missed, and the things I could never write here. wish I could thank him one more time. Goodbye Ian,” he wrote.

Born in Huntington Beach, California, Cauble discovered his passion for wine while studying at Sonoma State University.

He later traveled to Portugal for a harvest internship before returning to California to pursue his career.

Following his documentary success, he co-founded online wine retailer SommSelect in 2014, aiming to make exceptional wines more accessible.



He also appeared in Somm: Into the Bottle and Somm 3, cementing his reputation as one of the industry’s most recognizable personalities.

Former business partner Brandon Carneiro told the Napa Valley Register: “Ian always had an extraordinary gravity. People were drawn into his orbit by his enthusiasm and his genuine love for others.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His family said his influence extended far beyond the wine world.

“Ian’s impact on the culinary world has been deeply meaningful, and the way Ian has shared a love of life through travel, food, and wine has touched so many people,” the fundraiser read.

News.title: Driving instructor who ‘poisoned’ dad’s mind against his own brother after row over wedding seat loses £400k will fight
News.content:
SEAT DECEIT Driving instructor who ‘poisoned’ dad’s mind against his own brother after row over wedding seat loses £400k will fight







Next

A DRIVING instructor locked in a bitter row with his own brother sparked by seating at a wedding has lost a £400k battle for their dad’s inheritance.

Harish Verma, 57, and his wife, Paramjit “poisoned” his elderly dad’s mind against his older brother, convincing the frail 89-year-old that the rest of his family had abandoned him.



The couple are said to have plotted to snatch every penny of Gowerdhan Dass’s fortune by getting him to tear up his old will just three months before he died in February 2024.

That left cabbie brother Bani Verma, 67, and the rest of his family with nothing.



Bani went on to sue, claiming his brother had “unduly influenced” their ailing dad to rip up 2015 will.

After a week-long showdown at Central London County Court, a judge branded the pair “undoubtedly fraudulent” and ripped up the sham will.



The Judge said: “Harish did make false representations to Mr Dass

“The false representations were made for the purpose of inducing Mr Dass to alter his testamentary disposition and Harish made such representations knowing them to be untrue.”



Harish has now been stripped of his £100,000 share of his father’s home in Slough and hit with a £115,000 up-front legal bill – leaving him worse off than when he started.

The court heard that the bad blood between the brothers had been festering for 30 years over missing stock at a corner ship and an unpaid £5,000 loan that was meant to bankroll Harish’s failed dream of becoming a DJ.

Things exploded at Bani’s daughter’s wedding in 2011 when Harish and Paramjit tried to sit on reserved seats at the family reception.



Told the chairs were taken, Harish stormed out in a huff; a move Bani saw as a deliberate slap in the face in front of both families.

When Harish later barred Bani from visiting their dad at his home, the rift became permanent.

Grilled in the witness box, Harish bluntly admitted he didn’t just dislike his older brother, he “he actually hates him”.

In a desperate bid to hang on to the cash, Harish tried to paint Bani as a heartless son who turned his back on their dad and mocked his memory.

Harish’s lawyers claimed Bani treated his dad’s funeral “as if it were a wedding” joking around while wearing a loud tartan Tam-o-Shanter hat.



They pointed to a damning clause in Gowerdhan’s November 2023 will, which cut Bani out entirely because they had “little to no contact” and Bani had his own money.

Mr Dass’ last will of 2024 included a specific clause which stated: “I declare that no provision is made in this Will for my son BANI PARSHAD VERMA as there has been little to no contact for many years and my son is not financially dependent upon me and has his own wealth and financial resources.”

Harish claimed he had been silent next to his dad at the solicitor’s office because he didn’t think it was his place to correct him.

Recorder Jonathan Cohen KC saw straight through the act.

While accepting the couple cared for Gowerdhan – a gentle former Heathrow security guard who loved making pickles – the judge ruled they exploited his vulnerability for cash.



He found Harish sat by knowing full well his dad’s claims that relatives had cut him off were completely untrue.

Recorder Cohen said: “Harish and Paramjit did poison Mr Dass’s mind so as to believe these untrue statements, which both knew were untrue and were for their own financial gain.

“There is no other sensible explanation. They were undoubtedly fraudulent.”

The court heard Paramjit even blocked another daughter-in-law from seeing Gowerdhan after the new will was signed.

This took place as the pair secretly plotted to sell his home and pocket the cash to buy a place together.



The judge reinstated Gowerdhan’s 2015 will, splitting the £400,000 pot four ways between Bani, Harush and the families of two late siblings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But he ordered Harish and Paramjit to pay Bani’s legal costs as well as their own massive court bills.

These costs completely wiped out Harish’s £100,000 windfall.

News.title: Doctor shares 6 Christmas dinner swaps for Mounjaro and Wegovy users
News.content:
Doctor shares 6 Christmas dinner swaps for Mounjaro and Wegovy users

A GP has shared simple ways to enjoy festive favourites while helping to avoid an unwelcome side effect

View 3 Images Millions of people across the UK take weight-loss jabs (Image: Getty Images)

Christmas dinner is one of the biggest meals of the year, but for people taking popular weight-loss medicines, the traditional spread can bring some unwanted challenges. With nearly one in 10 British households now including someone using a GLP-1 medication, a GP has shared six ways to make the festive meal easier to manage.

‌



‌



Research by Numerator found that 8.5 per cent of households in Great Britain had someone using a GLP-1 weight-loss medicine in August. Asda Online Doctor has also reported a 29 per cent rise in orders for its weight-loss treatments over the past year.

‌



Dr Crystal Wyllie, GP at Asda Online Doctor, says medicines such as Mounjaro and Wegovy can cause nausea and other digestive side effects, particularly when people eat large or high-fat meals. She said: "Being on weight loss medication such as Wegovy or Mounjaro doesn’t mean you have to miss out on enjoying your favourite festive foods, as with a few simple swaps, you can still enjoy the day and limit nausea and stomach upset."

‌



Ensure our latest Health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

1. Build a balanced plate

Dr Wyllie recommends filling half the plate with vegetables, a quarter with lean protein and the remaining quarter with carbohydrates. Starting with a smaller portion and eating slowly can help people recognise when they are full.

View 3 Images A balanced plate (Image: Getty Images)

‌



2. Choose boiled potatoes or lighter mash

Rather than roast potatoes cooked in oil or goose fat, try boiled new potatoes or mash made with a little milk instead of butter. Herbs such as rosemary and thyme can add flavour without piling on extra fat.

3. Pick leaner meat

Turkey breast and skinless chicken are lighter alternatives to fattier choices such as duck, pigs in blankets and some cuts of beef or pork. Fish can also make a festive centrepiece for anyone looking for another option.

‌



4. Try ginger tea

A cup of ginger tea between courses may help some people manage feelings of nausea, Dr Wyllie says. She suggests steeping fresh slices of root ginger in hot water for five to 10 minutes.

View 3 Images Ginger tea (Image: Getty Images)

‌



5. Start and finish with something lighter

A prawn cocktail salad could provide a cooler, lighter starter, while Greek yoghurt topped with cinnamon, clementine or cranberries offers an alternative to heavier Christmas pudding. Dr Wyllie says strong food smells can also make nausea worse for some people.

6. Be mindful of alcohol

Alcohol can aggravate nausea, vomiting and dehydration, so limiting it or choosing a festive mocktail may be a better option. Anyone who does drink should consider smaller measures, water between drinks and avoiding alcohol on an empty stomach.

Article continues below

Dr Wyllie also warns against taking a break from medication simply to eat more freely. She said: "I’d caution against skipping doses or going on a medication vacation so you can eat whatever you like." People should speak to their prescriber before changing or stopping treatment.

News.title: Manchester Co-op Live: Don Toliver gig evacuated and 50 assessed after ‘unknown substance’ released
News.content:
The Co-op Live venue in Manchester was evacuated at 10pm on Sunday after an unknown substance, initially thought to be tear gas, was released while fans enjoyed the US rapper Don Toliver's show

Around 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert in Manchester after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.

One person has been hospitalised and "several" others are being assessed for injuries after the substance - which police initially believed to be tear gas - was released towards the end of US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena on Sunday night.

Videos show gig-goers making a swift exit to the concourse, coughing and covering their faces. At around 10pm, the show was officially cancelled and fans were told to leave.

Greater Manchester declared a major incident to allow emergency services to "work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response". Armed police, ambulances and fire engines were pictured outside Co-op Live, Britain's largest indoor venue.

News.title: Heart doctor names one sign on waist that's most powerful way to reduce heart risk
News.content:
Heart doctor names one sign on waist that's most powerful way to reduce heart risk

Dr Paddy Barrett has been a cardiologist for more than 10 years.

View Image A heart doctor has names one sign on your waist that's a "most powerful" way to reduce heart risk (Image: Getty)

A heart doctor has named a sign on your waist that is one of the "most powerful" ways to reduce your risk of heart disease. Heart disease, also called cardiovascular disease or CVD, can be a silent killer because in many instances there will be no symptoms. The first symptom for many people may actually be having a heart attack or stroke. There are several symptoms and risk factors you should be aware of, and you can read them below.

‌



‌



But Dr Paddy Barrett has named 10 ways we can all reduce the risk of heart disease — and they are all achievable and easy to understand. Dr Barrett is a consultant cardiologist at Blackrock Health, which has five clinics across Ireland. Writing on Facebook, he named his "10 most powerful ways to reduce heart disease risk", though he stressed they didn't provide "guarantees" of heart health but reduced your odds of developing problems.

‌



Optimise all your risk factors: Dr Barrett said a study found nine modifiable factors "accounted for ~90% of heart attack risk at population level" and added: "Tackle cholesterol, blood pressure, glucose, diet, activity and smoking together."

Lower LDL cholesterol: Every 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) reduction cuts major vascular events ~22% over 5 years, said Dr Barrett. ‌



Heart disease symptoms

Fellow cardiologist Dr Jeremy London named a surprising symptom on the front of your leg that your heart may be in trouble. The British Heart Foundation lists nine symptoms that could mean you have heart disease:

Chest pain: One of the most common signs of a heart attack. Of course, chest pain doesn't always mean heart disease but the BHF says "if it’s a heart attack, this pain may feel like heaviness, tightness or pressure in the chest — people often describe it as ‘an elephant’ standing on their chest or ‘a tight band’ around it". They say pain may also spread to your arm, neck, upper back or stomach.

News.title: Prince William contributes to mental health book inspired by Sam West, 15, who died by suicide
News.content:
Prince William contributes to mental health book inspired by Sam West, 15, who died by suicide

The Prince of Wales has shared a heartfelt message in a new book exploring mental health, grief and loneliness. The collection was inspired by campaigner Ben West's brother, Sam, who died by suicide aged 15

View 3 Images Prince William spoke about the importance of human connection (Image: Getty Images)

Prince William has written a touching foreword for a new book encouraging conversations around mental health, featuring letters from people across the world.

‌



‌



The Prince of Wales has contributed to Reasons to…, a collection of anonymous letters exploring grief, loneliness, joy and other personal experiences. The book aims to encourage conversations around mental health and bring people together through shared experiences. It is written by mental health campaigner Ben West, is set to be released in January 2027.

‌



In his foreword, William said: “At its heart, this project is about starting conversations, however imperfect or uncomfortable they may feel. It connects those who write with those who read, people who may never meet, yet share something profoundly human: the need to feel connected.”

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Reasons to... is set to be released in January

The book follows the success of the Reasons to Stay project, which was launched by Ben in January 2026 in honour of his brother, Sam, who died by suicide in January 2018 at the age of 15.

‌



Explaining why he launched the project, Ben said: “Through complete shock and devastation, I realised that I wanted to stop what happened to Sam from happening to anyone else ever again.”

Ben said Sam was a mental health campaigner who, while experiencing depression, had put up posters around his school to support others going through similar struggles. He said: “I have no doubt that had Sam survived, he would be doing this work himself. He cared deeply about others, had a strong sense of social justice and spent so much of his shortened life making others happy.”

‌



View 3 Images Ben West pictured with his late brother Sam (Image: iambenwest/Instagram)

Ben added: “I will make sure that what started as a devastating and tragic story, ends as a story of change and hope. Sam lives on in the lives that my work touches, some of whom are still here because of it. That is my why. It’s the reason behind everything I do.”

‌



The suicide prevention initiative allows people to write anonymous letters to strangers who may be going through difficult times, offering messages of support and encouragement. Since its launch, more than five million letters have been delivered to people across the world, with the project reaching over 80 million people in 160 countries.

The forthcoming book draws on 120,000 anonymous submissions, sharing personal reflections on life’s challenges and the importance of human connection.

Article continues below

Reasons to… will be published by Penguin on January 14, 2027.

News.title: Pharmacist ‘get help straight away’ alert for anyone taking amlodipine with symptom
News.content:
Pharmacist ‘get help straight away’ alert for anyone taking amlodipine with symptom

A TikTok pharmacist has explained why one symptom should never be ignored

View 2 Images Amlodipine may cause some serious side effects (Image: Getty Images)

People taking a commonly prescribed heart medication are being reminded that it may not protect them from every warning sign. Pharmacist Raj Patel has shared an important message about what to do if a particular symptom suddenly appears or becomes worse.

‌



‌



The Straight Talking Pharmacist on TikTok has more than 100,000 followers and regularly shares advice about medicines. In a recent video, he explained how amlodipine works and why people taking it should understand what the tablets can and cannot do.

‌



Amlodipine is prescribed to treat high blood pressure and angina, a type of chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle. According to the NHS, it belongs to a group of medicines called calcium channel blockers, which relax blood vessels and make it easier for blood to flow.

‌



View 2 Images Amlodipine is another common medication used to treat high blood pressure in Ireland.

For people taking it for angina, the medicine can improve blood supply to the heart muscle and help prevent chest pain. However, it does not provide immediate relief during a sudden angina attack, as Patel was keen to emphasise.

"You won't feel this happening and not feeling anything doesn't mean your tablet isn't working," the pharmacist explained. "It does not treat sudden chest pain if this happens."

‌



His key warning was that people should not wait for symptoms to settle if they are experiencing potentially serious chest pain: "If your chest pain is sudden, isn't settling or getting worse, you should seek help straight away."

‌



NHS guidance says to call 999 if chest pain comes on suddenly and does not go away, or if it spreads to the arms, neck, jaw, stomach or back. Sweating, feeling sick, light-headedness or breathlessness alongside chest pain are also reasons to call an ambulance, as these can be signs of a heart attack.

Anyone with diagnosed angina whose symptoms are becoming worse, happening more often, lasting longer or occurring at rest should also seek urgent medical advice through NHS 111. The British Heart Foundation stresses that chest pain which does not settle after a few minutes of rest could be a heart attack and needs emergency help.

Article continues below

Amlodipine should be taken as prescribed, and the NHS warns against stopping it suddenly without speaking to a doctor. Mr Patel's message is that feeling no immediate difference from the medicine does not mean it is failing, but new or worsening chest pain must never be ignored.

News.title: Russia warns of 'painful consequences' after Ukraine blows up warship
News.content:
Russia warns of 'painful consequences' after Ukraine blows up warship

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky earlier confirmed that Ukraine was behind an attack that sank a 150m Russian warship off Libya

View Image

The Kremlin has warned that Ukraine will face "highly painful consequences" after Kyiv blew up a £150m Russian warship docked in Libya.

‌



‌



Ukraine said it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Benghazi - the de facto capital of Libya's eastern administration - in the early hours of Sunday.

‌



Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on X on Monday that his country had deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones against the Russian corvette Merkury. He hailed the hits - which come as Ukraine steps up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines - as "an exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia's war".

‌



Reacting to the attack, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday: "These actions result in highly painful consequences for the Kyiv regime." He added: "I would like to recall a statement made by Putin in Shenzhen, in which he affirmed that this practice, this course of action by our military will continue."

Authorities in eastern Libya said a Russian ship docked at Benghazi port was hit, causing an explosion but no casualties, before a second ship, a merchant vessel, was targeted off the coast of Benghazi "by explosive-laden sea drones".

Ukraine's SBU security service said the corvette Merkury "regularly escorted enemy maritime convoys" and was part of Russia's Black Sea Fleet. "A Ka-27 multipurpose helicopter was on board the corvette and also sank," the SBU said.

‌



It comes as Russian attacks in the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people over the weekend, including a teenager. A seven-year-old boy was pulled alive from the rubble after spending nearly 14 hours trapped beneath a collapsed building in the town of Dymer.

The Russia-backed administration in eastern Libya said it will launch a joint investigation with Russia.

‌



Libya is split between rival administrations - one in the east led by strongman Khalifa Haftar and another in the west led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah in Tripoli, whose government is internationally recognised.

The country has never recovered from the turmoil that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled long-time dictator Muammar Gaddafi.

‌



The rival UN-recognised government in Tripoli said in a statement that it was alarmed by "risks posed by involving civilian ports and facilities in activities linked to external conflicts".

Zelensky named the second ship as the dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, "which the enemy used to transport weapons".

Article continues below

The UN mission in Libya, UNSMIL, expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X.

News.title: Dementia warning as UK hit by cold snap - full list of guidance as ‘they could forget’
News.content:
Dementia warning as UK hit by cold snap - full list of guidance as ‘they could forget’

One of the UK's leading dementia charities has advice for people caring for someone with dementia on how to support them in the cold weather this winter

View 2 Images There are extra steps carers should take when looking after people with dementia in the wintertime - file image (Image: Getty)

One of the UK’s leading dementia charities has issued a warning as the UK is hit by a bitter cold snap. The Met Office says that snow is likely at times across parts of the UK in the days ahead as winter truly digs in.

‌



‌



Now Dementia UK has issued a full list of guidance for the carers of people with dementia as temperatures fall. The specialist dementia nursing charity warns that people with dementia “could forget to turn on the heating and may not wear appropriate clothing, so it’s important to be prepared to manage temperatures during the colder period.”

‌



The organisation’s specialist Admiral Nurses work with families to provide important advice and support. According to the NHS, almost one million people in the UK have dementia. Dementia UK says one in two Brits will be affected by dementia - either by caring for someone who has it, by developing it themselves, or both. The Alzheimer's Society also warns: "Winter can be a particularly difficult time for somebody living with dementia.

‌



"The bad weather and colder temperatures can bring specific challenges, and can sometimes make symptoms temporarily worse. What’s more, people with dementia aren’t always able to communicate the fact they’re cold - or they may not even recognise it themselves."

Free school meals update after 2 eligibility rule changes - key details READ MORE :

The condition is a syndrome or group of related symptoms linked to an ongoing decline of brain functioning. The charity says that people with dementia encounter communication difficulties that may mean they are not able to explain to anyone when they feel cold.

Dementia UK list of guidance to help people with dementia this winter

Temperatures: Try to keep the main living areas between at least 18 and 21 degrees, or warmer if the person with dementia prefers. Dementia UK says the rest of the house can be less warm.

‌



For those who cannot heat all rooms, the advice is to heat the living room during the day and the bedroom just before the person goes to bed. You can use hot water bottles and electric blankets to maintain warm temperatures during the night.

Layers: Dementia UK says people with dementia should be encouraged to wear lots of thin layers. Cotton, wool or fleecy fibres are the best options to go for. It is also a good idea to encourage them to wear a scarf or hat indoors if they are cold because a lot of heat escapes through the head.

‌



Stimulation: If it’s cold, people with dementia can end up being cooped up indoors for long periods. Carers should think about playing games and puzzles to stimulate both the person with dementia and the carer themselves.

Simple indoor exercises and movement can also help someone with dementia to keep warm and healthy, Dementia UK says.

‌



View 2 Images Britain is set for some snow in the coming days, the Met Office says (Image: Getty)

Food and drink: Ensure people with dementia have regular meals and snacks across the day, as well as hot drinks. This can help keep up their energy levels.

‌



Flu: It’s important to consider a flu jab for someone with dementia. If you have not already, you may be able to get one for free depending on eligibility . Getting flu is one of the main reasons people with dementia go to hospital - something that can raise distress levels and worsen their symptoms.

Vitamins: It can be hard to get the right amount of sunlight during the winter. This can reduce Vitamin D intake. In order to boost bone strength and the immune system, carers for people with dementia should consider Vitamin D supplements.

‌



If anyone needs advice or support on living with dementia, contact Dementia UK’s Admiral Nurse dementia helpline on 0800 888 6678. Alternatively, email helpline@dementiauk.org. For more information on helping someone with dementia during the winter time, visit the Dementia UK web page on the subject here.
