Setford put in a man-of-the-match performance for The Boro as they edged past Notts County 1-0 at the weekend.

The 20-year-old made four saves, including an 84th-minute penalty stop that sparked Stevenage to go up the other end and grab a late winner moments later.

The confidence-boosting performance came after Setford had a difficult international break for England Under-21s.

During the break, Setford scored an own goal against France and made a huge error that gifted Portugal a goal in his other appearance.



ISMEAL KABIA

After returning from a calf injury before the international break, Ismeal Kabia was back in action for St Mirren again.

The midfielder got another 90 minutes in the tank, but was on the losing side as St Mirren fell to a 4-1 defeat away to Celtic.

CHARLES SAGOE JR

There was no football for Charles Sagoe Jr this weekend as he is set to take to the pitch tonight as FF Kalmar take on Orgryte IS in the Swedish top flight.

It is another huge game for Kalmar, taking on bottom of the league Orgryte as they look to go six points clear of the relegation play-off spots with a win.



KHARI RANSON

During the international break Arsenal made the decision to loan out highly-rated goalkeeper Khari Ranson to Billericay Town.

Ranson has joined the National League South outfit on an initial 28-day loan and has already got two games under his belt.

The 19-year-old kept a clean sheet on his debut, helping Billericay earn a point in a 0-0 draw against Truro City.

Ranson was also in between the sticks for Billericay’s 4-1 win over Slough Town on Saturday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

ARCHIE STEVENS

Like Ranson, Archie Stevens completed an initial 28-day loan away from Arsenal last week, joining National League outfit Sutton United.



Stevens, 20, made his debut on Saturday, playing 42 minutes from the bench as Sutton beat Boston United 1-0.

Sports.title: Watford set to hire ‘most Watford manager ever’ in journeyman with 13 jobs in 15 years who used to date pop star
Sports.content:
Next

WATFORD are reportedly set to appoint journeyman coach Edward Iordanescu, who has had 13 jobs and once dated pop star Delia Matache.

The Hornets are looking for their sixth permanent manager in three years after sacking Alessio Dionisi.



Dionisi lasted just five months after overseeing a run of just three wins in 13 games.

The last straw was Watford’s 4-0 hammering by Sheffield United on Saturday.



According to Sky Sports, Watford are now in talks with Romanian Iordanescu to take over as head coach.

But some Watford fans might be scratching their heads over the potential appointment given his sketchy track record in management.

Iordanescu has had more than a dozen managerial roles in 16 years and hasn’t coached since October 2025.

And even that stint was short-lived as he was axed four months into his tenure following a run of poor form.

He had two spells with Romanian club CFR Cluj – both lasting just over a year.

Iordanescu spent two years in charge of the Romania national team and had much more success there as he guided them to Euro 2024.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He secured an opening 3-0 win over Ukraine and Romania went on to top the group after a defeat to Belgium and a draw against Slovakia.

But they were beaten 3-0 by the Netherlands in the last-16 and Iordanescu stepped down in July of that summer.

Away from the pitch he made headlines by briefly dating Romanian pop star Matache between 2005 and 2006.

Fans reacted to the news on X as one called it “the most Watford appointment ever.”



Another said: “Who? League One is coming for us.”

A third added: “Sounds like a name that will last 2 months.”

The Pozzo family are moving onto the 25th manager of their tenure since taking over in 2012.

The club called Dionisi – who only arrived in June – “a really good guy” in their statement announcing his departure this weekend and said a new appointment would be in place soon.

Watford chief Luke Dowling said: “We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As I’m sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

“The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly.”

Sports.title: Non-League club put up for sale as owner releases emotional statement eight years after starring in infamous documentary
Sports.content:
Next

STEWART DONALD is struggling to flog Eastleigh after deciding to put the non-League minnows up for sale.

The chairman and majority shareholder, 51, starred in the infamous Netflix documentary series Sunderland ‘Til I Die following his decision to snap up the now-Premier League side in 2018.



But Donald is now looking to walk away from Eastleigh after being forced to deal with tragic events off the pitch.

And the multi-millionaire plans to find a buyer before the end of the season.



In an emotional club statement, Donald said: “My wife was diagnosed with cancer at 36. We had a young family.

“My mother sadly passed away shortly before my wife, and my father was also diagnosed with terminal cancer.



“With everything going on at home and several businesses to run, I had to spend less time at the club than I had hoped.

“Despite this, my commitment never waned, and I continued to fully fund the club throughout this period.

“At the start of this season I made a decision it would be my last and that I would use this time to find suitable investors.

“Sadly, as of this moment, there have been no serious candidates. There have been many enquiries but as is usually the way with people offering to acquire football clubs, they have no credentials or serious funds.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Eastleigh currently uses all its revenues to cover ever increasing operational costs.

“Any investors must be prepared to fund the entire first-team budget, as I currently do, which is something no one has currently offered to do, even a reduced budget.

“So, with around five months of the season remaining, the board will seek a meeting with the supporters’ group to discuss the future of the club in more detail.”

Donald returned to Eastleigh, having previously owned the National League outfit, after selling Sunderland to Kyril Louis-Dreyfus.



But the businessman conceded heading back to the Silverlake Stadium may have been a mistake.

Donald added: “It’s around 15 years since I first acquired Eastleigh, with a brief pause whilst I went to Sunderland.

“Before departing, I ensured the club was financially stable by leaving over £3million in the club’s account.

“Upon my return, these funds had been understandably exhausted and it was a difficult time for the club but also for me personally. In hindsight, I perhaps should have not returned.



“However, the club needed funds to remain in the league for ground grading and I did not want the club to be relegated.

“The ground needed significant work for us to retain our league status, and I immediately invested a further £1m so the club could continue at the same level, altering the South Stand.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I also increased the playing budget in the hope that we could challenge again, albeit in a very changed landscape.”

Eastleigh are currently 16th in the National League ahead of facing Yeovil on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Diogo Dalot trolled by hilarious GTA 6 meme after Man Utd’s disastrous defeat to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL fans are cracking up at a GTA 6 meme taking aim at Diogo Dalot.

The right-back was one of the sorry Manchester United players who suffered through a humiliation at Anfield on Sunday.



Dalot, 27, played all 90 excruciating minutes as Liverpool ran out 4-0 winners to condemn United to 19th in the Premier League.

The Portuguese has faced stiff criticism this season, with many Red Devils fans convinced he is not good enough.



And now, four days after the release of GTA 6, Dalot is the subject of a brutal meme.

A still image, which has gone viral on X, shows a mocked-up version of a ‘mission’ on the game which involves buying a gift for the first-person character’s girlfriend, Lucia.

But some savvy editing work has changed the title of the mission to ‘SELL PLAYER’ and the instruction to ‘Sell Diogo Dalot.’

It also says: “Lucia will appreciate this.”

The meme – captioned “GTA 6 is very realistic” – has been liked tens of thousands of times.

One fan replied: “I think she would love that.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And another added: “Sell the whole team.”

Dalot was run ragged by Liverpool’s wide players on Sunday as the hosts let off 27 shots in a one-sided mauling.

United weren’t helped by Leny Yoro‘s eighth-minute red card but it was still a nightmare start for new boss Mauricio Pochettino.



And they now have statistically the worst defence in Europe’s five major leagues.

Club legend Gary Neville told Sky Sports after the game: “It’s negligent not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we have seen this now for two or three years.

“You’ve got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they’re in fear.”

Sports.title: Sky Sports presenter Kate Tracey treats fans to jacuzzi video as she wears low cut top on ‘zen’ retreat
Sports.content:
Next

SKY SPORTS presenter Kate Tracey gave fans a glimpse of her relaxing retreat as she enjoyed downtime in a jacuzzi.

The glamorous racing host shared a video on her Instagram story as she took a break from her busy broadcasting schedule.



Kate appeared in a black low-cut top while unwinding in the bubbling water during her peaceful getaway.

The popular presenter described the experience as “zen” as she made the most of her relaxing surroundings.



Kate has built up a loyal following on social media, regularly giving fans an insight into her life away from the cameras.

The broadcaster is best known for her work on Sky Sports Racing, where she covers some of the biggest events in the horse racing calendar.

The 31-year-old has become a familiar face to racing fans through her appearances at major meetings across Britain.

But her sporting interests extend beyond the racecourse, with Kate also working as a presenter for Aston Villa‘s official television channel.



The presenter is a passionate football supporter and has regularly featured in the club’s matchday coverage.



Away from her television commitments, Kate often shares pictures of her holidays, glamorous outfits and trips with friends and this latest one was no different.

She’s managed to find the balance between being a reporter and an influencer.

Her social media updates have previously attracted plenty of compliments from admirers, with fans praising her fashion choices and stylish appearances.

And her latest jacuzzi getaway offered another glimpse of how the Sky Sports star enjoys spending her time away from the spotlight.

Sports.title: Man Utd hire Arsenal coach who helped Mikel Arteta transform Gunners into title winners
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED have hired Arsenal’s former lead physical performance coach Sam Wilson.

He is joining United as a fitness coach for the first team and the hiring process began before Mauricio Pochettino was appointed last week.



Wilson was on the bench at Anfield for Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, which was Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Prior to that, the fitness coach had been with the Gunners for 12 years before leaving them in the summer to join Parma.



Wilson left the Italian club in October, but has not been out of work long after United moved to bring him in.

Wilson’s arrival is not expected to impact whether the club pushes ahead with a move to bring in former US national team fitness coach Silvia Tuya, who specialises in strength and conditioning.



Tuya arrived in Manchester on the same jet as Pochettino, but was not named in his official staff on Wednesday and United sources said a decision still needed to be made about whether she joins.

United had some of the worst running stats in the Premier League this season before Michael Carrick was sacked earlier this month.

They rank second from the bottom for total distance covered in the Prem, with an average of 111.5 km per match.

Pochettino faces a big task to turn that around and Wilson has a role to play in that, too.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He was a popular figure at Arsenal after joining the club in 2014 as a strength and conditioning coach for the Under-18s.

Wilson worked his way up the ladder at the Emirates and got his opportunity with the first team as part of Freddie Ljungberg’s interim coaching staff, when Unai Emery was sacked in November 2019.

Mikel Arteta kept Wilson as part of his backroom team and handed him the role of Arsenal’s lead physical performance coach in the summer of 2022.

The Gunners squad were big fans of Wilson and some even went on holiday with him, doing extra fitness work as part of the break.



Wilson left Arsenal this summer – but that was his own decision as he took up the chance for a fresh challenge.

He joined Arteta’s former assistant, Carlos Cuesta, at Parma after being handed the role of their head of performance.

Cuesta was sacked in September, however, and Wilson left the Italian side the following month.

Sports.title: Man Utd are in a genuine battle against the drop with their biggest problem clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd are in a genuine battle against the drop with their biggest problem clear

Manchester United's defeat on Sunday leaves them with one Premier League win - the fewest of any team - as they continue to sit in the bottom three

View Image Man Utd sit 19th and are without a Premier League win in nearly three months

Manchester United sit second bottom with December just around the corner - at what point do we start talking about relegation?

‌



‌



It is scarcely believable to see the Premier League's most successful team sitting in 19th with one win from 11 games, but that is the current reality. The 4-0 loss at Liverpool on Sunday was the latest setback for a team who don't look like winning a game.

‌



They sit on eight points. This time last year Tottenham had 19, and they needed a win on the final day just to stay up. You look at United's squad, even if they are underperforming, and think they must click into gear eventually. But there's no sign of that yet.

‌



Jamie Carragher confessed that the quality of the mid-table teams has never been so strong - and that could be the biggest problem for United.

‌



Quizzed on relegation prospects he said: "No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are. But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it's as strong as it's ever been.

"Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren't many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that's a problem for Man United."

Article continues below

Gary Neville and Roy Keane maintain their former side won't find themselves in the Championship next season, but at what point does a prolonged run of poor form become a genuine danger of relegation?

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes 'very proud' of Man Utd with Liverpool result 'hiding good things'
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes 'very proud' of Man Utd with Liverpool result 'hiding good things'

Bruno Fernandes hyped up his Manchester United teammates in light of their heavy loss at Liverpool, citing the pride he felt as the Red Devils dug in with ten men

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes was full of praise for his teammates despite their loss at Liverpool

Bruno Fernandes claimed he was "very proud of everyone" despite being part of a Manchester United side that were hammered 4-0 at Liverpool.

‌



‌



The Red Devils were thrashed at Anfield, losing convincingly with ten men after Leny Yoro was given his marching orders after ten minutes. That led to the hosts establishing a two-goal lead inside 13 minutes and there were fears that the floodgates could open.

‌



Fernandes was present back in 2023 when Liverpool secured a historic 7-0 win over United, but Mauricio Pochettino's side dug in somewhat to prevent some of the damage, although that also owed to Liverpool being wasteful in front of goal.

‌



The Portugal playmaker, who has shelved contract talks with the club, has already been scathing in post-match interviews this season, but this time poured praise on his teammates for their desire despite the scoreline.

He said on the defeat: "Very painful, it hurts a lot. Coming to our rivals and losing is always bad. It's a difficult moment for us, but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation. Everyone tried very hard. The result won't show that and will hide a lot of good things that the team did.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"We still created a lot of chances to try and do something in the game, even with one player less. Unfortunately, we were not able to avoid two more goals in the second half. We were very brave. In some moments, we lost the ball, but we were trying to play, we were trying to do something in the game, we were not afraid.

‌



"There were some moments we maybe even played a little too much, and we ended up conceding goals. But I would rather that and see the confidence of my team, to replicate the ideas of what we want to do than just defend and be afraid of anything that we can do.

"You want to get results, but today, it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at, and I saw a lot of character from the team. The result won't show that, but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room."

‌



View 2 Images Man Utd played 80 minutes on Sunday with ten men (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

The loss leaves United with one win from their 11 Premier League games - no team in the top flight has fewer. They languish down in 19th with December only a week away as talk of them becoming relegation contenders continues.

‌



Yoro's red card had a huge bearing on the result but Fernandes was left raging by the decision, insisting the heavy touch by Alexander Isak meant a dismissal shouldn't have been the end result.

"Today, you can't give a red card. It's very clear they show us if the player is not in control of the ball, it's never a red card," said the United skipper.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino must accept blame for his first huge Man Utd mistake
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino must accept blame for his first huge Man Utd mistake

Mauricio Pochettino's late arrival at Manchester United was largely down to his own decision making and his lack of preparation time didn't aid the team in their loss to Liverpool

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino was forced to watch his Man Utd team get dismantled in his first game (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United debut went as bad as he could've imagined - a hammering at the hands of their rivals having seen a player sent off inside ten minutes.

‌



‌



It was always going to be a baptism of fire for the Argentinian, returning to the Premier League having had stints with Tottenham and Chelsea.

‌



He inherits a troubled side at its lowest ebb in the Premier League era, and he himself had next to no preparation time, which many would argue was self inflicted. Pochettino chose to see out his commitments with the USA before taking on the United gig.

‌



That meant he couldn't arrive at Carrington on Monday, instead rocking up on the Thursday. That left him with two days in which to get to know his players, see them up close and make decisions off the back of that.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Eyebrows were raised when Matthijs de Ligt was handed a start at Anfield despite being out injured for so long, and showing so little in the loss at Como weeks earlier. Nevertheless he was given the nod ahead of Harry Maguire.

It was the Dutchman's poor positioning that allowed Alexander Isak to get behind the United defence, which led to Leny Yoro being sent-off seconds later. De Ligt continued to struggle with the pace of the game, which may have been evident to Pochettino had he seen more of him in training in the days leading up to the Liverpool clash.

‌



The reason for Pochettino's late arrival into Manchester was due to his decision to oversee both of the USA's games against Haiti. It was a two-legged affair, the first of which was won 6-0. There were grounds to leave after that, but instead he remained to see his side win 2-0 days later.

View 2 Images The Argentine chose to see out his last two games as USA boss - delaying his Manchester arrival (Image: Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images)

‌



Sandwiched in between that the ex-Tottenham boss chose to take himself off for a bit of NFL. He was present at the Paycor Stadium to see the Cincinnati Bengals see off rivals Pittsburgh Steelers.

Despite the subsequent preparation Pochettino was keen to add perspective to the Liverpool defeat, suggesting that even the world's best teams would've been cut apart by Liverpool had they gone down a man early on.

‌



"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino. "Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?

"We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing room."

Sports.title: Gary Neville slaps himself in the face during Man Utd rant to leave Jamie Carragher stunned
Sports.content:
Gary Neville slaps himself in the face during Man Utd rant to leave Jamie Carragher stunned

Gary Neville lamented Manchester United's defenders and during his rant took the bizarre step of twice slapping himself in the race - to the amusement of the Sky Sports studio

View 2 Images Gary Neville was slapping himself in the face as he lamented Man Utd's defence (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville took aim at Manchester United's failing defence and then twice slapped himself in the face during a bizarre post-match debrief as his frustration boiled over.

‌



‌



The Red Devils, beginning their new era under Mauricio Pochettino, endured more pain as they were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield. Their hopes were all but quashed inside 10 minutes when Leny Yoro was sent-off.

‌



The Frenchman hauled down Alexander Isak after Matthijs de Ligt had been caught in a poor position as the United backline was again exposed following another summer of neglect. Neville has been among the most vocal critics of their defensive options and a line-up that included Yoro, De Ligt and Lisandro Martinez were constantly got at. Eventually Harry Maguire was introduced, but couldn't stop the Liverpool onslaught.

‌



All of which led to Neville calling out their body language, claiming they never look alert. He then hammered home that point with several slaps to the face.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Speaking in the Sky Sports studio after watching his boyhood club get demolished, Neville blasted United defenders’ body language. He said: “I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head). I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…”

Neville then stared blankly for several seconds before saying “wake up" twice, slapping himself each time, and finishing by adding: “You play for Man Utd!”

‌



The former United captain was particularly critical of Pochettino's decision to include De Ligt in his starting XI given his lengthy period out with injury. Neville had sympathy with the Dutchman, acknowledging how difficult it is to return after a year on the sidelines.

View 2 Images Matthijs de Ligt endured a difficult afternoon at Anfield

‌



He said: “I have a lot of sympathy for him. It’s like playing football after having six pints. It’s a strange feeling. I have a lot of sympathy for him, it’s alarming to watch.”

During commentary he said: “When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the team sheet I was absolutely stunned and the reason I was stunned was because of this. You watched him in Como four weeks ago and he was very much off it and that is just a basic ball over the top of him."

Article continues below

United's loss at Anfield leaves them in the relegation zone having won just one of 11 Premier League games, conceding more goals than any team in Europe's top five leagues.

Sports.title: Chelsea star reveals he was 'robbed' after Leeds thrashing as statement released
Sports.content:
Chelsea star reveals he was 'robbed' after Leeds thrashing as statement released

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha has confirmed there was an incident following Saturday afternoon’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United.

View Image Emmanuel Emegha marked his first Chelsea start with a goal. (Image: Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images)

Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening. Shortly before the incident, the 23-year-old striker had marked his first start for Chelsea with a goal in a disappointing 4-1 defeat by Leeds United.

‌



‌



Emegha broke the deadlock inside the opening half hour, smashing the ball past James Trafford at his near post. Noah Okafor levelled proceedings a few moments later, then doubled his tally for the afternoon in the second half, just minutes after Dominic Calvert-Lewin had put the West Yorkshire outfit in front from the spot.

‌



Brenden Aaronson came off the bench to put the fourth and final nail in the Blues’ coffin, securing Leeds three points and a place in the top six of the Premier League. On Saturday evening, a user uploaded a couple of pictures of Emegha to X, standing alone on the side of a road in a Chelsea tracksuit.

‌



“Nah man Emegha got robbed tonight as well ffs,” they captioned the post, which, at the time of writing, garnered nearly 300,000 views and over 2,000 likes. Then, on Sunday night, the Netherlands international confirmed that an incident had occurred after the game.

Make sure you don’t miss sport’s biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In a post on Instagram, Emegha wrote: “First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday. Unfortunately, after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support [praying emoji].”

‌



Mike Penders and Geovany Quenda joined a few of the Dutchman’s former Strasbourg teammates in the comment section to show their support, posting heart emojis.

Chelsea signed Emegha from the French outfit, also owned by BlueCo, in the summer after initially wrapping up a deal back in September 2025.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The striker spoke to club media ahead of the defeat by Daniel Farke’s side, and he described himself as a ‘nightmare’ for defenders. In Saturday's match-day programme, Emegha said: “I'm a winner, I'm a fighter.

‌



“I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it. I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders.

“Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.”

Article continues below

With Joao Pedro on the sidelines nursing an injury, Xabi Alonso will hope Emegha can add to his tally when Chelsea lock horns with Nottingham Forest at the City Ground on Friday night.

Sports.title: Villarreal deny ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery due to solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Villarreal deny ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery due to solar eclipse

Villarreal have released a club statement designed to debunk claims Nicolas Pepe underwent eye surgery after watching the solar eclipse in Spain earlier this year

View 2 Images Villarreal have denied Nicolas Pepe underwent eye surgery due to watching the solar eclipse (Image: Manuel Queimadelos/Quality Sport Images)

Villarreal have been forced to release a club statement to shoot down reports that Nicolas Pepe underwent eye surgery after looking at the sun during the solar eclipse in Spain.

‌



Pepe, 31, had recently played with a face mask in La Liga after undergoing eye surgery. Claims that the former Arsenal winger had sustained an injury after looking at the sun during the solar eclipse back in August have recently begun circulating on social media.

However, Villarreal have come out fighting against the "completely false" claims about the Ivory Coast star, saying that Pepe's recent surgery was pre-planned in a blunt statement.

"Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," said the club.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health."

A Snapchat video which was allegedly posted from the player’s social media account, showing the eclipse, had recently gone viral alongside the claims regarding Pepe's eye surgery. Pepe missed five games in October following his eye surgery before returning to action.

View 2 Images Pepe failed to meet expectations at Arsenal (Image: Matthew Ashton - AMA)

Pepe has been plying his trade in Spain's top league for two years after joining Villarreal following a spell in Turkey with Trabzonspor.

He endured a torrid stint at Arsenal after becoming the club's then-record transfer signing following a £72million switch from Lille in Ligue 1 back in the summer of 2019.

Pepe struggled to live up to his price tag, scoring only 27 goals across 112 games for the Gunners. After spending time out on loan, Pepe was eventually allowed to leave the club on a free transfer.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim takes dig at clubs sacking managers after latest Ineos dismissal
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim takes dig at clubs sacking managers after latest Ineos dismissal

Former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim has questioned how some big clubs operate on a weekend where Mauricio Pochettino prepares to oversee his first Red Devils game

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim has hit out at the strategy of some big clubs (Image: Claudio Villa/AC Milan via Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim, the former Manchester United manager, has bemoaned the lack of long-term strategy at "big clubs" on the eve of his previous employers' first game under Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



Amorim, 41, arrived at Old Trafford as one of Europe's most exciting young coaches following a fine spell in charge of Sporting Lisbon. However, the Portuguese lasted just 14 months at United after failing to live up to the hype in the Premier League.

‌



With Amorim now embracing a new challenge in Italy with AC Milan, United are about to start life under another new manager after Michael Carrick paid the price for a disastrous start to the season.

‌



Milan are fourth in Serie A, with Amorim losing just one of his first 11 league games in the Italian capital - and he has shared some interesting thoughts around strategy.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs," said Amorim in a press conference. "Is thinking that I look at the table: If we are near, let's invest. Crazy invest. If we are not near, let's not invest.

‌



"I think the key point is - have a long term plan. If you lose, all the games, sack the manager. That is normal. I'm not talking about that [laughs]. But what I'm saying is that stick with your plan.

"We have a plan. What kind of player we want. Whether he's able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want. Not a big star, like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team."

‌



He continued: "If we have a clear plan, don't look at the table. Look at the table only to evaluate the process. But to buy, to spend money, only consider things for the next 5 years. Don't spend money by constantly looking at the table at the end of November or December. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs."

View 2 Images Amorim's time in charge of Manchester United was unsuccessful (Image: Getty)

‌



Although Amorim arrived in the Premier League with a burgeoning reputation, his period in charge of Manchester United failed to yield much in the way of success. He won 25 of his 63 games in charge of the Red Devils, who paid £9.25million to trigger Amorim's release clause at Sporting Lisbon.

His 14-month reign came to an explosive end when Amorim took aim at the club hierarchy. Confirmation that he had left his post came the following day.

‌



"I just want to say I came here to be the manager, not to be the coach," Amorim said in press conference. "In every department - the scouting department, the sporting director – [they] need to do their job. I will do mine for 18 months and then we move on.

"I just want to say that I'm going to be the manager of this team, not just the coach. I was really clear on that. That is going to finish in 18 months and then everyone is going to move on. That was the deal. That is my job. Not to be a coach."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino fumes over two decisions in Man Utd's trashing by Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino fumes over two decisions in Man Utd's trashing by Liverpool

New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his new job as the Red Devils were thumped by Liverpool at Anfield

View 2 Images Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino after defeat to Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino was left fuming after Leny Yoro’s red card condemned Manchester United to a “painful” humiliation at Anfield.

‌



‌



Pochettino suffered the biggest defeat of any new United manager’s first game in charge in 100 years which left them rooted in the relegation zone.

‌



But Pochettino said United should have had a penalty for Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet’s challenge on Bryan Mbeumo a minute before Yoro got his marching orders for pulling back Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick.

‌



United boss Pochettino said: “It is painful we lose 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men but also it was a penalty to Mbeumo. We can make a mistake, and we were punished and they were not.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“We need to be critical of ourselves but also at the same time we need to put some situations that happened during the game that we are not happy.

“The ball was going to the keeper. I think in that situation if you review the VAR you can see, like we see on the cameras now, that Yoro never had the intention to connect with Isak. The striker saw that the ball was going to the keeper and he delayed a little bit of his run and goes down.

‌



“But if you go two minutes before. Sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo, they are similar, no? When you compare the actions, that's a penalty, no. And if we score after six minutes for sure we are talking in a different way.”

But Pochettino admitted they have to “accept the reality” of the situation they are in but insisted they showed fight after going down to ten men.

‌



View 2 Images United were thrashed by Liverpool at Anfield (Image: Getty Images)

Pochettino added: “So, so painful. So disappointed. It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together and we feel disappointed because it is clear what happened.

‌



“The plan was in the bin but what I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team and to the club and they want to win games and today we made an effort. Today was a test that for me is very positive.”

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola celebrated after the final whistle with fist pumps in front of the Kop and was adamant that it was a foul on Isak.

‌



Iraola said: “It is clearly the last man, clearly a foul, Alex on the keeper, will he score, we never know, but for us it is a good moment because we are going to play a lot of time against ten men.

“I always enjoy the moment with the fans and I think we owe them because we have had much better results and we want to solve this and give them a big win and more to celebrate.”

Sports.title: Armstrong is Everton's running man and Moyes believes he can get better
Sports.content:
Harrison Armstrong has started every Premier League game for Everton this season, ranking in the top three for distance covered in the competition going into the weekend. This has been some year for a player who started 2026 on loan at Preston North End.

There was talk of a big move to Nottingham Forest in the summer and interest from elsewhere remains as Everton try to persuade him to sign a new contract. Supporters will be desperate for one of their own to stay. And David Moyes feel the same way.

"He is a big player for us," the Everton manager tells Sky Sports. "For a 19-year-old young midfield player he is doing really well. I hope he can continue to do that." That recall from Preston in January already feels like a pivotal moment in Armstrong's career.

Image: Harrison Armstrong ranked third for distance covered going into the weekend

"I was watching him quite regularly. He was doing really well and we had to bring him back. They did not like it obviously because Preston were going really well. But we had got so many injuries around December time that we needed to bring him back."

In truth, it was not ideal for Armstrong in some respects. "I think if he had got another 20 games with them it would have been good for him." But there were opportunities off the bench and the fact that he did not have things all his own way will have helped him too.

Image: Everton's Harrison Armstrong is being trusted in his favoured central role this season

There were substitute appearances against Arsenal and Manchester City when he was brought on to help tighten things up only for Everton to concede late. But even those experiences are useful. "He is a confident boy. He has got a lot of belief in himself."

Most importantly, he has responded. "Since then he has stepped up again." Speaking to Moyes at Everton's training ground, he acknowledges that it was Armstrong's work in the summer that made him sit up and take notice. "He was very good in pre-season."

Moyes explains: "There was no way we could really put him back out on loan this year. We knew that we would find more minutes for him. But his form in pre-season games was the reason which made me think that we were certainly centred around him."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Everton's win over Coventry in the Premier League

Circumstances helped. "We lost Jimmy Garner with a hernia operation in the opening games of the season, which left Hayden Hackney, who had just arrived and was still carrying a bit of an injury from last season. So it gave Harrison the opportunity to start."

In Moyes' words, it was a chance "to show what he could do" and Armstrong has done just that. "He has taken it with both hands." The youngster's obvious enthusiasm instantly endeared him to an Everton crowd that demand work rate from their players.

Brentford

Everton Monday 23rd November 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Those distance-covered statistics stand out but Armstrong sets the tone for Everton with his off-the-ball work. "You have got to have some attributes which are really important and that one is really important for him and for us," Moyes explains.

"He works incredibly hard for the team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Premier League match between Newcastle and Everton

The result is that even with Garner and Hackney fit, he has stayed in. "Without doubt he has earned the right to be in the team. He has earned the right by his performances every week because we have got competition. But if you are doing as well as he is…"

Of course, Moyes remains the archetypal tough-taskmaster and it is only natural that the 63-year-old Scot opts to couch his praise for the player with a reminder that Armstrong must add more to his game if he is to fulfil his potential in the long term.

Image: Harrison Armstrong's heat map and passing sonar for Everton this season

"There are things we want him to improve on. He has still got a bit to learn." What exactly? "We would like him to do a bit better with his passing at times and I certainly want him to score more goals or get more opportunities. They would be the things."

But there is optimism that he can add these elements. "We must not forget that he is a 19-year-old midfield player and very much learning his trade." Moyes knows. He has overseen the development of top-class teenagers from Wayne Rooney to Declan Rice.

What is his verdict on how good Armstrong could go on to become? "I think that he can develop into a really top-notch midfield player," adds Moyes. It has been a breakout year for him in the Premier League. But this could be just the start for Harrison Armstrong.

Sports.title: 'Price knows he can win Worlds after Grand Slam glory'
Sports.content:
Wayne Mardle says Gerwyn Price knows he can win the World Championship at Alexandra Palace again after ending his major trophy drought to claim a fourth Grand Slam title.

'The Iceman' had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.

But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton.

Gerwyn Price - Major Honours

🏆 World Darts Championship (2021)



🏆🏆🏆🏆 Grand Slam of Darts (2018, 19, 21, 26)



🏆 World Grand Prix (2020)



🏆🏆 World Series of Darts Finals (2020, 22)



🏆🏆 World Cup of Darts (2020, 23)



Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the first time since 2021 - the same year he won his sole world title, when he was forced to celebrate behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

"Gezzy knows he can win it. Yes, winning the Grand Slam four times is amazing for him, but he knows he can win the Worlds," said Mardle.

"He's done it before and he's got a new-found fanbase.

"He's enjoying himself and it's incredible the way that everything's turned around for him. And, look, he's enjoying life.

"It's good to see Gezzy smile."

Looking ahead to Ally Pally, 'Hawaii 501' said: "Those that are at the top of the tree right now, call it top six, top five, top four, they're the ones to beat. They really are.

"Luke Humphries, Luke Littler, Gezzy Price.

"Let's be honest, we know that he got beat [in the semi-finals] and didn't play great but Michael van Gerwen shone this week.

"Don't rule out a fourth world title for him. With timing and a bit of luck, anyone can win."

'Price is talking about the next one already'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the moment Price ended his wait for a major title...

Mark Webster said it does not look like Price is done after returning to the winners' circle with his eighth major title.

Price will be eyeing further televised success at the Players Championship Finals which takes place at Butlin's Minehead Resort from November 27-29.

Van Veen, Humphries and Van Gerwen will also headline, as a 64-player field compete in the final tournament before the 2027 World Darts Championship.

"He's still got tournaments to win. He's talking about the next one already," said Webster.

"He goes to Minehead and he's talking about this trend with winning this and winning the Worlds.

"He wants another World Championship, and particularly all the heartache he's had getting to finals this year, to get over the line, really important for him. It could open up some floodgates for him now to go on and win major after major."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price hopes he can follow Michael Smith, Humphries and Littler twice over the past four years to win the Slam and then go on to win the World Championship in just over a month

The 2008 Lakeside world champion believes the cream will rise to the top on the grandest stage of them all.

"At the Worlds, there'll be upsets, but I think it will come to the top players," said Webster as Price aims to follow Michael Smith, Humphries and Littler - twice over the past four years - to win the Slam and then go on to win the Worlds in just over a month.

"I think the two Lukes left this event - they just got beat by the better player. There's no real concern in the way they played, so they'll be a force, along with Price, Gian, and it's good to see Michael [Van Gerwen] in glimpses, but it's going to be a brilliant three weeks at Ally Pally."

Has winning the Grand Slam done Price a huge favour?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at ALL FIVE of Price's ton-plus checkouts during his sensational win over Van Veen

Victory for Price means he is provisionally up to world No 3, with Littler still No 1, Van Veen at No 2, and Humphries down to No 4 - potentially shaking up the draw heading into the Worlds.

Price, who took home the £200,000 jackpot in Wolverhampton, has also overtaken Littler with the most ranking money earned this season.

Commentator Dan Dawson explained: "Price has had to battle to this title, and I think he's had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.

"But I think that's what he's had to do to become a winner again, and seeing him smile and seeing that pressure lift, just hearing him talk, I think that is an enormous sign because he's already looking ahead. What can I win next?

"We know that at Ally Pally he is up into No 3 in the world, with Humphries and Littler on the same side of the draw provisionally.

"That game there between Gian and Price, that would provisionally be the semi-final in the other half of the draw.

"So that has done him a favour if he is looking to become a world champion again."

Sports.title: Wolff: Russell-Verstappen provocations a good factor of F1 entertainment
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says the "provocations" between his driver George Russell and Red Bull's Max Verstappen are a "good factor of the entertainment" in Formula 1.

Hostilities between the pair were renewed at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as a collision in final practice was followed by a war of words that threatens to continue at next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday.

After Russell had criticised Verstappen ahead of Saturday night's race in Las Vegas, the pair battled for the lead for much of the race, with Verstappen claiming victory as Russell finished ninth after a late error - made as he tried to pass his team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second - dropped the Brit down the field.

Verstappen poked fun at Russell at the time over team radio and then laid into the Mercedes driver during the post-race press conference, claiming that "he's so far below my level".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell hits the barrier after a lock-up when trying to overtake team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, much to the delight of rival Max Verstappen

Wolff, who was speaking after the race but before Verstappen had spoken in the press conference, suggested the rivalry was good for the sport.

Asked whether it was a bad idea for Russell to engage in 'mind games' with Verstappen, Wolff replied: "They have known each other so long since karting.

"I think it's probably been a bit of cat and mouse.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell reacted to the collision with Max Verstappen in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, accusing the Red Bull driver of of 'screwing' his rivals over

"These provocations in either side is another good factor of the entertainment."

Their feud has reignited almost exactly two years on from a major blow up following the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, which saw a remarkable war of words follow an incident in which Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard to get him penalised by the stewards.

'Max was a deserving winner'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix

The collision between the pair in final practice happened after Verstappen had overtaken Russell as the pair were both preparing for push laps, which Russell felt was in breach of a gentleman's agreement the drivers have.

The stewards gave Verstappen a warning for causing the collision, which Russell accepted as an appropriate outcome, but he insisted that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy".

Asked if he knew whether the pair had exchanged words following the incident, Wolff said: "I guess in the stewards' room there was a bit of an exchange."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell tussles with Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar at the start of the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Verstappen drove superbly to win the race, managing his deployment expertly to immediately regain the lead on several occasions.

Wolff, who publicly courted Verstappen after it was confirmed Lewis Hamilton was leaving Mercedes to join Ferrari, was impressed by the Dutchman's display.

"I think Max is a deserving winner [of the race]. He made no mistakes, and that's why he won the race.

"He always had a response. Some very good driving."

Sports.title: The day Liverpool's attack showed its devastating potential
Sports.content:
The conditions were favourable. Leny Yoro's red card after just eight minutes. A Man Utd team devoid of confidence and defensive resilience. But on Sunday, Liverpool's attack showed its devastating potential.

"We've questioned the attacking players but they looked absolutely electric," purred Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher after his former side had put four past their biggest rivals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Carragher has been clear in his criticism of Liverpool's expensively-assembled frontline previously. In August, he suggested Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz - brought in for £240m - were part of a summer 2025 splurge which could go down as the "arguably the worst transfer window we've probably seen in Premier League history".

Under new boss Andoni Iraola, those Liverpool players are starting to shift the narrative now.

"The attacking players from Liverpool certainly turned up today," agreed Sky Sports' Roy Keane, amid his dressing down of United's defending.

Key to Liverpool's attacking play was the much-maligned Wirtz.

According to Opta, he created five big chances in the game. That's the most by a player in their records for that metric, dating back to 2010.

Image: Florian Wirtz's first five Premier League games of the season vs his past six

For context, Wirtz had created just one big chance in his previous 10 Premier League games this term - that came in his last outing at Crystal Palace, where he also scored his first goal of the season. His next came at Anfield, brilliantly flicking in a quickfire second for his side after Dominik Szoboszlai's free-kick to give 10-man United little hope of a result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Florian Wirtz scores Liverpool's second against 10-man Manchester United.

It's been a long wait but it seems to finally be coming together in England for the undoubtedly talented 23-year-old. "This is why they spent the money on him," said Carragher.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville’s reactions from Liverpool's 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

Wirtz's own assessment of his form gave a nod to his team-mates. "I feel very good, but I think it's also because the team has just developed and gets better," he said. "Being part of this, you also get better. I'm enjoying this."

The development, though, runs beyond just a set group of starting attackers. It's the options and variety at Iraola's disposal which can make Liverpool fans optimistic.

Alexander Isak leads the line but, without Cody Gakpo in the side on Sunday, there was the chance for 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha to step up and he seized it, assisting Wirtz and then converting Bradley Barcola's cross to become the youngest scorer against United in Premier League history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rio Ngumoha impresses with 'speed and zest' as he scores Liverpool's third against Manchester United.

Ngumoha's expected assists total for the game of 1.05 was the second highest by a player in a Premier League game this season. Top spot was taken by Wirtz, with 1.08.

Victor Munoz then stepped off the bench to add a fourth from a Wirtz pass - the third time the German has teed up Munoz in a Premier League game this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Victor Munoz nets Liverpool's fourth against Manchester United at Anfield.

And there is still Hugo Ekitike to come back from his injury.

Liverpool are still developing and it wasn't always perfect at Anfield. They missed six big chances to further punish United, while Isak went goalless from an xG of 1.32. Barcola, too, was at times erratic, completing just one of his seven dribbles.

The quality of their opposition shouldn't be lost, either. Liverpool are the third team to put four past United in the past month.

Iraola, though, called on his side to deliver a statement Premier League win at Anfield for the first time this season before the match and his players delivered.

The challenge is to realise that attacking potential consistently in the tests to come. But with Wirtz finally starting to shine, Liverpool's future looks bright.

Sports.title: Playoff picture taking shape and Mendoza belongs - NFL Sunday Review
Sports.content:
It's an oft trotted out cliché that 'football season starts after Thanksgiving'. Well, with the American holiday only three days away, the NFL playoff picture is truly starting to take shape going into the stretch run.

The San Francisco 49ers (9-1) further asserted their dominance in the NFC with a thumping 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings and their much-vaunted defense in Mexico City - the final International Series game of the season - while the Buffalo Bills (9-1) share the same record as the AFC top seeds, albeit they were far less convincing in their 26-9 dispatching of the one-win Miami Dolphins.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the San Francisco 49ers against the Minnesota Vikings from Week 11 of the NFL season.

Josh Allen threw two interceptions to allow the Dolphins to hang around until the Bills pulled away late. He and the team will need to sharpen up for their mouthwatering Thanksgiving night meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) - live on Sky Sports NFL from 1.20am, Friday - that could ultimately end up deciding where the road to the Super Bowl runs through in the AFC.

However, it's below the Bills and the Chiefs, and the 49ers on the other side of the conference divide, where things are really starting to get interesting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kansas City Chiefs' Nohl Williams lifts Arizona Cardinals' Elijah Higgins into the air in a WWE-style tackle.

The Denver Broncos (8-2) are also in the mix for top billing in the AFC, after claiming a sixth straight against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) have the opportunity to match that mark with a Monday night victory at the Washington Commanders.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) stumbled at the New York Giants (6-3-1), whose impressive victory strengthened their grip on the NFC East division, which the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) are still in the hunt for after hanging 51 on the Tennessee Titans defense.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Jacksonville Jaguars against the New York Giants from Week 11 of the NFL season.

The Jaguars' loss was far from fatal, with the Titans, along with the Indianapolis Colts and the Houston Texans all floundering in their division, though the Pittsburgh Steelers' (6-4) shock loss at the Philadelphia Eagles might well have opened the door to the latter in the race for a wildcard berth.

The Texans, who started the season 0-4, now sit 4-6 and - after a meeting with a Baltimore Ravens team in the midst of a six-game losing streak - will likely have the opportunity to match the Steelers' record when the two teams meet in a fortnight, following Pittsburgh's tricky assignment against the Broncos where they'll try to avoid dropping three in a row.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Detroit Lions' Jameson Williams catches a 57-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff before celebrating with a flip into the end zone against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Meanwhile, back in the NFC, the greatest intrigue lies in the NFC North and the four-way battle unfolding for the division, with the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2), Vikings (7-3) - even with their chastening loss to the Niners - and Green Bay Packers (6-4) all currently playoff bound.

Mind you, they all have the looming threat of the wildcard-hunting Los Angeles Rams (6-4) and defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) from the NFC West.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chicago Bears' Colston Loveland leaps over a New Orleans Saints defender on his way to scoring a spectacular 15-yard touchdown.

It makes the Thanksgiving night clash between the Lions and Bears in Detroit - live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm, Thursday - even more crucial.

See, 'football season (really does) start at Thanksgiving'.

What we learned

The Cowboys' offense is unstoppable!

Quite literally.

Lost in amongst how historically bad their defense is - even the one-win Titans scored on five of their first six possessions, one week on from the 49ers managing to score 46 points and a staggering 584 yards against them - is how impressive their offense is, and needs to be!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Tennessee Titans against the Dallas Cowboys from Week 11 of the NFL season.

The Cowboys are just the fourth team in NFL history to allow at least 20 points in each of their first 11 games and still win at least five of those games. They have allowed 20 points in 18 straight games dating back to Week 12 of last season.

But Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran in another score as Dallas found the end zone on each of their first six drives in their 51-30 thumping of the Titans to somewhat mask their continued defensive woes.

Fernando Mendoza looks the real deal.

There's still teething issues as the No 1 overall draft picks eases his way into NFL life - most notably the game-sealing pick-six he threw that ensured he starts his career with back-to-back defeats in his first two starts. But there was a lot to like too.

Image: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza threw three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL - against the Denver Broncos

Mendoza and the Raiders hung with the Broncos far longer than many expected, with it being just a one-score game when the rookie QB tossed that costly interception.

Prior to that, he completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three passing touchdowns - his first in the NFL.

"I felt more comfortable than last week," Mendoza admitted afterwards. "I was able to settle in and able to see the entire field better.

"If you just do your job, your momentum is going to swing your way eventually."

Overreaction or reality?

Are the Steelers in danger of dropping out of the AFC playoff picture?

It certainly looks like they're in trouble. The 19-16 reverse in Philadelphia not only was the Eagles' first win in eight games, it was the Steelers' second straight loss, with Aaron Rodgers, who turns 43 on December 2, looking every bit his age as he limped to 95 passing yards when going 17 of 20 in the first half.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Philadelphia Eagles from Week 11 of the NFL season.

That turned into 227 yards by the end of the game after some garbage-time stat-padding, but it's looking a little rough for the Steelers, who currently occupy the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC and have a dire run of stellar defenses to come over the next three-week stretch in the Broncos, Texans and Jaguars.

Helping their cause is the fact that the AFC isn't exactly flush with challengers. The New England Patriots (5-5) are currently their closes rivals but they're in the midst of their own crisis with starting quarterback Drake Maye out for the year, then there's the Texans (4-6) and that's pretty much it.

Though Houston's record looks pretty ugly at the minute, they won nine straight from 3-5 to get into the playoffs last year, so are well capable of going on a run.

Their visit to Pittsburgh in two weeks' time could prove pivotal.

Winners and losers

Winners:

David Bailey: The New York Jets rookie edge rusher had two sacks in their win at the Los Angeles Chargers that broke their five-game losing streak, giving him nine-and-a-half sacks on the season to go with six forced fumbles, including one against the Chargers.

The No 2 overall draft pick generated five pressures, meaning he has now recorded 45 pressures this season, the third-most by a rookie defender through Week 11 since 2018, trailing only Jared Verse (50 in 2024) and Nick Bosa (49 in 2019).

Travis Kelce: The veteran Chiefs tight end had 74 receiving yards to go with two receiving touchdowns in their win over the Arizona Cardinals, his first game with multiple receiving touchdowns since Week 11 of the 2022 season against the Chargers.

Image: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce celebrates his two-touchdown day against the Arizona Cardinals

The 37-year-old's eight-yard score on Kansas City's opening possession also saw him pass Rob Gronkowski into third place for the most total touchdowns (including playoffs) by a tight end in NFL history with 109.

Only Pro Football Hall of Famers Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115) have scored more.

Losers:

DK Metcalf: The Steelers receiver was ejected from their game in Philadelphia after committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties 10 offensive plays apart, with the second of those appearing to see him reach into Cooper DeJean's facemask and poke the defensive back near the eye, sparking a melee between the two teams.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pittsburgh Steelers' DK Metcalf is ejected following a second clash with Philadelphia Eagles' Cooper DeJean.

The ejection is Metcalf's third for his career since his debut in 2019. That's tied with 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most in the NFL during that span.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said afterwards. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed. We can't have players getting ejected from games."

Tennessee Titans: "All gas, no brake" is Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh's much-quoted mantra.

Well, the Titans took that sentiment a touch too literally on Sunday with someone seemingly cutting the breaks as they went careering off a cliff against the Cowboys.

And the coach, renowned for his defensive acumen, was NOT happy about the performance as his defense let up 51 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tennessee Titans QB Cam Ward scrambles across the field before throwing across his body to find Calvin Ridley for a remarkable 12-yard touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys.

"It was disgusting, embarrassing football," Saleh said afterwards. "That starts with me. I got to figure it out.

"We have no choice but to get better. It can't get any worse."

Player of the Weekend - Jeffery Simmons, DT, Chicago Bears

Jeffery Simmons has been everything the Bears could've hoped for following their blockbuster mid-season trade for the former Titans defensive tackle which saw Chicago cough up two first-round draft picks.

Image: Jeffery Simmons has five sacks in three games since his blockbuster trade to the Chicago Bears

He was the standout from Dennis Allen's unrelenting defense in their victory over the New Orleans Saints in which Chicago racked up a season-high 23 quarterback pressures and six sacks - Simmons recording three of those, tying his career high in a single game.

In doing so, he also became the first Bears defensive tackled to have three sacks in a game since 2014, taking his tally to five in three games since arriving in Chicago.

Game of the Weekend

This one had a bit of everything, with the Carolina Panthers and Baltimore Ravens combining for 68 points and seven lead changes. There were also five turnovers, two muffed punts, a kickoff return for a touchdown and a safety!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Baltimore Ravens against the Carolina Panthers from Week 11 of the NFL season.

Ultimately though it was the Panthers who prevailed 35-33 on the back of Ryan Fitzgerald's game-winning 37-yard field goal inside the final two minutes, their second straight win seeing them back to .500 at 5-5 on the season and strengthening their hold on the NFC South, while the Ravens are left reeling a sixth defeat in a row.

Carolina rode QB Bryce Young and running back Chuba Hubbard to victory, the former throwing for 254 yards and two TDs (as well as an interception), and Hubbard tallying 120 yards on 27 carries and two scores. The defense also finally stepped up in the second half to limit Baltimore to only seven points after the interval.

Sports.title: Qatar GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the last two rounds of the 2026 season with the Qatar Grand Prix hosting the penultimate event this weekend.

After a dramatic Las Vegas Grand Prix which saw 34 lead changes and Max Verstappen pull off a defensive masterclass, the F1 circus has moved to Qatar and the high-speed Lusail International Circuit.

Verstappen, who is set to finish runner-up in the Drivers' Championship behind Kimi Antonelli, won in Qatar last year after McLaren made a poor strategy call when in position for a one-two.

Like last year, there is a tyre limit which will create a minimum two-stop race with no driver allowed to do more than 27 laps on a set of tyres in the 50-lap race on Sunday.

This is due to the heavy loads which the tyres are put through in the fast corners which come one after another. The combination of this and this year's 2026 cars could create another fascinating race, particularly with high tension at the front between Mercedes and Red Bull as Verstappen and George Russell's rivalry escalated in Las Vegas.

Qualifying on Saturday is at 6pm UK time with the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday at 4pm, all live on Sky Sports F1.

Qatar GP track - Lusail International Circuit

The 3.367-mile Lusail International Circuit joined the F1 schedule in 2021 and is one of the highest speed tracks on the calendar due to its fast, flowing corners which punish the tyres but also makes following the car in front difficult.

In the first four editions of the event, which took place when DRS was still in use, most of the overtakes came at Turn One where drivers can make moves on the outside and inside, so it will be interesting to see whether the 2026 regulations create any additional opportunities.

Sports.title: 'This cannot continue' - Ferrari to hold fresh Leclerc-Hamilton talks after collision
Sports.content:
Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue".

After costly clashes in Monza and Mexico City earlier this season, the Ferrari drivers came together when battling over sixth place with 12 laps to go on the Strip circuit in a race dominated by slip-streaming in which the leading runners were covered by a handful of seconds for most of the race.

Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton with a move down the inside of Turn Seven but made contact with the Briton, who was spun around. Stewards found Leclerc at fault and handed him a 10-second penalty, which dropped him to 10th place. Hamilton finished seventh.

In an unusually-strongly worded statement in Ferrari's post-race press release, Vasseur said: "For the second time in three races, something unacceptable has happened between our drivers, and this cannot continue.

"We sent a very clear message to both drivers in Brazil, and today during the race we told them to think about the team when racing each other.

"Of course, in this kind of race you cannot freeze the positions because, with the slipstream, if you slow down, the car behind will overtake you.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton spins after contact with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, which led to a 10-second penalty for the latter at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

"But our drivers should have handled the situation differently, as other team-mates did both in front of and behind them.

"Charles knows he made a mistake and apologised, but that doesn't change the result."

Speaking to the written media after the race, Vasseur had said: "All the other teams, they were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race.

"[Kimi] Antonelli-[George] Russell, [Oscar] Piastri-[Lando] Norris, even Isack [Hadjar] overtook Max [Verstappen].

"Honestly, you can't imagine the frustration for me but, for more importantly, for all the guys at the [team]."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix

What will happen next?

The situation is increasingly frustrating for Vasseur given it was only three weeks ago that he had to resolve the fallout from a first-lap battle between the drivers that likely cost the team a one-two result in Mexico.

Vasseur brought Hamilton and Leclerc together to speak four days later ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, a meeting he said had "cleared the situation" and acted as "a good reset on the mindset" ahead of that weekend. The Frenchman added that they even "left my room joking together".

Immediately after Sunday's race in Las Vegas, the Ferrari team principal held an initial conversation with Leclerc having asked the Monegasque driver to see him before anything else.

Asked afterwards what they had talked about, Vasseur said: "It was not a discussion, I spoke!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur has branded Charles Leclerc's driving 'unacceptable' after he collided with Lewis Hamilton during the Las Vegas Grand Prix

"He apologised, he understands, but the result is there. That you do a mistake, you say 'it's my mistake, I'm sorry' but you did a mistake."

Asked what would happen next, Vasseur said: "I want to digest tonight [after the race] and we'll have to sit down tomorrow with both of them and to take a decision."

He added: "I want, once again, to have a discussion tomorrow. Also Charles will digest the situation and I think it's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race.

"I saw Charles a bit down and I told him what I wanted to say but I'd prefer to discuss with him tomorrow about it."

Image: Hamilton and Leclerc are approaching the end of their second season as Ferrari team-mates

'It's not a matter of rules' - Vasseur insists 'respect' the key between team-mates

The Las Vegas incident has placed renewed focus on what Vasseur will do to try and bring his drivers definitively into line, with scrutiny growing on whether Ferrari will follow the lead of other teams, such as McLaren and Mercedes, and introduce more formal 'rules of engagement' for what is allowed when in team-mate combat.

Hamilton has called for clearer policies in recent months and said after Sunday's race that "hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out".

Vasseur, however, believes the chaotic nature of Sunday's race shows that clean driving between team-mates is all about respect rather than predefined agreements.

"Honestly, it's not a matter of rules," insisted Vasseur.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the most heated clashes between Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc this season before Las Vegas

"What can you do differently except that you have to respect your team-mate? In this kind of race you have to overtake the car who is in front of you. You can't stay behind, it's completely unmanageable.

"It means you just have to do it with respect when it's your team-mate, to take less risk, perhaps to come side by side and to come back behind. But you can't put it on the paper. I think the race of today [Sunday] nobody would write a scenario like this. Nobody can imagine a race like this. It means they just have to act in a professional way.

"Today it was unprofessional."

Sports.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian.

Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century.

Infantino hopes to be re-elected for a fourth term as president in March and is the favourite to win that contest.

Quick Guide How do I 

An internal Fifa risk assessment dated 17 July, designed as one of the final steps before concluding the FFE agreement, spells out the scheme’s extraordinary scope. “This deal provides for Fifa to create a for-profit subsidiary which would have all the commercial rights for Fifa events transferred to it for commercial exploitation for the next 96 years,” one section reads.

Another internal Fifa document written the following day, outlining the proposed agreement with Thrive, says the deal’s contract period “would be for rolling 12-year license periods to a sum maximum total of 96 years” and goes further in stating Fifa would assume 51% ownership “in perpetuity”.

The existence of a lucrative “management incentive plan” for unnamed individuals helming the scheme casts into stark light the extent to which its architects could have profited. The plan is first mentioned in a term sheet and “backstop letter” drawn up by Thrive on 17 July, which refers to FFE as “Project Box”, and sets aside up to 5% of FFE’s stock as a bonus pool for the new firm’s management. In theory it could have paid out up to $50m (£38.2m) for each $1bn added to the scheme’s value above $20bn, which was its initial valuation.

The term sheet says the plan “will permit the issuance of profits interests representing up to 5% of the fully diluted capitalisation of FFE, which will dilute all unitholders on a pro rata basis”. According to the Fifa memo the pool’s existence aimed to “ensure sufficient motivation to perform well”.

A further clause states that, if Fifa breached its agreement with Thrive or completed an agreement with a rival party, Thrive would have been entitled to a break fee totalling 1.25% – $250m – of FFE’s worth. Fifa would not have been permitted to engage in talks with other potential lead buyers for a year, or until the FFE deal closed.

Fifa’s memo of 18 July confirms there was no tender process “owing to the specific and unique nature of the proposed investment”. The risk assessment document confirms its own finance department was “not directly privy to the terms of the transaction”, casting further doubt about the processes followed in pursuing the deal.
