Fifa declined to comment when contacted by the Guardian. The world governing body has consistently denied that Infantino stood to profit personally from FFE, which will raise questions as to who would have benefited from the management incentive plan.

The documents make clear that the issuance of so-called MIP units would be managed by the board of FFE, which Infantino was due to chair.

Sports.title: Inside Fifa and US Soccer’s plan for 2031 World Cup: ‘the largest women’s sporting event in history’
Sports.content:
The biggest and most lucrative event in the history of women’s sport will be confirmed at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress in Zurich on Monday, with a joint bid from the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031’s Women’s World Cup to be formally ratified by a vote of Fifa’s 211 member associations.

In the bid book submitted to Fifa last year the prospective hosts pledged to generate total revenues of $4bn if awarded hosting rights, which would represent a staggering increase on the $570m earnings from the last World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand three years ago, the first women’s tournament to break even.

While Fifa is forecasting an almost doubling of tournament revenues to $1bn for next year’s competition in Brazil, achieving a further fourfold growth by 2031 would appear to be challenging.

The United Kingdom’s bid for the 2035 tournament, which will also be ratified on Monday, does not include a revenue target. So how do the US and their co-hosts plan to generate $4bn, and what will be the impact on fans?

View image in fullscreen The 2026 World Cup brought in a record amount of revenue to Fifa. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters

The legacy of 2026

Fifa has yet to publish its financial accounts relating to last summer’s men’s World Cup, but it was undoubtedly a huge success. Gianni Infantino told the national associations on the eve of the final in New Jersey last July that Fifa’s revenue projection for the 2023-2026 cycle had increased from $11bn to $15bn, the majority of which was the product of the World Cup itself.

Emboldened by that success, the US Soccer Federation is confident $4bn is a realistic target for 2031, a projection largely based on bringing in $1.4bn from commercial deals, $1.25bn in matchday revenue and $1bn in broadcast income.

“It is a very significant increase from 2023, but I expect [the] 2027 [Women’s World Cup] to continue to be a step forward, and in 2031 to really blow this out of the park because of the maturity of our market here and the excitement that we see,” Emily Cosler, US Soccer’s vice-president of strategy who will present the bid to Fifa in Zurich, told the Guardian.

“The market here in the US is unlike anywhere else. The 2026 World Cup will be well north of $10bn in revenue, and we’re looking at a tournament with the same number of teams involved. We do have a high level of confidence in that revenue number. We expect and plan for the 2031 Women’s World Cup to be the largest women’s sporting event in history.”

Stadiums

The most likely driver of growth is the sheer size of the would-be hosts’ plans for the tournament, which will be the first women’s World Cup to feature 48 teams, increasing the number of matches from 64 to 104.

Just as significantly, most games will be played at large NFL stadiums, with the 13 of the provisional shortlist of 20 venues in the official bid – 14 in the US, four in Mexico and one each in Jamaica and Costa Rica – having capacities of more than 60,000.

To further illustrate the scale of the tournament’s ambitions, seven of these US-based stadiums hosted matches at the 2026 World Cup, with three others having staged games at the 2025 Fifa Club World Cup.

While some smaller stadiums will be used in the group stages, the hosts are targeting a total 4.5 million tickets sold, which would bring average crowds of 43,000 per match, enough to generate ticket revenue of $550m, more than 10 times the $43m made from ticket sales of 1.8 million in 2023.

The bid also projects hospitality sales of $300m, plus $400m in other match day income such as merchandising, parking and transport.

The bid actually contains 50 potential stadiums across 35 different cities, and the initial shortlist is largely theoretical at this stage, with the final decision on venues to be taken by Fifa by the end of 2028.

All of the US venues are in operation other than the proposed redevelopment of the Washington Commanders’ RFK Stadium, which is due to be completed in 2030 but is under consideration.

Mercedes-Benz Stadium (Atlanta), AT&T Stadium (Dallas), SoFi Stadium (Los Angeles) and MetLife Stadium (New Jersey) have been identified as the most likely candidates to host the final, although that decision will not be taken until 2030.

“We think every knockout round can be in a 60,000-plus seat stadium,” Cosler said. “We’ve got the infrastructure to do that, and I have a high level of confidence that every knockout round game can be a sellout. The success of our women’s national team and the NWSL has proven that we’ve got the demand for that.”

View image in fullscreen Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which hosted a 2026 World Cup semi-final, will probably be a candidate to host the 2031 final. Photograph: Brian Snyder/Reuters

Ticket prices

Fifa’s Evaluation Report published earlier this month is even more bullish than the bid in terms of the potential value of ticket sales, claiming that the widespread use of NFL stadiums should mean that ticketing and hospitality revenues “significantly exceed” the $550m forecast, which is described as “a very conservative position with significant upside potential”.

Given that the bid is forecasting a tenfold increase in revenue from the 2023 tournament based on selling two-and-a-half times more tickets, it is clear that the prices will also increase significantly from that tournament. However, lead bidders US Soccer are determined to make the event more accessible than last summer’s men’s World Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We propose a pricing table that balances what the women deserve in terms of the revenue generated from this tournament, but also access in a way that will continue to grow the game,” Cosler said. “I think there are some really good initiatives that US Soccer has done with our own national team games. We’ve partnered with local universities. We’ve offered $25 tickets that have resulted in filling stadiums and success. This isn’t a charity, but at the same time, we want this game to be accessible to fandom everywhere.”

In comparison to the men’s World Cup and other premium events in the US the pricing structure proposed in the bid looks affordable, with tickets ranging from $35 to $120 in the group stage, and $120 to $600 for the final.

Fifa will make the final decisions though, and after making almost $5bn from ticket sales last summer may choose to demand more from fans, many of whom will be concerned by one paragraph in the Evaluation Report.

“Based on the performance of other recent tournaments hosted in the region, most notably the Fifa World Cup 2026, gate revenues may far exceed initial projections,” it states.

View image in fullscreen The four-nation bid for the 2031 tournament includes the US, Mexico, Jamaica, and Costa Rica. Photograph: Howard Smith/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty Images

Commercial

The 2023 World Cup was the first time Fifa sold sponsorship deals separately from the men’s event, with 30 new partnerships bringing in $110m. This program has been scaled up significantly ahead of Brazil next year.

The projection for 2031 is $1.4bn in commercial revenue due to the size of the US market and the prospect of bespoke deals for individual cities, although that proved a source of tension last summer.

US Soccer and the other host federations are pushing for greater local control this time around, and crucially the prospective host cities have not signed binding contracts just to enter the contest, which should give them greater freedom to negotiate their own commercial deals.

“I think the end state we ultimately arrived at in 2026 resulted in a really successful tournament,” Cosler said. “Fortunately we can start there from a negotiation perspective, rather than where we maybe were six or seven years ago. Contracts were signed eight years beforehand in a way that didn’t reflect the nuances of the business model.”

Media rights

After banking $270m from the first separate sale of Women’s World Cup rights in 2023, with many of the deals coming in at the last minute, Fifa have sold $424m worth of rights for Brazil with the 2031 bidders projecting to break through the $1bn barrier, which would value the competition’s media rights as the same as the men’s 2025 World Cup.

Independent analysis conducted by Nielsen Sports has predicted that global TV viewers will increase by 58% from Brazil due to the expansion to 104 matches, and more favorable time zones for the large North American audience.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino will preside over the selection of the 2031 World Cup hosts. Photograph: Harold Cunningham/FIFA/Getty Images

Other income and tensions

The bid book is forecasting an additional $400m in “ancillary gameday revenue”, which will come from merchandising, fan fests, parking and transport charges, many of which were sources of long-running disputes involving the local authorities, venues and Fifa in the build up to this year’s World Cup.

After belatedly reaching agreements, which often involved state and local government subsidising the cost of transport and parking in particular, US Soccer is hopeful that preparations for 2031 will be more harmonious.

Having backed down from their initial demand for fan fests in every city last summer which proved undeliverable due to escalating costs, Fifa has already agreed to adopt a hybrid approach based on local provision.

“Each city ultimately had a slightly different fan fest strategy,” Cosler said. “There’s been a willingness and openness from Fifa to continue to have flexibility in that. So you might see an instance in which a city has one fan fest, like Atlanta right next to the stadium, but other cities could go down a route where there’s a couple of smaller fan fests around different neighborhoods of the cities.”

Despite inevitable difficult conversations looming over Fifa’s extensive tax demands, there is also optimism among the organizers that some of the major disputes around transport costs that plagued World Cup preparations in New Jersey and Boston in particular last summer can be avoided.

“We also have a greater understanding around the importance of funding, and the prices of public transit and security,” Cosler added. “So that will all act as the starting point. I expect a lot less friction.

“We’re starting in a slightly different position this time around. Of course, cities will still have to contribute. We’re not saying that Fifa is going to cut the check for everything, but I think it will be a more equitable type model.”

Sports.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
Sports.content:
A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.

“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.

“Haaland must be worried about him catching him now,” Moyes said. That line was delivered in jest but also represented a welcome departure from the position Barry found himself in this summer, and from where Everton stood at the close of transfer deadline day.

“I’m stopping, I’m stopping,” says Barry in a searingly honest video released on his YouTube channel in September. Entitled Never Give Up, the episode shows the striker doing exactly that after one miss too many during a private training session with his personal coach. He then breaks down in tears, head in hands in despair, after a dressing down from his lawyer. “Don’t give up, bro,” snaps the lawyer. “Where you come from, you can’t give up.”

Many players in that position would have buried the footage, afraid of broadcasting weakness or of the vicious comments that would invariably follow on social media. Barry told the BBC he spent three weeks worrying whether to post before deciding: “No, I just need to show myself. They need to learn about me because last season I showed a version of me that is not me. And they need to learn about me, how I train hard to be the best on the pitch.”

Barry’s openness was refreshingly well received, even online. In the episode he admits hitting “rock bottom several times last season” when, after a £27m move from Villarreal, he went 16 games without a goal for Everton and failed to register a shot on target until December. He finished his debut campaign in English football with eight goals from 41 appearances, a tally surpassed in 13 matches this season, and was often watching Beto from the bench.

Never Give Up is revealing not only for Barry’s emotional side. It features the striker having private training sessions in England, France and Morocco in the summer. The personal coach, lawyer and personal physio who make an appearance are part of an entourage that also includes a nutritionist and a chef. Barry will not be found wanting in his efforts to establish himself in the Premier League, a process well under way before Everton’s visit to Brentford on Monday night.

View image in fullscreen David Moyes shakes hands with Thierno Barry after the striker’s match-winning display against Coventry. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

“His general all-round play has improved,” says Moyes. “There’s lots of his all-round play that still needs to get better but I’d say his game knowledge, his understanding, has improved. I would never do down any leagues but I think coming to the Premier League from abroad is really difficult in the first year. I think he found it difficult. The expectation on players coming in and being good immediately is built up and he’s needed time to settle.

“He still needs lots of things to make him a rounded centre-forward but there are bits of it that are getting better; he’s beginning to look more clinical. Even in training I’m seeing much better actions than I did last year. Leighton Baines does quite a lot with him, and shows him stuff to make him better, but his integration is much better now too.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barry can be a bewildering player capable of inexplicable misses and touches one minute, clinical finishes and creative distribution the next. Everton’s only recognised forward should be closer to Haaland’s tally of 14 club goals for the season. But it is only five years since he started playing as a striker for Sochaux, who he joined after failing in trials as a defender for Clermont and as a central midfielder with Hamilton Academical. Lyon-born, Barry did not come through the academy system in France that could have polished the rough edges. He has had to do it all for himself and, fortunately for Everton given their calamitous end to the transfer window, he has stepped up at the right time.

Moyes, far from just being on Barry’s case, believes the 24-year-old’s story can inspire others. “It should definitely be factored in,” he says of how people should judge a player without an academy background. “Also, not understanding how it works at football clubs and how you go about it. Not in terms of how you behave – he is not a problem in that department – but just how you go about your job and what is expected of you. He is still getting used to it.

“He was in France, then went to Basel [via Beveren in Belgium], then Basel to Villarreal and then Villarreal to here. He also had quite a lot of rejections before he even got out of France, by all accounts. But there is also inspiration behind that. You can show young people that if you put the work in, keep challenging yourself and keep pushing yourself, somebody might just like what they see and pick you up.

“Basel saw something in him and obviously other clubs have decided to go for it as well. We took him as a young, inexperienced centre-forward for £27m, and a year and a half ago it was probably a worse time to be looking for strikers in the market. What ones who were bought at that time have done absolutely brilliantly? Not many. We took a gamble early. Has the gamble paid off? It’s beginning to look better than maybe it did last year but that is because of Thierno’s hard work.”

Sports.title: WSL talking points: Captain Spence inspires Spurs shock win at City and Lionesses impress
Sports.content:
1 Spence key in Spurs’ dramatic comeback win

Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a shock 3-1 victory away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” Tom Garry

2 Lionesses looking up the table

London City Lionesses head into the international break with a spring in their step, their 6-2 defeat of Crystal Palace helping them to move to within two points of City and four of league leaders Chelsea, who both dropped points at the weekend. There was a resilience to Eder Maestre’s team in their last game before the international break and the full impact of their squad depth was on show against Palace. The visitors cancelled out Daniëlle van de Donk’s opener and pulled a goal back to make it 3-2 after 64 minutes but they ultimately could not cope with the fresh legs London City could turn to in the second half. Talk may be focused on the big-spending side being in the running for Champions League football next season, but on the basis of recent form, and with Chelsea up next in mid December, thoughts may turn to am unlikely title challenge. SW

View image in fullscreen London City Lionesses’ Jana Fernandez takes a photo with fans after the win against Palace. Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

3 Charlton show grit to get campaign up and running

After 10 straight defeats in the WSL, Charlton finally have something to show for their efforts, registering their first point of the season on Sunday. It has been a tough few months for the promoted side who have been statistically interesting for all the wrong reasons. In their 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, it was their bravery and work rate that shone through as they set about defending a 17th-minute lead. They had to spend significant periods without the ball but kept Villa to eight shots and matched their three on target. At the heart of it was the 21-year-old Keira Flannery who led the midfield with a performance that was beyond her years. She exemplified the character on show in stepping up to take Charlton’s early penalty despite having missed from the spot a fortnight previous. “I’m so proud of the girls,” she said. “We all dug deep and stuck it out to the end. A point is massive. It’s a stepping stone.” Sophie Downey

4 Questions mount as Arsenal held at home … again

“You’re nothing special, we draw every week,” sang the Emirates faithful as an abject Arsenal were held to yet another stalemate by West Ham, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw their first six home games. This was probably the poorest performance of their disappointing season, the home side generating an xG of just 0.88. By half-time, they had registered one shot on target and failed to get out of their stupor until the final quarter. The full-time boos were reflected by high emotions on the pitch as the pressure on head coach, Renée Slegers, continues to mount. “I take my responsibilities because the results haven’t been good enough,” she said. “We’re not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases. It’s not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better.” One positive of the afternoon was the news that Lisa Baum was stable after being carried off on a stretcher in the first half. The club confirmed that she was responding well having suffered from “shortness of breath”. SD

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

5 Chelsea stumble at Liverpool as the goals dry up

Chelsea had 47 touches in the Liverpool box and 19 shots but came away from St Helens with a scoreless draw. The Blues have scored just three goals in their last five games in all competitions, having found the net 30 times in the 11 matches prior to that. The goals have dried up. Getting their attack clicking without the injured duo of Melvine Malard and Lauren James will be critical if they are to find the balance between attack and defence that Sonia Bompastor says they need. “I’m really happy with a lot of things we are doing right now. When you have ambitions, when you want to win titles, you need to make sure to find the right balance between being strong defensively but also being able to score goals,” she said. Their defence is doing the heavy lifting, with the fewest goals conceded in the WSL – five, with Arsenal and Everton next best with 11 conceded – and none in Europe, and they need their attack to share the load. Suzanne Wrack

6 Another set-piece mistake ruin the afternoon for Birmingham

Failing to defend a set-piece cost Birmingham badly for the second week in a row as they conceded a 94th-minute winner against Manchester United, undoing much of the promoted side’s good work in a close contest. Second-from-bottom Birmingham, who were beaten 1-0 after conceding from a back-post header from a free-kick last time out away at Aston Villa, were again caught out with a far-post delivery, this time with Simi Awujo nodding in to give Manchester United victory. Eva Olid’s visitors are now unbeaten in nine WSL matches, winning six of those, and are enjoying a club-record 14-match unbeaten streak in all competitions, while Birmingham have lost four WSL games on the bounce. TG

7 Phelan calls for consistency as Everton struggle to score

Scott Phelan said Everton need to be more consistent in attack after their 1-0 defeat to Brighton. Phelan’s side have scored just eight goals in 11 league games this season – only 14th-placed Charlton have scored fewer. Everton had 12 shots on goal in the game, six of which were blocked. The result leaves them 11th in the league and they will have to find their shooting boots soon to avoid falling down further, especially with fixtures against Arsenal and Manchester City coming before the Christmas break. “We’ve been OK defensively,” Phelan said. “Those attacking phases of play need to be more consistent. We need to be calmer, we do enough work on it at the minute but we just need those attacking moments to be brighter and calmer on matchdays.” Emillia Hawkins

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 United owe Pochettino an apology

What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson

2 Liverpool’s £100m+ trio show their worth

Liverpool in late 2026 feature three £100m-plus signings. Each of them enjoyed among their best moments yet at Anfield. Florian Wirtz appeared refreshed by working over the international break with Jürgen Klopp, clearly still a scouse whisperer. Wirtz scored an improvised goal and set up another among 10 chances he created. Alexander Isak exposing Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro for the latter’s dismissal was the moment to break the dam. If Bradley Barcola showed that finishing might not be his forte, his assist for Rio Ngumoha’s goal evidenced there is composure to accompany lightning speed. Ngumoha showed he has the talent to fetch a similar price tag, scoring and assisting at 18 years and 85 days, the youngest Liverpool player to do so since Michael Owen versus Leeds in December 1997. If Manchester United’s performance, and Mauricio Pochettino’s bizarre selection of De Ligt, opened the door, Liverpool stormed through it. Beating United never gets old, no matter their desiccated state. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola was far from perfect against Manchester United but suggested there is composure to accompany lightning speed. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

3 Tigers offer fight in overdue victory

It has been a long time between drinks for Hull when it comes to Premier League wins: three months, in fact. Perhaps that is why the celebrations were so extreme after their win over Brighton on Sunday – though the manner of it, two injury-time goals after absorbing so much pressure all afternoon, will have contributed too. It was a much-needed victory for Hull, who continue to show signs they are perhaps the best equipped of the three promoted teams to survive. The gap to the relegation zome is now five points and their win underlined why the Tigers have the two real ingredients needed to survive. Konstantinos Tzolakis produced the goalkeeping display of the Premier League season to deny Brighton time and time again, while Oli McBurnie’s late double exemplified the kind of goal-poaching Hull will need if they are to beat the drop. Keep those two areas thriving, and Hull can perhaps look upwards, rather than over their shoulders. Aaron Bower

4 Jaissle turns to Newcastle’s old guard

When Yasir al-Rumayyan, over from Riyadh to watch Matthias Jaissle’s team live for the first time this season, studied his team sheet, Newcastle’s chair presumably read between the lines. There was no space for Bazoumana Touré or Aladji Bamba (who cost a combined £78.5m) on a substitutes’ bench that in Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo featured more than £100m worth of summer signings. Meanwhile, Amar Dedic and Sean Steur (a joint £50m outlay) were withdrawn at half-time and replaced by two members of Newcastle’s old guard, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey. They played key roles in a renascent second half performance, with Jaissle’s revitalised team overcoming a 1-0 deficit to draw 2-2 against table-topping Arsenal. Afterwards Jaissle and al-Rumayyan chatted. “The chair analysed the game the way I did,” he said. “He knows about football.” Newcastle’s manager wants an increased say in a recruitment process currently controlled by sporting director Ross Wilson. Significantly, the goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek was the sole summer buy to feature in the second half. Over to you, Yasir. Louise Taylor

5 Frugal Farke teaches Chelsea a lesson

Chelsea’s injury list was no excuse for their performance in their 4-1 defeat by Leeds. They have spent more than £1bn putting this squad together and still had an £117m attacking midfielder, Morgan Rogers, in the starting XI. Leeds, by contrast, have had to be smarter with their budget and Daniel Farke has revitalised players who previously looked unlikely to flourish in the Premier League. Ethan Ampadu had to drop down a level after leaving Chelsea, while Jayden Bogle was relegated with Sheffield United five years ago. James Justin suffered a serious achilles injury not long after making his England debut in 2022 and Dominic Calvert-Lewin was close to being written off after leaving Everton in 2025. Yet Farke has found ways to improve these players. They are not fashionable names and did not cost much, but they are being coached well and are in a team with an identity. There is none of that at Chelsea. Jacob Steinberg

View image in fullscreen Dominic Calvert-Lewin (centre, bottom) loops a header over Emiliano Martínez and on to the crossbar during an all-action display from the Leeds striker. Photograph: Daniel Hambury/EPA

6 Maresca still seeking best City formula

Enzo Maresca is still in the experimentation stage as Manchester City manager. Maybe the seven straight Premier League wins to start was a false indication of where the team are, in terms of progression in the post-Pep Guardiola era. It’s inevitable that a team will dip once the early adrenaline wears off and Maresca is finding this out. To rectify his team’s slow play and lack of energy, the all-action Elliot Anderson was pushed further forward to provide the thrust from the middle of the park, while his teammates were pedestrian. Ayyoub Bouaddi was given the responsibility of sitting, with Enzo Fernández left out. “We are trying to find different solutions, right balance, and to be more consistent,” Maresca said. It looks difficult to fit all three into the team and Maresca is yet to find the right answer after four games without a win, leaving the manager to return to the lab. Will Unwin

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

7 Frank’s shift to back four poses risks

Frank Lampard said he had expected Thomas Frank to field a back three and that the realisation Crystal Palace would play a back four had prompted a hasty rejig. “I felt we needed a formation change and a little bit different players in different positions,” Frank said. “Getting some of the better players central, so I think in many spells it was very good. The main bit was the defensive side we need to keep working on and adjust.” But Palace are a team that have played with a back three for more than two seasons, and their squad is set up to play that way. If a back four is Frank’s vision, there will need to be some reprogramming; in the first half, as Frank admitted, there were times when both full-backs, Anan Khalaili and Tyrick Mitchell, pushed high and left them exposed, particularly given the lack of a natural defensive midfielder. The second half offered hope Frank’s changes can come good, but there is work to be done. Jonathan Wilson

View image in fullscreen Thomas Frank issues orders to Adam Wharton. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

8 Maddison mentors Williams-Barnett

James Maddison has backed Luca Williams-Barnett to take his spectacular full debut in his stride after helping the 18-year-old prepare for the game against Ipswich. Roberto De Zerbi revealed that Maddison played an important role in the buildup after deciding over the international break that he would give the England Under-19s forward the opportunity he has been craving. The Tottenham manager’s decision paid off handsomely as Williams-Barnett scored the opener before setting up Dominic Solanke for the second goal, with De Zerbi even comparing him to Lamine Yamal after the game. “It’s not always easy,” said Maddison when asked whether it would be difficult for Williams-Barnett to keep his feet on the ground. “He’ll have a lot of people in his ear, and it’s just about making sure he doesn’t get carried away with the praise he’s going to get. But he deserves it. He is someone who has big self-belief and confidence, so he doesn’t need to be held back. We’ve got a group of lads that I don’t think would let him get too big for his boots.” Ed Aarons

Match report: Tottenham 2-0 IpswichA

9 Ahoka makes leap for Black Cats

There was no greater endorsement of Jules Ahoka’s full Premier League debut than the words of Thomas Meunier, who knows what an elite player looks like. The 35-year-old Belgium defender counts Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Kevin De Bruyne as former teammates, but another sprung to mind on Saturday afternoon after Ahoka helped win the midfield battle at Villa Park. “Jules, incredible … six months ago he was playing in Belgium for [Royal] Antwerp and now playing like Busquets,” Meunier said. The rangy 20-year-old, who again ably deputised for Granit Xhaka, was composed in possession and quick to eliminate danger. He made 16 defensive contributions in the game – attempted tackles, blocks, clearances and interceptions – more than any other player. Ahoka began last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s second division for AC Normands but already looks at home at the top level. Ben Fisher

View image in fullscreen Jules Ahoka glides away from Aston Villa’s Boubacar Kamara. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

10 Smith steps in to boost Bournemouth

Bournemouth beating Nottingham Forest for a ninth victory in succession in all competitions speaks to the continued accomplishments of a recruitment policy that imports new faces into a settled structure. Adam Smith is a survivor from Eddie Howe’s promotion team of 2014-15. After the exile of Álex Jiménez for off-field reasons, Smith resumed at right-back to embody a club ethos that remains close to its roots despite the current rarefied status. Antonio Silva, the summer arrival who replaced Marcos Senesi, arrived into a settled defence alongside James Hill, Adrien Truffert and Smith. Only two goals have been conceded in that nine-game run, staging a platform from which attacking players are flourishing. Another week, another goal from Evanilson, in whom patience was placed under Andoni Iraola and now Marco Rose. “Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9,” said Rose. The bigger clubs trailing in Bournemouth’s wake have plenty to learn from them. John Brewin

Sports.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
Sports.content:
Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.

Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and Peter Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.

Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.

Atlético Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe.

Diego Simeone’s side are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off Real Madrid. Álex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julián Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Álex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sørloth.

In Serie A, Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the title pace despite Pio Esposito’s hat-trick.

View image in fullscreen Franck Kessié puts his arm up in delight after scoring a dramatic equaliser. Photograph: Matteo Ciambelli/Reuters

Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic’s penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito’s goals, but Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessié penalty salvaged a point.

It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season, but kept Cristian Chivu’s side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.

Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter’s lead by heading home from a corner. Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.

De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta’s fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic’s spot-kick.

View image in fullscreen Nick Woltemade scores Juventus’ opening goal in their 4-0 home win over Venezia. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters

That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessié calmly converted.

Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.

Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”

Milan returned to the top four as Gonçalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone.

Ruben Amorim’s side sealed back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month to go fourth, five points behind leaders Lazio, as club record signing Ramos broke a five-match goalless streak.

Milan got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes. Amorim accused his players of “not helping Ramos” before the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

View image in fullscreen Gonçalo Ramos enjoys ending his scoring drought for Milan. Photograph: Roberto Bregani/EPA

His third was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaká in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.

The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counterattacking as substitutes Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse struck before Christian Pulisic’s dinked finish completed the biggest victory of the Amorim era.

Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals Paris Saint-Germain with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.

Le Mans struck five minutes into stoppage time to complete a stunning 3-2 comeback ⁠victory at Marseille to move ⁠clear of the ⁠relegation places.

Substitute ​Jean Vercruysse delivered the decisive blow to end Marseille’s run of five successive league victories.

Marseille appeared in complete control ⁠after Amine Gouiri scored for a fourth consecutive game and the Brazilian winger Igor Paixão doubled their lead during a dominant first half.

Louis Mafouta pulled one back with a powerful free-kick 20 ‌minutes from time, although he then had a penalty saved in the 78th minute. Erwan Colas equalised six minutes later before Vercruysse struck late to seal all three points.

Musiala reportedly suffers further seizure

Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala reportedly suffered another seizure in training this week, according to information received by an AFP subsidiary on Sunday.

Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Last Monday’s incident was the second since he made the announcement; the player is reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play.

News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union Fifpro over what they claim is a “coordinated campaign” to pressure Musiala to renegotiate the contract he extended in 2025.

On Friday, Bayern’s supervisory board member and former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the Germany international may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form.

“Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation … because frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.”

Sports.title: Pochettino’s new-manager bounce falls flat with De Ligt move a disastrous step | Jamie Jackson
Sports.content:
Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino.

This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Factor in this result coming against United’s fiercest rivals and Pochettino’s despair is complete.

He is firmly in the dock for this loss, due to a disastrous preference for Matthijs de Ligt over Harry Maguire, the hapless Dutch defender playing a leading part in three Liverpool goals.

Towards the end the Kop chirped: “You’re going down with the City.” There may be truth in the humour unless Pochettino gets hold – fast – of the rabble inherited from Michael Carrick.

Eight short minutes into a nascent tenure and a disgusted shake of his flowing locks was the greeting to the madhouse he has taken over. By then Leny Yoro had been sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak and Anfield was in bearpit mood.

Very far from ideal – and worse was to follow. Far worse. After the Frenchman departed, Dominik Szoboszlai smashed the free-kick through a nonexistent wall and beyond Senne Lammens and Liverpool were 1-0 up.

The visitors’ next act? To enter full meltdown as Diogo Dalot allowed Rio Ngumoha room to cross and Florian Wirtz hooked home, De Ligt losing his man.

Thirteen minutes in and 2–0 behind made Omar Berrada’s talk of the “buzz” of Pochettino’s entrance at United farcical and made the chief executive appear to be as much as a chump as his latest appointee, who was authoring a new head-coach plummet, not bounce.

Yoro had been forced into hauling down Isak after De Ligt lost first the ball, then the Liverpool striker. De Ligt’s inclusion was Pochettino’s headline selection move, the dropping of Maguire handing the centre-back a first league start in a year and it backfired almost immediately.

“I don’t know who played the last game – we assessed the squad from the day we arrived and we believe it’s the best team for today,” Pochettino said beforehand when quizzed about the XI he sent out.

Words to haunt him and, as De Ligt’s only other start was in United’s 4-1 humiliation at Como last month in the Champions League, questions regarding the coach’s judgment were already being posed.

By now “sacked in the morning” was the derisory cry of Kopites as Pochettino’s new project was in the damage-limitation mode of a 5-3-1 with 21 minutes played, as off went Bryan Mbeumo for Maguire.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino had a day to forget in his first game as the Manchester United head coach. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

After spells with Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA, Pochettino’s honours roll reads one Ligue 1 and one Coupe de France – a modest two trophies in a 17-year managerial career.

Losing a Champions League final (with Spurs) and two EFL Cup finals (Spurs and Chelsea) had characterised him, to some, as a “bridesmaid” and at half‑time his team were definitively second best, fortunate to be only two behind.

In the perpetual soap opera that is United, the buildup featured a drone filming Pochettino’s first training session, Berrada’s interview and Bruno Fernandes saying new contract talks between the captain and club were paused due to the worst league start in 40 years.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Going into the game, United’s dire form contained a solitary win in 10 league matches and eight points. Why? Because they are a rabble, lacking cohesion from goalkeeper to attack, with individuals consistently embarrassing themselves and the shirt.

It cost Carrick, culpable for this too, his job and cleared the path for Pochettino to occupy a role he has long coveted. Each new manager since Ferguson has faced a two-pronged challenge: the state of the squad and the state of the club – each related.

Those who know Pochettino say he will bring charm and warmth – useful, maybe, for man-managing a group of multimillionaires, but at the interval he needed to perform the miracle of convincing them that something, somehow, could be salvaged after a diabolical opening 45 minutes.

They were staring at defeat by an Andoni Iraola side that began 10 points and 15 places better off. Pochettino hoped to avoid this by taking off Matheus Cunha for Joshua Zirkzee for the second half but ended the non-contest ashen‑faced, with Berrada and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, appearing just as lost in the posh seats.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United's chief executive officer Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox watch on at Anfield. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

A main takeaway from Berrada’s interview was his conviction that “we are heading in the right direction”. When he spoke United were 18th, and by full time they were 19th, with De Ligt a glaring emblem of their disarray. When again he was marking air not Isak, the Swede saved the centre-back more blushes by spraying wide.

This had Pochettino applauding, unfathomably, when invective seemed an apt response.

Yet when Ngumoha made it 3-0 after 66 minutes there was no more faux touchline enthusiasm from a man who had promised to “create something from scratch”. As with all who have followed Ferguson, he had discovered that United’s shaky foundations make building anything sustainable a sisyphean task.

De Ligt’s loose pass led to Víctor Muñoz’s fourth, meaning the answer to whether Pochettino’s debut could have gone any worse was a resounding no.

Sports.title: McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton
Sports.content:
Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.

Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.

A blisteringly cold November afternoon in Hull, against a promoted side where the expectation for a team challenging for the title is to win, and perhaps win with minimum fuss, too. On another afternoon, Brighton may have done just that, were it not for the heroics of Hull’s goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis.

But the best teams, the ones that end the seasons lifting the silverware, almost always seem to find a way. Tzolakis was the Seagulls’ scourge with a string of sensational saves that kept Hull in a contest where, for large periods, they were struggling to keep their heads above water.

However, the goal Brighton deserved never arrived – and as this game wore on you wondered if a team like Hull, whose commitment can never be questioned and who are tough to beat on their own turf, could dig in for long enough to provide a sucker punch on the counter. That moment arrived, not perhaps with Oli McBurnie’s goal that broke the deadlock in stoppage time, but two minutes before.

When João Costinha was shown a second yellow card in the 89th minute for a foul on Sorba Thomas, the MKM Stadium responded. They sensed that Tzolakis’s heroics could perhaps produce more than just a point, with Brighton forced to sit in and try to hold out for the closing moments. Hull surged forward, with McBurnie bundling home from close to range to spark delirium among the home support.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie adds his second goal to seal an unlikely win for Hull. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Two minutes later, with Brighton now left pressing just to try to find an equaliser, Hull caught them cold and McBurnie would tap into an empty net to seal the most unlikely of victories for the Tigers, who remain unbeaten at home since promotion. This was their first win since August, however, and a welcome tonic to put breathing space between themselves and the bottom three.

“We played against an excellent team who play intensive football,” Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, said. “I wish this feeling would never stop because we’ve had to wait for this.” But this was an afternoon that was as much about Brighton as it was Hull.

A win here would have closed the gap to Arsenal at the top to three points. In the end, this was a huge missed opportunity, with Hürzeler understandably crestfallen post-match.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In the Premier League you can never expect to win,” he said. “For us, it’s very important with our identity and every game you have to lift your standards. If you drop, the Premier League is too good and it will punish you.”

McBurnie may have been the hero but there was no doubting the star man was Tzolakis. He denied Brighton on so many occasions and otherwise the game could have been over before the interval. First, he denied Diego Gómez from close range before stopping Yasin Ayari’s effort.

Two minutes later, Georginio Rutter was the next to be denied by the Greece international with another smart save before the pick of the bunch: Tzolakis made a reaction save with his foot to turn Gómez’s effort wide after Brighton cut Hull open at will again. At that stage it felt like when, not if, the visitors went ahead. Nobody told Tzolakis that.

Half-time did little to change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross was next to be denied by Tzolakis before Gómez then shot wide from six yards out. At the other end, Hull were showing signs of coming to life, with two Mohamed Belloumi breaks a warning sign of what was to follow for the visitors.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (third from left) opens the scoring for Hull late on. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Tzolakis was finally beaten by Charalampos Kostoulas when his chipped effort beat his fellow countryman, but Regan Slater was on hand to clear off the line. Then, as time ebbed away, Costinha’s second yellow decisively swung the momentum and within two minutes, Hull scored the goal Brighton had craved.

First, McBurnie bundled home before Belloumi’s break led to him squaring for the Scotland international to tap into an empty net. Was it what Brighton deserved? Probably not. But try persuading anyone of a Hull persuasion to care about that.

Sports.title: PSG tipped to target Premier League star after devastating Desire Doue injury
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain may turn to Marcus Rashford after star winger Desire Doue tore his ACL.

PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday was stopped for five minutes as Doue received medical attention and was then stretchered off with the devastating injury.



3 Doue is set for a significant spell on the sidelines Credit: AFP

It was a heartbreaking blow for Doue, who had enjoyed a tremendous start to the campaign with six goals and four assists.

With fellow winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia also sidelined with a ruptured ACL, the Parisians' forward stocks have taken a serious hit.

It may force PSG to dip their toes into the January transfer market for some reinforcements, especially if they are to push for a third-straight Champions League title.



And European football expert Andy Brassell believes Rashford could be just the man.

Andy Brassell explains why PSG could move for Marcus Rashford

"I think if they are going to get a player, I think it makes more sense to get someone more experienced on loan," Brassell said on the Trans Euro Express.



"[Maghnes] Akliouche and especially Mika Goedts, they're players who they've (PSG) bet hard on their future and how they are going to develop over the next couple of years. So what you need is older players to guide them.

"I know they've been linked to Marcus Rashford before, they were really into the idea and then they went off it.



"I think if you look at what Rashford did last season on loan at Barcelona, he did a great job, despite the fact he came in the door and they said, 'You're not going to be a starter for us.' And, they only saw him as a winger, not a centre-forward.

"To me, that really recommends him to PSG. Someone who can be quite selfless.

"What he did in Barcelona was very different to what he did at other clubs.

3 Rashford is yet to get up and running for United since his return Credit: Getty



"I think he understands what it's like to be part of a superstar squad, to guide younger players and to know when it's your time and when it's not."

Marcus Rashford's difficult return to Manchester United

Rashford, who returned to Manchester United after Barcelona opted not to sign him permanently, is currently sidelined with a hip injury and has not played since October 13.

The 29-year-old spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan at Barcelona and finished with an impressive 14 goals and 15 assists.

As Brassell outlined, Rashford enjoyed a mixed role within the squad as he started just 26 of his 49 appearances for the Spanish giants.



But the England international has struggled to replicate his Barcelona form since his return to United, having failed to make one goal contribution this term prior to the hip injury.

Could Mauricio Pochettino block PSG moving for Marcus Rashford?

Despite the difficult start, Rashford could enjoy a fresh lease of life under new Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino.

3 Rashford is contracted to United until June 2028 Credit: Getty

Pochettino has previously expressed his admiration for Rashford and stated in 2022: "He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him."



Should Pochettino's long-standing affection remain, it could hinder any potential approach from PSG for the winger.

But, given the financial muscle they possess, PSG will not make it easy for United to turn down any offer for Rashford should they pursue a move.

Sports.title: EFL boss sacked days after confronting own fans and ripping into players
Sports.content:
EFL boss sacked days after confronting own fans and ripping into players

Swindon Town have sacked Ian Holloway.

The decision comes just days after he clashed with a supporter and had to be restrained by stewards following a 2-0 loss to Newport County.

2 Holloway's tenure at Swindon ended on a sour note Credit: Getty

Holloway also questioned his players' commitment against Newport in a post-match interview, stating that some looked like they 'didn't care'.

Swindon's statement on Ian Holloway

"Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the Club make progress season upon season," Swindon said in a club statement.

"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Ian for his hard work, commitment and endeavour throughout his time at the Nigel Eady County Ground. We wish him every success for the future.

"However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

"This has not been an easy decision, but the Board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town Football Club at heart."

Who will take interim charge of Swindon?

Swindon confirmed a search for a new manager is underway.

Until Holloway's replacement is sourced, Gavin Gunning and Steve Mildenhall will take charge on an interim basis.

The pair will be assisted by first team coach David Carney.

Ian Holloway's Swindon tenure at a glance

Holloway departs the Robins with a record of 49 wins, 24 draws and 40 defeats from 113 games in all competitions.

He took over in October 2024 following Mark Kennedy's axing as the club hovered precariously above the drop zone in League Two.

2 Swindon was the ninth different club Holloway has managed Credit: Getty

After a slow start, Holloway eventually steadied the ship and steered Swindon to a 12th-place finish.

The Robins fared significantly better under Holloway in the 2025/26 campaign and were well in the mix for the promotion play-offs.

However, a run of three defeats and one draw in the final four fixtures of the season meant Swindon fell out of the play-off positions.

Holloway then oversaw a bright start to this season as Swindon won three of their opening five league matches.

But the club has won just two of their next 11 fixtures to slip down to 17th, where they sit six points above the relegation zone.

Swindon return to action on November 28 against Chesterfield, who sit third.

Sports.title: Heroes and Villains: Matthijs de Ligt ‘played with fridge on his back’ in horror show
Sports.content:
Heroes and Villains: Matthijs de Ligt ‘played with fridge on his back’ in horror show

It appears Tottenham could have saved millions had they looked in their own backyard before spending lavishly in the summer.

Meanwhile, one Man United player was singled out for criticism and an unlikely figure has continued to mount his case for the signing of the season.



6 De Zerbi has a new weapon to unleash against Premier League rivals Credit: Getty

So, who were the heroes and villains for the latest weekend of Premier League action?

Let's hand it over to Sam Matterface, Troy Deeney and Alex Crook, who named their candidates in the latest episode of the Premier League All Access podcast.

Heroes

Konstantinos Tzolakis

Oli McBurnie's late double may have sealed a surprise 2-0 win for Hull over Brighton on Sunday, but Deeney believes the plaudits belong to Konstantinos Tzolakis.



The Greek gloveman produced a staggering seven saves - five of which came in the first half - to keep Brighton at bay.

His heroics against the Seagulls also improved his tally of saves throughout the season to a league-leading 48, with Manchester United's Senne Lammens making the second-most with 40.



If the 24-year-old, who joined Hull in the summer for an estimated £20million, keeps producing similar performances, then there's every chance he will be in the conversation for the signing of the season.

Marco Rose

After a run of six games without a win to start the season, Rose has the Cherries flying.



A 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Saturday marked Bournemouth's fifth on the trot in the Premier League and ninth in all competitions.

6 Rose had a difficult job in following Iraola, but he's proved he is up to the task Credit: Getty

One area Crook has been especially impressed with Rose is his transformation of striker Evanilson.

"He's got Evanilson looking like a goal machine," Crook said.

"Six successive Premier League games in a row in which he's scored.

"And they're not conceding goals, either. They're brushing teams aside easily."



Luca Williams-Barnett

Tottenham may have witnessed the emergence of a new superstar.

6 Williams-Barnett has given Spurs fans hope for the future Credit: Getty

On his first competitive start, teenager Luca Williams-Barnett stole the show with a goal and an assist for Spurs in their 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

The 18-year-old showed his intelligence for the goal, nipping in front of his marker to poke home Pedro Porro's cross from close range.

He then ran, and ran, and then ran some more with the ball down the left flank before he fizzed in a cross that was tapped in by Dominic Solanke.



Unsurprisingly, Williams-Barnett was met with a standing ovation when he got subbed off just after the hour mark.

Matterface was keen to point out the difference in performance levels between the teenage wizz and some of Spurs' summer signings, who are yet to fully convince.

"When you think they spent a lot of money on Savio and [Omar] Marmoush, then they've got someone like that who is 18 years of age, really impressive," Matterface said.

6 The 18-year-old is Spurs' youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale Credit: Getty



Villains

The Premier League

Hear us - well, Deeney - out on this one.

Deeney selected the Premier League as his villain, purely because Arsenal have got the title wrapped up already.

Brighton's loss to Hull meant the Gunners maintained a six-point buffer at the top after 11 games.

But, as we all know, there is a long way to go in the season and the festive period typically provides a twist or two.

And, with Arsenal gloveman David Raya potentially facing a stint on the sidelines after he went off injured against Newcastle, a successful title defence for the Gunners is far from complete.



6 Deeney can't see anyone else challenging Arsenal for the title Credit: Getty

Matthijs de Ligt

The Dutch defender had a big role to play in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Manchester United.

But that's not a good thing given the Red Devils succumbed to a 4-0 loss against Liverpool, with De Ligt at fault for three of the goals.

De Ligt was one of three players Crook rated 0/10 in Sunday's forgettable display, as Pochettino's decision to start him over Harry Maguire backfired in spectacular fashion.



Crook doubled down on his stance in the Premier League All Access podcast, describing De Ligt as 'the man who looked like he was playing with a fridge on his back at Anfield'.

6 De Ligt may have dropped down in Pochettino's thinking after a stinker at Anfield Credit: AFP

The Chelsea defence

Being the Premier League's third-highest scorers is an - dare we say it - encouraging sign for the Blues.

But that goes out the window when you realise Chelsea also boast the fifth-worst defence.



Xabi Alonso's side shipped a comical four goals against Leeds at Stamford Bridge as they slipped to a second-straight defeat.

For a club that has aspirations of returning to Champions League football, Alonso has some serious work to do on tightening a backline that leaks like a sieve.

Sports.title: Villarreal forced to make statement about cause of Nicolas Pepe eye injury
Sports.content:
Villarreal forced to make statement about cause of Nicolas Pepe eye injury

Villarreal have refuted claims on social media that Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after staring at a solar eclipse.

It comes after fans began speculating over the reason behind the protective mask being worn by the forward during matches.



3 Villarreal say reports claiming Pepe's eye surgery was caused by staring at the sun are 'false' Credit: Getty

Pepe returned to action last month after missing five matches following his scheduled eye surgery.

He has since worn a mask over his eyes to protect the injury.

However, following Sunday's defeat to Barcelona, claims it was caused by staring at the sun went viral online.

They suggested Pepe had looked directly at the sun during the solar eclipse on August 12.



Doing so can cause damage to the retina if eye protection is not worn.

Villarreal statement

Villarreal have shut down those claims, with a statement dismissing the 'false' reports.



The club said: "Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse.

"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.



"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health."

Pepe was forced to miss LaLiga matches against Real Madrid, Elche and Valencia in October as a result of the surgery.

3 Pepe missed five matches due to the eye injury earlier this season Credit: Getty

He also missed Champions League clashes with Napoli and Liverpool.

The trip to take on Barcelona marked his fifth outing since returning to the side, though.



Pepe had provided an assist against Getafe last time out prior to the international break.

However, he was unable to prevent his side falling to a 3-2 defeat against the league leaders.

The 31-year-old has now scored three goals and provided one assist in 12 appearances across all competitions this term.

Pepe joined Villarreal from Trabzonspor in 2024 before signing a contract extension the following the summer.



3 Pepe has scored three goals for Villarreal so far this season Credit: AFP

He has gone on to score 14 goals and add 18 assists in 86 matches for the Spanish outfit.

At international level, he has 14 goals in 61 caps for the Ivory Coast after starting both their recent Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against The Gambia.

Sports.title: Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha victim of robbery after defeat to Leeds
Sports.content:
Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha victim of robbery after defeat to Leeds

Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha was the victim of a robbery after the Blues' 4-1 humiliation at home to Leeds United.

In one of the few positive moments for Chelsea, Emegha scored the opening goal at Stamford Bridge as he fired the ball in-off the post with his left foot.

2 Emegha suffered a scary moment after Chelsea's 4-1 defeat on Saturday Credit: AFP

Leeds equalised moments after Emegha's first half goal through Noah Okafor.

And Chelsea suffered a collapse in the second half with a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and goals by Okafor and Brenden Aaronson sealing Leeds' first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

A poor day for Chelsea but Emegha experienced a nice personal moment as he netted his first goal for the club.

However, a scary moment came for the 23-year-old after the game as he revealed he had been robbed post-match.

Emegha tells fans he was victim of robbery

"First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday," the Dutchman posted on Instagram.

"Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support."

Reports suggest he had his phone stolen shortly after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Emegha joined Chelsea in the summer from sister club Strasbourg in the summer with the deal being arranged a year earlier.

He came through the academy at Sparta Rotterdam in his native Netherlands with Emegha also representing Belgian side Antwerp and Austrian outfit Sturm Graz in his career.

Having missed the start of the season with a hamstring injury, Emegha has made just three appearances for Chelsea, two in the Premier League.

Jason Cundy fumes at 'rotten' Chelsea

The defeat means Chelsea have lost four of their last five matches in all competitions with former player Jason Cundy left shell-shocked by their display on Saturday.

The talkSPORT host warned Blues boss Xabi Alonso he risks losing his job unless the team fixes their wretched form promptly.

"We are rotten," Cundy explained. "We were so bad, it was so bad… I'm in disbelief at what I've just witnessed.

"That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won't keep his job, I'm telling you that for nothing.

"You can't do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can't do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games."

"We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting," Cundy continued. "I'm still trying to find the words… as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better.

2 After a positive start to life at Stamford Bridge, Alonso is under pressure Credit: Getty

"It's almost disbelief at how bad we were, seriously, I'm not even joking. I'm worried… I'm worried about how this season is going to go.

"Genuinely now, I'm worried… I am worried about what this season looks like for us.

"I'm being completely honest here, I don't know whether we're going to finish… we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder."

Chelsea's are eighth in the Premier League table with their next outing seeing them face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground on Friday night, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Broadcaster Emma Jones gives update after having gallbladder removal surgery
Sports.content:
Broadcaster Emma Jones gives update after having gallbladder removal surgery

Emma Jones has provided a health update for her social media followers after having her gallbladder removed.

The presenter underwent surgery earlier this month after she was hospitalised with pancreatitis.

3 Jones has provided a health update after undergoing gallbladder removal surgery Credit: Instagram @eljonesuk

Commonly caused by a gallstone, the illness causes the pancreas to become inflamed.

Jones was scheduled to have surgery on her gallbladder on November 11 and has now revealed she has undergone the procedure.

She took to Instagram on Sunday to provide an update for her followers.

The broadcaster has 445,000 followers on the social media platform.

Jones provides health update

Jones revealed that she was discharged from hospital the same day that she had the surgery.

Meanwhile, she has been recovering well, with only a slight stomach pain when she stands up.

In a post, she wrote: "For those asking about my recovery after my gallbladder removal, it’s been so easy.

"I was in and out the same day, walking Teddy the next day, earring absolutely fine and the only pain I have is a bit of tugging around my tummy stitches when I get up off the sofa/out of bed.

"I know it’s a common procedure, so if you’re due to have this done I hope this reassures you."

Jones fronts coverage of a number of sports across a range of platforms.

3 Jones was in hospital with pancreatitis before the operation Credit: Instagram @eljonesuk

Her work includes presenting MOTDx on the BBC as well as appearing on their radio stations.

The 36-year-old also hosts a Leeds United podcast alongside conducting player interviews for the Premier League club.

Away from football, she has also presented coverage of horse racing and motorsports in the past.

As well as her Instagram following, Jones boasts 323,200 followers on TikTok.

Her page has even amassed a staggering 3.5million likes on videos from both her personal and professional life.

Jones also went viral in 2023 after calling out inappropriate messages from trolls on social media.

3 The presenter reassured fans she has been recovering well from the operation Credit: https://www.tiktok.com/@eljonesuk?lang=en

She shut down one troll's vile sexist abuse with a 'DM Helpline' skit on Instagram.

In the video, she sported a headset to hilariously hit back at the troll.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher in stitches after Gary Neville deliberately slaps himself in face live on TV
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher in stitches after Gary Neville deliberately slaps himself in face live on TV

Sky's post-match analysis of Manchester United's defeat to Liverpool took a bizarre turn when Gary Neville deliberately slapped himself in the face.

Neville as well as former Red Devils teammate Roy Keane were left outraged as a feeble Man United suffered a 4-0 drubbing away to rivals Liverpool in what was Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge.



3 Man United were limp and lifeless and were deservedly put to the sword by Liverpool Credit: Getty

Things got off to a disastrous start when on eight minutes Leny Yoro was sent off for felling Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward ran towards goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored the resulting free-kick with Liverpool breezing to a comfortable victory at Anfield as Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz sealed the rout.

Getting anything out of a game at a raucous Anfield when down a man for over 80 minutes was always going to be a tall order for Man United.



However, what left the likes of Keane and Neville fuming was the application from Pochettino's men as they seemingly accepting their fate as losers of the game early doors.

And Neville's analysis of the Man United players' attitude led to a bizarre turn of events which had Jamie Carragher and presenter Dave Jones in stitches.



Neville began: "I didn't see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here [points at his head]. I never see any of them like that."

The former right-back then proceeded to stare into space with his mouth open before continuing: "They're like that."



And then Neville shocked everyone in the studio as he slapped himself round the face before saying: "Wake up!"

Neville slapped himself on the face again and added: "Wake up, you play for Manchester United... you know what I mean."

He suddenly stopped speaking with Carragher's cackle at what unfolded became audible.

After getting over his minor embarrassment, Neville added: "Where's the actual, where's that... there's no crouch there's never any of that."



Former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge then broke the ice as he expressed his surprise at Neville willingly slapping himself in the face.

Liverpool 4-0 Man United

Man United's winless run in the league stretches to nine games with their thumping at Anfield a particularly painful one.

The game got off to a far from ideal start as Yoro clattered into Isak after Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a ball over the top; although the Frenchman was perhaps unlucky to receive a straight red as Isak's heavy tough on the ball meant he didn't have a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Szoboszlai scored the close-range free-kick and Man United's response was to not lay a glove on their opponents.



Wirtz doubled Liverpool's advantage three minutes after the opener with a well-taken effort in-off the crossbar as he connected with Ngumoha's cross from the left.

3 Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League and just a point behind Manchester City and Brighton, who are third and second respectively Credit: Getty

3 If Pochettino didn't know about the size of the task that awaits him at Old Trafford before, he certainly does now Credit: Getty

The excellent Ngumoha went from provider to scorer as he slammed in Liverpool's third from inside the box after being teed up by Bradley Barcola.



And the victory was rounded off when substitute Munoz slotted past Senne Lammens after playing a neat one-two with Wirtz with Man United sloppily losing possession in their defensive third.

With this defeat, Man United are second from bottom in the Premier League table, only above Crystal Palace on goal difference.

After a Champions League showdown against Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night, live on talkSPORT, Man United's next league outing sees them entertain Brentford on Saturday.

Sports.title: Sheepish Man United stars roll into Carrington after 4-0 trouncing at Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino brutally scraps Michael Carrick's day off arrangement as relegation threat looms
Sports.content:
Sheepish Man United stars roll into Carrington after 4-0 trouncing at Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino brutally scraps Michael Carrick's day off arrangement as relegation threat looms

Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the new manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.
