Bennett Oghifo

For 10 years, Marketsquare has welcomed Nigerian families into its stores for the food and everyday essentials they bring into their homes. Today, with close to 50 stores nationwide, we remain guided by the same responsibility: to offer products our customers can buy with confidence.

Recent reports concerning inspections at our Benin City stores have raised questions. We understand why customers would want clarity, and we welcome the opportunity to provide it.

Marketsquare is a retailer. We do not manufacture the products on our shelves. We source them from manufacturers, their authorised representatives and established supply partners, and we maintain sourcing and product documentation as part of our operating processes. Where a question is raised about a specific product, we can trace its supply and review the relevant documentation.

Regulated products may be subject to different NAFDAC approval and documentation processes. This includes a listing scheme applicable to certain imported supermarket items. We believe questions about a product’s regulatory status should be resolved by checking the documentation that applies to that product, and we are available to provide that information to the appropriate authorities.

“Our customers trust us with the things they bring home and share with their families. We take that trust seriously. We stand behind our sourcing processes, and if anyone has a question about a product bought from us, we want to hear it and address it properly.”

The Customer Experience Manager, Sundry Markets Limited

Customers who would like information about a product or wish to raise a concern can Call 07000611007, Email customercare@sundrymarkets.ng, or speak to a Branch Manager. Please share the product name and any available batch or purchase details so our team can look into the enquiry and respond directly.

The trust that has helped Marketsquare grow over the past 10 years is earned in our stores every day: in the products we choose, the care we take in bringing them to our shelves, and the way we respond when a customer asks a question. We remain committed to doing that work and to giving every customer a reason to shop with confidence.

World.title: Tinubu Commissions 845 ASPs into Nigeria Police Force
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has commissioned 845 cadets of Regular Course 8 into the Nigeria Police Force as Assistant Superintendents of Police (ASPs).

Speaking during the Passing Out Parade of the graduating cadets at the Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, the special guest of honour urged the newly commissioned officers to embrace innovation and technology to advance intelligence-led policing and build public trust through a firm commitment to justice.

Represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the president noted that the commissioning aligned with the federal government’s broader security agenda aimed at strengthening internal security and modernising law enforcement. He expressed confidence that Nigerians would feel the positive impact of the knowledge and training the officers had acquired as they serve in communities nationwide.

According to a statement by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, the ceremony marked the successful completion of five years of intensive academic and professional training, through which the graduating cadets earned bachelor’s degrees in various disciplines, alongside professional policing qualifications.

He disclosed that the deployment of these 845 degree-holding officers across commands and formations would strengthen supervisory leadership at the operational level, enhance intelligence-led policing and expand the Force’s national manpower capacity to respond effectively to contemporary security challenges.

Earlier, in his opening remarks, the Commandant of the Nigeria Police Academy, AIG Auwal Musa Muhammad, highlighted the recent commencement of operations at the Academy’s new postgraduate school, which now offers a specialised programme in counterterrorism to deepen strategic policing capacity.

He expressed appreciation to the Inspector-General of Police for his sustained institutional support in enabling the Academy to produce well-trained and disciplined officers.

During the parade, the overall best graduating cadet, Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police (C/ASP) Muhammad Hamza Hussaini, was presented with the Sword of Honour by the special guest of honour.

The ceremony was attended by distinguished personalities, including the Governor of Kano State, Alhaji Abba Kabir Yusuf, represented by the Deputy Governor of Kano State; representatives of the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives; the Minister of Police Affairs, Senator Ibrahim Gaidam; the Chairman of the House Committee on Police Affairs, Hon. Makki Abubakar Yalleman; the Chairman of the Police Service Commission (PSC), DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd), represented by the Secretary to the Commission, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani; the Chairman of the Nigeria Police Trust Fund (NPTF), DIG Zanna (Rtd); and former Inspectors-General of Police, IGP Suleiman Abba (Rtd) and IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu (Rtd).

Representatives of the Chief of Defence Staff, Service Chiefs and heads of sister security agencies, alongside senior serving and retired police officers, members of the Academy’s academic wing, traditional and religious leaders, parents and well-wishers, also graced the occasion.

The Nigeria Police Force reaffirms its commitment to continuous professional training, academic excellence and institutional reform to ensure the delivery of accountable, people-centred policing across the country.

World.title: OPay Introduces Shield Pay to Protect Nigerians against Online  Scams
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Sunday Ehigiator

Leading digital financial services provider, OPay, has introduced Shield Pay, a payment protection feature designed to help Nigerians conduct online transactions more securely and reduce the risks of payment-related scams.

The new feature allows OPay to hold funds transferred by customers until vendors or service providers fulfil agreed transaction conditions, providing an additional layer of protection for individuals buying goods or paying for services online.

The initiative addresses the growing concerns around online transactions, particularly cases where customers transfer money to vendors they have never met but subsequently fail to receive the goods or services paid for.

Under the Shield Pay arrangement, both the person making the payment (Payer) and the recipient (Payee) must have an OPay account to use the service.

Before initiating a transaction, customers can search for vendors using their phone numbers or OPay account details, while also checking their trust levels and reviews to make informed decisions.

Once both parties agree on the payment amount, purpose and expected completion time, the Payee sends a payment request to the Payer, who has 24 hours to complete the payment.

Rather than transferring the funds directly to the vendor, OPay holds the money securely until the agreed transaction conditions are fulfilled.

According to the company, after completing the agreed obligation, the Payee is required to provide supporting information as evidence of delivery.

The Payer then has seven days to review the evidence and confirm that the goods or services have been delivered as agreed. Where additional time is required, the Payer can extend the review period once by another seven days.

Upon confirmation that the agreed conditions have been met, OPay releases the funds to the Payee, who can withdraw the money into their OPay wallet at no additional charge, provided no dispute has been raised.

The company also explained that the feature provides a dispute resolution mechanism for transactions that do not go according to plan.

Where a Payee fails to deliver, delivers later than agreed, supplies goods or services that do not meet the stipulated conditions, or engages in fraudulent or misleading conduct, the Payer can raise a dispute.

Even after confirming a transaction as completed, the Payer retains the right to raise a dispute within 15 days if they subsequently discover that the agreed conditions were not fulfilled.

Once a dispute is initiated, both parties are required to submit supporting evidence within 48 hours.

OPay will subsequently review the transaction, assess the evidence presented by both parties and determine the outcome of the payment dispute.

The company said Shield Pay would give customers greater control over their payments, improve protection against payment-related scams and provide a clearer process for resolving disagreements between buyers and sellers.

Customers can access the feature through the OPay application by locating Shield Pay.

Established in 2018, OPay is a digital financial services provider in Nigeria focused on promoting financial inclusion through technology.

The company offers services including money transfers, bill payments, card services, airtime and data purchases, and merchant payments.

OPay is licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and insured by the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), with the same insurance coverage as commercial banks.

World.title: Anosike Unveils Plan to Make Abia LGAs Rich through Improved IGR
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The Abia State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has said his strategic development plans for each of the 17 local government areas of the state would unlock the rich economic potential of the third-tier governments and improve their internally generated revenue (IGR), making them wealthy and self-sustaining.

Anosike said one such plan for Osisioma Local Government Area would be to develop it as a satellite town where industrial clusters and several government-sponsored housing estates would spring up to service Aba, the commercial nerve centre of the South-east region.

He unveiled the Local Government Strategic Development Plans during the mega rally of the PDP campaign for the 2027 general election in Osisioma LGA.

Addressing party faithful, Anosike said his plans, when executed, would make the council one of the richest LGAs in Abia State.

“Aba is already filled up. As part of the decongestion plan, the government will build several housing estates in Osisioma where people can live and go to work in Aba.

Also, industrial clusters will spring up in Osisioma to service Aba. Osisioma has the landmass suitable for our development plans, and when we assume power, the economy of the council will be turned around and its internally-generated revenue (IGR) improved. It will become one of the richest local governments in Abia State in a matter of months,” Anosike said.

The PDP standard bearer said he joined the governorship race because Abians are suffering, and he desires to improve their welfare.

He accused the current administration in the state of allegedly failing to improve the welfare of the people, and should therefore be changed.

According to him, “A government that didn’t provide empowerment, subsidy, grant, palliative and other incentives to improve the welfare of her citizens, should be changed because people need to be alive to enjoy the infrastructure built by the government.

“Under our administration, we will do all these daily because the people are suffering and my mission is to end that suffering,” he explained, lamenting what he described as the high cost of living in the state occasioned by alleged non-prioritisation of agriculture in the state.

Anosike promised to float a back-to-farm state policy named Operation Feed Abia (OFA) to stimulate abundant food production; a Traders Micro-finance Bank to give soft loans to women, youths, traders and artisans; train youths on multiple skills free-of-charge; pay N90,000 minimum wage; sponsor over 30 talented footballers abroad annually; and introduce health insurance and subsidised healthcare systems to cushion the high cost of healthcare services in the state, among other welfarist programmes.

“For a government minded to improve the welfare of the people, these programmes are possible. The money to do it is there; it is Abia money and should be spent on the people.

“We are coming to change the state and empower the people with the resources they need to thrive in their various endeavours. Go and spread the message that Kelechi Anosike is coming to develop Abia State. When we take over, the life of the people will change,” he added.

The governorship candidate approved the request by Osisioma stakeholders for appointment of more than one commissioner because of its special status.

Earlier, the Director-General of the PDP Governorship Campaign Council, Chief Obinna Nwachukwu, had requested their candidate to approve about three commissionership slots if he wins and also give attention to their dilapidated roads, lamenting that roads in the council have collapsed.

The Chairman of Abia State PDP and deputy governorship candidate, Elder Amah Abraham, and Chairman of the Campaign Council, Empire Kanu, told the rally that Anosike is the only candidate in the race with genuine zeal to transform the state and improve the well-being of her people.

Others who addressed the rally were PDP candidates, including the Abia South Senatorial candidate, Chinyere Onuoha; Aba North/Aba South federal constituency candidate, Elder Bob Chiedozie Ogu; Obingwa/Osisioma/Ugwunagbo federal constituency candidate, Hon. Solomon Akpulonu; Osisioma South State Constituency candidate, Ahamefula Young Onyike; and Obingwa West State Constituency candidate, Enyinnaya Appolos, who pledged effective representation and canvassed for votes for PDP victory in 2027.

The local government party chairman, Emeka Onyenso, the LG Woman Leader, Blessing Ahaiwe, and the Youth Leader, Ahamefula Ogidi, assured the party leaders that Osisioma votes were intact for PDP as the people have resolved to support the party because they were convinced that Anosike was coming to wipe off the tears of suffering Abians.

World.title: COP31 Ends in Deadlock as Guterres Blasts Fossil Fuel Interests, Demands Urgent Climate Action
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chiemelie Ezeobi

United Nations Secretary-General, António Guterres, has expressed deep disappointment over the failure of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to reach consensus on an overarching outcome, urging governments to intensify efforts to tackle the climate crisis.

The conference, held in Antalya, Türkiye, brought together governments and other stakeholders to deliberate on global climate action, financing and the implementation of existing commitments and despite dragging two days after its scheduled end, it ended in a deadlock.

Guterres, in a statement following the conclusion of the conference, said the absence of consensus was a setback for global climate diplomacy but should not distract from the urgent need for stronger climate action.

He said the scientific evidence on climate change remained unequivocal, stressing that the outcome of COP31 should serve as a reminder that the world must do significantly more to confront the crisis and do so immediately.

“I am deeply disappointed that the #COP31 Climate Conference has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands. But this setback does not change the facts,” he said.

The UN chief, who had his final outing during the just concluded COP31, identified dependence on fossil fuels as a major driver of the climate crisis, warning that the continued use of coal, oil and gas was worsening climate-related disasters, exposing economies to price shocks and undermining energy security.

He also criticised powerful fossil fuel interests for allegedly distorting scientific evidence, delaying policies and obstructing climate action while making huge profits at the expense of people around the world.

According to him, those benefiting from activities that damage the planet should not be allowed to dictate the terms of efforts to address climate change.

Guterres recalled the commitment made by countries at COP28 in Dubai to transition away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner, insisting that the priority should now be to accelerate, finance and implement that transition.

He called on major greenhouse gas emitters to take the lead, developed countries to fulfil their climate finance commitments and all nations to contribute to global efforts.

The Secretary-General also emphasised the need to strengthen protection for vulnerable countries, particularly those that contributed least to the climate crisis but are bearing some of its most severe consequences.

He described this as a matter of climate justice, noting that the real measure of climate action would be progress beyond negotiations.

He listed reducing fossil fuel dependence, expanding clean energy, modernising electricity grids, cutting methane emissions, restoring forests, ensuring climate finance reaches developing countries and protecting communities from extreme weather among the actions required.

Meanwhile, COP31 President, Murat Kurum, in his closing plenary remarks, defended the importance of consensus in climate diplomacy, urging countries to look beyond their individual interests and consider the collective responsibility to humanity.

Kurum said the conference had brought together countries with different economic capacities, energy systems, development needs and vulnerabilities, but argued that their shared exposure to climate disasters made cooperation imperative.

“No perspective that considers only a country’s own sensitivities while disregarding the interests of the world can be accepted or tolerated in the name of humanity,” he said.

He noted that the consequences of climate change, including floods, wildfires, droughts, extreme heat and rising sea levels, were affecting countries differently but remained a common global challenge.

According to him, the concerns of small island states fighting for their survival, farmers struggling with drought, societies seeking access to energy and countries trying to sustain their industries were different manifestations of the same crisis.

The COP31 President acknowledged the gap between climate commitments and their implementation, pointing to continuing loss of lives and the impact of floods and droughts on communities, including in Nepal.

He said the responsibility of governments was now to move beyond pledges and deliver tangible results.

Kurum urged delegates not to allow fatigue or differences to derail the opportunity to reach an agreement, stressing that mutual respect and prioritising consensus over individual national interests remained essential.

“We built common ground through dialogue. Consensus brought us together in this room. And now, it is time for action,” he said.

World.title: Heat and heavy rain: Is your backyard chicken coop ready for summer?
World.content:
Chickens pant to release excess body heat, but high humidity can make it harder for them to stay cool during summer. Image: Unsplash

Keeping chickens can provide families with fresh eggs, meat and extra income.

But as South Africa enters the summer season, rising temperatures, humidity and heavy rain could make poultry keeping more challenging.

For backyard chicken owners, the weather can affect more than the comfort of their birds.



It can influence how many eggs their hens produce, how quickly chickens grow and, in severe cases, whether birds survive.

Hot weather can add an effect on chicken

Chickens cannot sweat, they pant instead to get rid of excess body heat.

However, high humidity makes it harder for them to cool down.



When temperatures rise and become too uncomfortable, chickens tend to eat less and drink more water.

Egg production decline, severe heat stress can also lead to bird deaths.

This can leave small-scale poultry keepers facing unexpected losses. Expecially those selling eggs or chickens to earn an income.



One way to reduce the risk is to make sure birds have access to shade, clean drinking water and enough ventilation.

Heavy rain can create problems too

While hot weather can affect the birds directly, heavy rain can turn poorly maintained chicken houses into unhealthy spaces.

Leaking roofs, wet bedding and poor drainage can leave chickens exposed to damp conditions.



Wet litter can also encourage the growth of harmful organisms and increase ammonia levels inside poultry houses.

Keep bedding dry and make sure rainwater drains away from the area where birds sleep.

Good ventilation remains important, even when its raining.



Why checking the weather forecast matters

Poultry keepers do not have to wait until their chickens show signs of heat stress before taking action.

A 72-hour Enthalpy Comfort Index Forecast can help farmers anticipate periods when temperature and humidity may create uncomfortable conditions for their birds.

This gives them time to check ventilation, refill water containers and make other preparations before the heat becomes severe.

World.title: Da Cruz takes another swipe at referee ahead of Kaizer Chiefs vs Pirates final
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz still feels aggrieved by his side’s Soweto Derby defeat to Orlando Pirates last month.

The Frenchman will get another opportunity to face the Buccaneers in the Carling Knockout Cup final after guiding Amakhosi to a 2-1 victory over Mamelodi Sundowns in Sunday’s semi-final.

When asked about facing Pirates in the final, Da Cruz once again reflected on their previous meeting, suggesting that a refereeing mistake played a role in Chiefs’ defeat.

“I know it’s not easy to be a referee, especially without VAR, so it can happen. But we produced a good game against Orlando Pirates. We know it will be a tough game, so let’s see what will happen.”

Da Cruz not happy with Pirates game

Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates last met in a cup final during the 2025 Nedbank Cup, with Amakhosi emerging victorious with a 2-1 win.



With Chiefs now looking to repeat that achievement and get one over their bitter rivals, the Carling Knockout final promises to be another fiercely contested Soweto Derby. Da Cruz will hope to beat Pirates to earn his first trophy with Amakhosi.

The two giants are scheduled to meet in Cape Town on 12 August.

World.title: Springboks name debutant to face France
World.content:
Emmanuel Tshituka will be in line to make his Test debut in the Springboks’ Nations Championship final against France on Sunday in London if he takes the field in a rejigged team.

In total, seven changes and one positional switch have been made to the starting team that faced Ireland last weekend.

One of these switches was injury enforced, following a niggle picked up by Damian Willemse in Dublin. As a result, Manie Libbok will start at flyhalf, with Sacha Feinberg Mngomezulu moving to fullback.



Ruan Nortje, who was withdrawn before the match, has also not recovered in time, which paves the way for Salmaan Moerat to start in a new lock combination with Lood de Jager, who was on the bench in Dublin.

The other changes are in the front row, where the trio of Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit will start.

Erasmus again opted to name six forwards and two backs on the replacements bench, with Malcom Marx, Ox Nche and Wilco Louw serving as the back-up front row, while Eben Etzebeth provides lock cover, and Tshituka – the brother of Springbok Vincent Tshituka – and Paul de Villiers offering loose forward support.



Morne van den Berg (scrumhalf) and Canan Moodie (utility back) are the two backs on the bench.

Only four players in the match-23 did not face Ireland last week – Moerat, Libbok, Tshituka, and Reinach – while a further four have dropped out of the matchday squad that faced France at Stade de France two weeks ago – Willemse, Nortje, Jasper Wiese (who is currently serving a suspension), and Franco Mostert.

Moerat, who will play his first match on the Springboks’ November tour after being forced to withdraw from the clash against Italy due to back spasms experienced in the warmup, is in the engine room alongside De Jager, while Erasmus retained the same loose trio as last week of captain Siya Kolisi, Pieter-Steph du Toit, and Cameron Hanekom.



Reinach and Libbok slot into a settled backline, which includes centres Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel, and the back three of Kurt-Lee Arendse, Ethan Hooker, and Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

World.title: All Blacks lose another key player to France
World.content:
The All Blacks will lose another experienced player to French rugby, with Chiefs captain Luke Jacobson confirming he will leave New Zealand at the end of the 2027 season. Image: Patrick Hamilton / AFP

The All Blacks will lose another experienced player to French rugby, with Chiefs captain Luke Jacobson confirming he will leave New Zealand at the end of the 2027 season.

The 29-year-old loose forward has signed a contract with French club Aviron Bayonnais that will keep him in France until 2030.

READ | Not even Rassie Erasmus can save these All Blacks!



Jacobson’s departure will come after the next Super Rugby Pacific campaign, which will be his final season with the Chiefs, the team he made his debut for in 2018.

His move to France will follow the conclusion of his New Zealand Rugby commitments in 2027.

However, Jacobson is hoping to remain part of the All Blacks setup through next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Jacobson’s All Blacks future

Jacobson has played 30 Tests for New Zealand since making his international debut in 2019.

He became an increasingly important figure under All Blacks coach Dave Rennie this year, starting the team’s first six Tests of the season.



He also captained New Zealand against the Sharks before an elbow injury brought his season to an early end.

His experience and leadership have made him an important part of the Chiefs and the All Blacks, with his departure representing a significant loss for New Zealand rugby.

Chiefs face losing influential captain

Jacobson has made 106 appearances for the Chiefs since his debut in 2018.

His final Super Rugby Pacific campaign will give the franchise another opportunity to end its title drought.

The Chiefs have lost their past four Super Rugby finals, with Jacobson captaining the side in three of those defeats.

His departure will leave a sizeable gap among the Chiefs’ loose forwards, although the franchise has already started preparing for the future.

Jacobson’s move is another reminder of the growing attraction of French club rugby for established international players, with the Chiefs now facing the challenge of replacing one of their most experienced leaders.

World.title: Louis Oosthuizen joins Nedbank Golf Challenge field
World.content:
South Africa’s Louis Oosthuizen has been added to the strongest contingent of Major champions in recent Nedbank Golf Challenge history as he returns to Africa’s Major this year.



The 2010 Open champion will join fellow Major winners Wyndham Clark, Justin Rose, Bryson DeChambeau and Bubba Watson at Sun City’s Gary Player Country Club from 3-6 December.



This group of five players has a combined eight Majors between them, and all of them are chasing their first victory in Africa’s Major.

READ | Louis Oosthuizen quits LIV Golf

‘Excited to see the changes’

“I’m looking forward to competing in front of the Sun City crowd again. The Nedbank Golf Challenge is one of the highlights of the golf year, and the field this year is incredibly strong. I’m also excited to see the changes to the Gary Player Country Club course, which is such an iconic golf course,” said Louis Oosthuizen.



This will be Oosthuizen’s eighth appearance in the Nedbank Golf Challenge, and his first since 2019.



The former world number four, 11-time winner on the DP World Tour and holder of a rare career “Grand Slam” of runner-up finishes in all four Majors returns to a Nedbank Golf Challenge where he has an enviable record of consistency.



Louis Oosthuizen has never finished worse than tied 14th in his previous seven appearances, including a top finish of third in 2018.



Now he’s hoping to add his name to a glittering list of fellow South Africans who’ve triumphed in Africa’s Major.



‘Incredible champions’

“Since my first Nedbank Golf Challenge in 2013 I’ve always performed well in the tournament. The golf course and the whole atmosphere there brings out the best in my game. We’ve had some incredible South African champions over the years and I’d love to add my name to that list,” he said.



The Major winners join a field that also includes multiple DP World Tour champion and 2026 Race to Dubai Rankings runner-up Eugenio Chacarra, three-time DP World Tour champion and 2025 Race to Dubai Rankings runner-up Marco Penge, PGA Tour champion Ben Griffin, and a strong South African contingent including Casey Jarvis and Jayden Schaper – who both had standout seasons on the DP World Tour and have secured dual membership of the PGA Tour – Branden Grace, Dean Burmester, Aldrich Potgieter, Christiaan Bezuidenhout, Yurav Premlall, Hennie du Plessis, Michael Hollick, Thriston Lawrence, Richard Sterne and Shaun Norris.

World.title: Malcolm Marx rewrites Springbok history books with Ireland try
World.content:
Malcolm Marx's try against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday saw him move to joint-third in the list of all-time Springbok try scorers. Image: SA Rugby

Malcolm Marx’s try against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday saw him move to joint-third in the list of all-time Springbok try scorers.

It also saw the 32-year-old hooker extend his record as the leading all-time forward try scorer for South Africa.

Marx, who was playing in his 97th Test, scored his 33rd try in the green and gold jersey.



Marx, the reigning World Rugby Player of the Year, has now scored six tries in his last six Tests.

Saturday’s try was his first against Ireland.

Move up the list

Malcolm Marx tied Makazole Mapimpi in the Springbok try-scoring charts and could well challenge second-placed Joost van der Westhuizen (38 tries) before hanging up his boots.



Leading try scorer Bryan Habana with 67 tries may be out of reach of the two-time Rugby World Cup winner.

Marx’s 165 Test points puts him in joint 14th place in the list of all-time Springbok Test points scorers, alongside Mapimpi and Frans Steyn.

Many years ahead

In terms of the all-time leading try-scoring forward in Test rugby history, Marx currently sits joint second alongside Diego Ormaechea from Uruguay (33 tries), while All Blacks star Ardie Savea (34 tries) leads the way – for now.



At just 32 years of age, Marx has several years ahead of him – if he so wishes – to further rewrite rugby union’s history books.

Meanwhile, Marx confirmed his departure from Japan in recent weeks, electing to return to South Africa and join the Bulls in Pretoria.

World.title: This one crime is nearly extinct in South Africa, but not thanks to SAPS
World.content:
The banking industry has helped to eradicate this crime. Image: Pexels

Many will argue that South Africa is a naturally dangerous country. But one crime suggests criminality can be drastically reduced.

In the last 10 years, this crime has only been recorded 4 times.

In 12 months, no province has recorded this crime

South Africa places seventh in a global criminality ranking of 193 countries.



But one type of robbery suggests the country doesn’t need to be as dangerous.

Bank robberies have been almost eradicated in South Africa.

According to crime statistics released by the South African Police Service (SAPS), a bank robbery hasn’t occurred since the first quarter of 2025.



Between April and June 2025, SAPS recorded one bank robbery. The robbery occurred at Balfour TVL in Mpumalanga’s Gert Sibande District.

Annual statistics from 2024-2025 show the crime was recorded 3 times.

Those robberies occurred in the Eastern Cape and Gauteng.



Before then, no bank robbery had been recorded since April 2016.

Although bank robberies are declining, commercial robberies and cash-in-transit robberies are not.

This suggests the decline isn’t the result of policing but action taken by the banks.



Why is bank robbery extinct?

South Africa has over 4 000 bank branches. With four bank robberies in 10 years, the bank robbery rate is less than 0.1%.

The Cambridge Handbook of Forensic Psychology highlights the “main motivation for robbery is a need for fast cash.”

South African banks are making branches the worst targets for thieves wanting quick cash.



The industry has been phasing out cash, encouraging customers to use ATMs or digital channels.

Without cash at a branch, thieves have no reason to attempt the crime.

Can SAPS take credit?

Unfortunately, bank robberies show how the industry could eradicate the crime.



Bank robberies have been declining globally as the global industry finds ways to trim losses.

In South Africa, banks have focused on reducing cash handling.

But data focused on other commercial robberies show how little effect SAPS has had on crimes that affect businesses.



Commercial robberies are only slowly declining, and cash-in-transit robberies have stalled, except for a few quarterly spikes.

In the second quarter, for example, SAPS recorded a 50% rise in cash-in-transit robberies compared to the same period the year before.

In the first quarter, cash-in-transit robberies declined by 2 counts.



Sharp swings in robbery numbers show that SAPS isn’t a deterrent.

Burglaries at non-residential premises rose 2.8%, and uncategorised thefts rose 3.8% in the second quarter.

The difference between first- and second-quarter cash-in-transit crimes highlights how eager thieves are to find quick wins.



Only one barrier exists between a thief and cash in a cash-in-transit vehicle: armed security.

But the amount of cash in the vehicle makes this crime enticing to criminals hoping for a big payday.

World.title: 'We will never give up on Joburg': Zille on coalition negotiations
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - “He who laughs last, laughs loudest.”

That was the message from Democratic Alliance (DA) Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille, who insists the party is not giving up on its bid to govern the City of Johannesburg.

Speaking to eNCA ahead of the city's inaugural council sitting, Zille said the DA would not seek to delay proceedings through legal action, but maintained that the party had not thrown in the towel.

“We definitely never throw in the towel,” she said.

Zille said the DA was prepared to take its place on the opposition benches if its coalition proposals were rejected.

She maintained that the party had made its final offer, although negotiations between political parties were still underway.

“Negotiations are still ongoing. We've made our final offer. And if people don't want to accept our final offer, we'll be in opposition. I think the negotiations are still going on between all of those 18 parties, those tiny opposition parties that have been scrambling to get into some coalition and get a piece of the pie. And I know that the negotiations aren't finished in the ANC.”

Zille said the DA remained committed to representing Johannesburg residents who had voted for the party and wanted a change in the city's political leadership.

“We stand here for the residents of Joburg who voted for us and most residents actually chose not to vote for the former coalition and to vote for a new deal. And if they don't get one, well, that'll be sad, but we will be in the opposition fighting for Joburg. We will never give up on Joburg.”

She added that coalition negotiations could not be considered final until the relevant party structures had formally ratified any agreements.

“As we sit here today, negotiations aren't over. We've made our final offers, and that's fine. But in parties that get into coalitions, they normally have their executive committees, their federal executive or their national executive committees, actually ratifying those agreements. And that has not happened yet. So, we're saying that the negotiations aren't over, and let's do things when they are.”

World.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992: media
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday.

The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard's win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress' 435-member House.

The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

It also beats the 257 seats won when Barack Obama was elected president in 2008 but falls short of the 334-seat majority the party won at the end of the 1930s, which is the largest on record.

Republicans have not controlled more than 250 House seats since the start of the Great Depression which saw mass unemployment, acute deflation and widespread poverty.

"House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM," House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X.

The 56-year-old New Yorker is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House, after being nominated by his party.

Sunday's result came after Foxx requested a recount.

Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who "graciously conceded following the results of the recount process."

"Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices," he added on X.

Roy Cooper, the state's former governor, won election to the Senate, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from North Carolina since 2008.

Four other House races remain outstanding: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff.

The Democrats midterm triumph hands the party the power to block Trump's agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

Democrats have already unveiled plans for wide-ranging investigations into Trump officials and his business interests when they take control of the lower chamber in January.

Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters on Wednesday, warning members of Trump's family and senior administration figures to preserve documents ahead of investigations into alleged corruption, immigration abuses and the handling of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The administration has pushed back against the threatened scrutiny.

November's midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump's war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

World.title: Dumisani Khumalo, other top cops sue State for unlawful charges
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Crime intelligence boss Dumisani Khumalo, Dineo Mokwele and several other senior police officers are taking legal action against the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) and the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA).

Mokwele’s lawyer has confirmed the legal action to eNCA.

Among those facing legal action are former IDAC head Andrea Johnson, as well as the ministers of Justice and Police.

The legal battle comes amid growing controversy surrounding the arrests of Mokwele, Khumalo and other senior police officials, who were charged before the cases were subsequently withdrawn.

Johnson is also facing a separate legal challenge linked to her testimony before the Madlanga Commission.

During her testimony, she described Mokwele’s appointment as a “token appointment” but later apologised.

Mokwele, Khumalo and five other top cops were arrested on charges of fraud and corruption. The charges were withdrawn in August.

World.title: 136 seats stand between ANC-led coalition and power in Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The DA is calling for the first sitting of the Johannesburg council to be postponed, as the party faces the prospect of being shut out of leadership by an ANC-led coalition.

On Sunday, the DA said it had submitted a proposed “stability framework” to the ANC, aimed at securing stable government in 137 municipalities across the country where no party won an outright majority.

The party said it had yet to receive a response.

Under the proposal, the ANC would lead 93 councils, the DA 24 and the IFP 20, subject to an agreement with the IFP.

Elections analyst Wayne Sussman says the ANC could secure enough support to govern Johannesburg by joining forces with the EFF, MK Party and smaller parties.

A total of 136 seats is needed to secure a majority in the 270-seat council.

“The magic number is 136. If you get 136 seats in the council meeting today, you form a government.

“So, we're expecting Herman Mashaba to be the mayoral candidate of this bloc of four parties. That gets you to 43 seats. Then you add the ANC, taking you to 106. Add the EFF, which came fourth in Johannesburg, and you're getting close. Bring in uMkhonto weSizwe and you get over the line.

“But there was that famous picture on Thursday or Friday, with Panyaza Lesufi and a whole host of other political parties, including Rise Mzansi. That takes you to 143. The Patriotic Alliance brings you to 148.

“That is a big coalition, and you've got a buffer. The risk is that the more parties you bring into a coalition, the more positions you have to dish out, leaving fewer portfolios for your own party.

“These are delicate balancing acts, but this could well be the coalition we see today.”

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Witness C takes stand at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
PRETORIA - 'Witness C' is expected to take the stand when the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry resumes its hearings in Pretoria on Monday.

The inquiry has been hearing allegations involving the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD).

The commission heard testimony from JMPD Chief Superintendent Tintswalo Rikhotso last week.

During her testimony, Rikhotso alleged that a syndicate involving JMPD members, Hawks officers and informers used tip-offs to identify, target and rob businesspeople.

She claimed that the alleged network exploited information to carry out the robberies, raising questions about possible collusion between law enforcement officials and informers.

Rikhotso also faced allegations that she had offered a bribe to have a case against former JMPD officer Eric Mphahlele disappear.

However, she denied the allegations, rejecting claims that she attempted to interfere with the case.

World.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
World.content:
KYIV - Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, after attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people.

Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.

Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed last week a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with US counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping.

An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometres (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko.

AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smouldering rubble.

"Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11.

World.title: Ukrainian drones sink Russian warship in North Africa
World.content:
Ukraine sank a Russian warship docked in Libya and disabled a cargo vessel off the North African country’s coast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, in Kyiv’s latest attack on Russian assets far from the frontlines.

The warship — identified as the 344-foot navy corvette Merkury — was attacked with with seven maritime drones, sinking the ship and destroying a combat helicopter on board, Zelensky said in a post to Telegram.

Dramatic footage Zelensky released showed Ukrainian sea drones speeding towards the ship –– one of the newest ships in Russia’s fleet — which erupted into a giant ball of flames in the dock in Benghazi in eastern Libya. Photos taken by satellite imagery company Vantor showed the vessel submerged following the attack.

Ukraine’s second target was cargo ship the MV ANGARA which Zelensky said was being used by Russia to transport weapons.

The drone boats were “transported to the designated location and launched from a so-called ‘mothership,’” said Ukraine’s intelligence agency.

Russia has not yet commented on the attacks, which came hours after a suspected Ukrainian drone hit a Russian cargo ship about 2,000 miles away in the Baltic Sea.

The Ukrainian strikes also came days after a historic summit between US President Donald Trump, Russian leader Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping failed to make any progress towards ending Moscow’s war in Ukraine.

The 1,800 ton Merkury was in Benghazi to refuel under a maritime cooperation agreement before it intended to return to Russia, according to Libya’s Government of National Stability (GNS).

It incorporates some of Moscow’s latest shipbuilding technology, including radio absorption materials and a hull and superstructure designed to decrease its radar signature, Russian state media TASS reported when the ship joined the fleet in May 2023.

The GNS, which controls eastern Libya, said it has launched a joint investigation with Russia into the incident. It said it was not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, and would not allow its territory to be turned into an “arena for settling scores.”

War spills into Africa

CNN has previously reported on Ukraine’s presence in Libya, Mali, Chad, Niger, Sudan and Burkina Faso as it tries to counter Russia’s growing influence in Africa, particularly the mineral-rich, coup-prone Sahel region.

Oil-rich and war-torn Libya is ruled by two governments: the UN-backed Government of National Unity (GNU) in the west, based in Tripoli, and the GNS in the east.

One Ukrainian naval drone operator deployed in Libya told CNN earlier this year his unit was using a military base in Misrata, a city east of Tripoli, as a launchpad to attack Russia’s shadow fleet in the Mediterranean in exchange for training local forces.

As the Merkury erupted in flames Sunday, a cross-border firefighting operation was underway roughly 2,000 miles away in the Baltic Sea, where one day earlier a Russian cargo ship was struck by suspected Ukrainian drones, according to the Finnish military.

Emergency services from Finland, Russia and Estonia were working to put out a blaze on the Sparta II, in a rare instance of cooperation between Russia and the NATO members and steadfast Ukrainian allies.

The Merkury joins some 40 other Russian naval vessels lost in the war, most notable among those the guided-missile cruiser Moskva, the flagship of Moscow’s Black Sea fleet, sunk by a Ukrainian missile attack in April 2022.

Naval analyst Carl Schuster told CNN protecting ships in foreign ports is difficult for any navy.

“When a warship is in a foreign port, the host country is responsible for the ship’s physical security and protection,” he said.

A foreign vessel must be absolutely certain it is under attack before it can engage an enemy in port, and Libyan security is circumspect, Schuster said.

Ukraine has a large merchant fleet that can “provide a lot of seemingly innocent launch platforms” for attacks like the one in Benghazi, he added.

“We are looking at a new era of maritime unconventional warfare,” Schuster said.

This story has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are at the highest levels since the conflict began
World.content:
Reported attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz are at the highest levels since the Iran war began, maritime data shows, as Tehran seeks to re-exert its control over the critical waterway amid falling oil prices.

In October, the number of attacks reported to the Royal Navy-affiliated United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) exceeded 30 for the first time since the US-Iran war began in late February.

As of Sunday, at least 22 attacks were reported in November, the second highest figure since the war began, according to a CNN analysis of UKMTO data. The reporting area covers the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

The numbers from the UK maritime monitor are likely an undercount since the organization only reports incidents verified through primary sources. “Additional incidents are known but cannot be independently verified,” UKMTO said in its weekly overview published on Friday.

As attacks on ships in the strategic waterway have stepped up in recent months, many are believed to have switched off their commercial tracking devices to avoid detection. In a report released in mid October the organization said it was “struggling to accurately report true number of attacks with majority of vessels attacked refusing to report to UKMTO.”

Meanwhile, Iran’s military has claimed near-daily incidents involving commercial ships transiting through the strait, often attributing them to sea mines rather than drone or missile attacks.

Before October, the number of reported attacks in the region averaged around 10 per month. Numbers vary, but data from the International Maritime Organization also points to October as having the highest number of confirmed incidents so far this year.

Since the conflict began, the strait has become a heavily contested frontier, with attacks there disrupting oil and gas shipping and sparking global economic fallout.

Iran began trying to halt traffic in the wake of the US-Israeli attacks that launched the war. In response, the US imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, and as CNN previously reported, Gulf producers have found ways of getting ships through the strait.

Commercial traffic through the channel – through which a fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war – remains at a reduced level when compared to the 2025 baseline.

As global oil prices fall and the Iran’s domestic crude revenues come under increasing strain, Tehran has been stepping up attacks, with experts saying the country is losing its leverage over the waterway and could escalate attacks further in an attempt to force concessions from Washington.

No need for a deal, Trump says

The International Energy Agency attributes the recent decline in oil prices to a recovery in Gulf exports. Prices also fell after the US midterm results as concerns over fresh US military action in the Middle East subsided.

“Markets appear to be increasingly assuming that a return to full-scale war is unlikely and that oil supplies will gradually recover,” Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group (ICG) think tank, told CNN. “But that assumption could change quickly if Iran decides to intensify the confrontation.”

A man pumps fuel at a gas station in Miami, Florida, on November 10. Joe Raedle/Getty Images

Meanwhile, Iran’s domestic oil revenues are falling sharply as the US blockade of Iranian ports continues to stifle the country’s supply of oil to global markets, according to maritime data tracking service Kpler.

“Iranian oil on water outside the (US) blockade zone has hit zero as the last cargoes discharged in China earlier this month. Consequently, Iran’s oil revenues could drop to zero by mid-December,” Kpler reported in late October.

US President Donald Trump said this month the US doesn’t “need a deal” with Tehran and ordered Vice President JD Vance to turn his focus elsewhere.

“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed!” Trump posted on Truth Social. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”

He later indicated he wouldn’t hesitate to resume military strikes in Iran if necessary.

Three tankers struck in Hormuz since Friday

During the latest attacks, projectiles struck three tankers exiting the strait on Friday and Saturday, according to Marisks, a maritime risk management company.

Marisks did not confirm who was behind the attacks, though it said Iranian involvement was “assessed as likely.”

Fire erupted aboard the Captain Leon, a Marshall Islands-flagged chemical and oil tanker, after it was struck at the bow at 3 p.m. UTC (10 a.m. ET) on Friday. All crew were reported safe, Marisks said.

The Torkel, a Hong Kong-flagged crude oil tanker, caught fire after being hit in the stern at 5 a.m. UTC on Saturday (midnight ET on Saturday). Less than an hour later, the Arina, also Hong Kong-flagged, was struck in the engine room by a missile.

The attacks demonstrate the “continued critical threat” to commercial shipping in the region, Marisks said, particularly through the “southern corridor” near Oman’s coastline which Iran vehemently opposes.

World.title: Trump’s showdown with Congress is catching fire, weeks before Democrats take power
World.content:
In a major power play, President Donald Trump is seeking to limit who, how and what Democrats can investigate as they gear up to use their new powers in the next Congress to target his alleged corruption.

Key Democratic investigators are pushing back, including against Trump’s executive order Friday that warned businesses that deal with the federal government to coordinate requests for information or communications with the White House.

Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin, incoming head of the House Judiciary Committee, said Sunday that the order “has all the force of an interoffice memo. It’s like saying, ‘We’re closing early before the Thanksgiving holiday.’ It doesn’t mean anything in terms of federal law.” Raskin insisted on CNN’s “State of the Union” that “we have got the Constitution on our side.”

Trump ordered companies to comply with executive privilege, the president’s constitutional prerogative, to withhold information from Congress or the courts that could infringe on his office’s capacity to function. He stipulated that firms that refused would risk “the potential termination or cancellation of contracts and the potential debarment or suspension of contractors.”

Preemptive exchanges over congressional oversight on multiple fronts offer a taste of the intense Beltway battle sure to unfold next year. The administration has already threatened Democratic investigators with possible prosecution as it resists probes into White House dealings with corporate CEOs, Trump’s architectural projects, including his new ballroom; the business activities of Trump’s family and Cabinet members, and the origins and conduct of the Iran war.

The aggressive White House mobilization suggests the president’s claims of executive power will be as expansive in his own defense as they were when he went on offense early in his second administration. A fierce rearguard action was reinforced by the appointment of the combative Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and House Republicans’ selection of Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan, an adept force of disruption, as their leader.

Treacherous days loom for companies that did business with Trump

Trump’s order previews a novel confrontation with Democrats over the scope of executive privilege, which is derived from the president’s Article II powers in the Constitution and the separation of powers. The concept seeks to protect the confidentiality of the president’s decision-making.

His order on Friday appears — taken to its limits — to imply that any administration business, including with outside contractors, is immune from investigation by Congress. Yet the Supreme Court held in various rulings that the privilege is not absolute and must be weighed against the need for public disclosure. It has stated that the courts, not the president, are the final arbiter in most cases.

Any prolonged legal showdown with Congress over the constitutionality of likely blanket privilege claims would mirror a classic Trump strategy in life, business and politics: using the legal system to delay accountability.

The sun sets behind the US Capitol building on November 2 in Washington, DC. Kevin Carter/Getty Images

Executive branch power consolidation over recent decades went into overdrive with Trump, who believes there are few limits on his authority and has sometimes been emboldened by a conservative Supreme Court majority with its own expansive view of the presidency.

But Trump’s order also points to another significant possibility: that companies who contract with the federal government could find themselves drawn into a bitter fight with two separate and co-equal branches of government. Such firms might risk their immediate business prospects by declining to cooperate with the White House or antagonize Democrats who might — depending on future election results — take the presidency and maintain control of Congress when Trump leaves office in two years.

The Trump Justice Department is unlikely to prosecute executives who refuse to comply with congressional subpoenas. But a future administration might take a different view, and top firms could be faced with agonizing political choices.

The looming showdown may help define how the public perceives the new House and Senate. Democrats are under pressure to immediately alleviate voters’ cost-of-living woes — a mission that will require the support of a veto-wielding president already balking at their investigative ambitions. But voters also wanted Trump’s bulldozing presidency reined in, and if Democrats have a mandate, it is partly based on concerns about alleged corruption.

Political complications to come were reflected in Trump’s comments in a Fox News interview Saturday that he could do “tremendous things” on healthcare and even on immigration with Democratic leaders Sen. Chuck Schumer and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries. But on Sunday, he wrote on Truth Social that Schumer, who faces a leadership challenge from Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, “failed badly” as leader before, “and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”

Trump is already pitching a narrative that Democratic probes are overreach amounting to political persecution — a move he used effectively in winning back the White House in 2024, despite being investigated over his attempt to overturn the 2020 election results and his alleged hoarding of classified material.

‘A lawless royal edict’

Raskin insisted on “State of the Union” that Democrats won’t be deterred.

“Trump is scrambling to cover up all of the corruption, the kickbacks, the bribery, the insider influence,” the Maryland lawmaker told CNN’s Dana Bash. “They have issued a totally unprecedented and lawless royal edict that private companies not speak to congressional investigators. Every US company, every citizen owes Congress his or her truthful, honest testimony when called to come and testify. And Donald Trump may not like that, but that’s the reality of the situation.”

Democrats have already made clear that their investigative sweep will be huge.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal has sent letters to multiple companies ahead of a planned inquiry into the funding and construction of the White House ballroom. Rep. Henry Cuellar, top Democrat on the House Appropriations Homeland Security subcommittee, is seeking to investigate contracts awarded by the Department of Homeland Security in the last two years. Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia, incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, sent letters requiring the preservation of documents to Vice President JD Vance, members of the Trump family, Miller and Attorney General Todd Blanche, among others.

Democratic Rep. Jim Himes, in line to run the House Intelligence Committee, last week warned that Congress would withhold government funding for systems developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX if Musk and the Trump administration refuse to disclose who is responsible for ordering the slowdown of Starshield, Ukraine’s military-grade Starlink satellite service.

Democrats may also come calling on law firms that bowed to Trump’s pressure to avoid litigating politically sensitive cases.

Democratic Sens.-elect Juliana Stratton of Illinois, Annie Andrews of South Carolina, Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, James Talarico of Texas, Josh Turek of Iowa and Troy Jackson of Maine at the US Capitol on November 9. Win McNamee/Getty Images

The threat of Democrats using Congress’ funding power to enforce their investigative push is a serious one for both the administration and firms that do billions of dollars’ worth of contracting work for the federal government.

The coming months therefore look treacherous for CEOs and firms caught in Washington’s political stew, threatening bottom lines and raising the possibility of reputational damage to corporations that abhor such political complications.

Brad Smith, president and vice chairman of Microsoft — which contributed to the White House ballroom project, according to a list of donors provided by the administration — told CBS’ “Face the Nation” on Sunday that “we always have the same philosophy for every administration regardless of which political party it comes from. We partner where we can. We stand apart when we should.”

Trump’s executive order comes with teeth. It tasks the Office of Management and Budget with ensuring all contractors comply with its requirements “to enhance efficiency and the protection of Executive information.”

And White House Counsel Will Scharf told Garcia this month that the “administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred, or any other unlawful motive to intimidate, penalize, or interfere with the lawful functioning of government.”

It’s clear that one key outcome of the midterm elections will be a monumental clash over government power, the Constitution and the Trump’s vision of the presidency that will soon define the contours of the 2028 election.

World.title: Trump organization hosts ‘exclusive’ dinner to promote president’s meme coin
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s meme coin club held a private event at his golf club in Virginia on Sunday where the price of admission was a major stake in the cryptocurrency.

Trump was a featured speaker at the event for $TRUMP coin holders, which was advertised as an “evening of legends,” featuring boxing legend Floyd Mayweather and former NBA player Tristan Thompson. Also in attendance was “Shark Tank” investor Kevin O’Leary.

The White House referred CNN’s questions about the event to the hosts. The companies behind the event — CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight LLC — are affiliates of the Trump Organization. They did not respond to a request for comment. Trump’s official schedule on Sunday listed him going to the golf club, like many weekends, but did not specify that event.

The top 29 holders of the coin were promised a special VIP reception at the gala held at Trump’s National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, billed as a “once-in-a-lifetime experience.” The top four holders were promised a Trump 18-karat gold watch. The $TRUMP coin has about 224,000 holders, according to CoinMarketCap, which tracks live data for cryptocurrencies.

The Trump family’s rapidly expanding crypto empire has been a subject of concern for Democrats, who have alleged that the president is using his office for financial gain. The president attended a similar gala last May, which his critics called a textbook pay-to-play venture. During an interview on CBS’s “60 Minutes” earlier this month, Trump defended the fact his net worth has gone up by $3 billion since the start of his second term, largely due to cryptocurrency, comparing his earnings to those of previous presidents.

“Well, but they own something, whatever crypto was at the time,” the president said. “You know, there’s crypto and before that there was oil …”

The value of the $TRUMP meme coin has recently plummeted, trading at $0.89 on the Kraken cryptocurrency exchange Sunday after reaching $1.73 just before Halloween.

The venture is nonetheless likely to be among a list of targets for investigation by Democrats when they gain control of Congress in January. Last month, several Democrats sent a letter to the White House pushing for more details on the first meme coin gala.

On Sunday, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a ranking member of the Senate Judiciary Committee who last year sponsored a resolution condemning the meme coin venture, heaped fresh criticism on the operation.

“Trump is clearly more focused on profiting from his pump-and-dump meme coin operation than addressing Americans’ soaring cost of living crisis,” Blumenthal said in a statement. “He has put a ‘For Sale’ sign on the White House through the $TRUMP coin and other crypto dealings. Countless Americans have likely been deceived by an apparent pump-and-dump scheme that benefited a privileged set of insiders and cost ordinary investors billions of their hard-earned money.”

Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, or CREW, a liberal-leaning watchdog group, said the sweeping Republican midterm losses should serve as “a clear mandate” to the president and Congress that corruption is a top concern.

“Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner is the clearest evidence that he cares more about lining his pockets and giving access to his personal investors than addressing the problems facing the American public,” Sherman told CNN. “Congress needs to ensure oversight of and accountability for the president.”

Speaking to attendees Sunday, Trump expressed support for proposed legislation around cryptocurrency, known as the CLARITY Act, and said he believes there will be bipartisan support for it.

“In fact, I think we’re going to have a lot of bipartisan support for everything because I’ll be the veto king of the world,” he added.

The website for holders of the president’s meme coin states that it is “not political and has nothing to do with any political campaign or any political office or governmental agency.”

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: Israel escalates occupation of West Bank, with 50 structures demolished and 13 vehicles torched
World.content:
Israeli occupation forces and settlers escalated their attacks across various parts of the West Bank on Sunday, demolishing approximately 50 residential structures and livestock enclosures in the Northern Jordan Valley, and setting fire to 13 vehicles and an agricultural outbuilding in the governorates of Ramallah and al-Bireh, Hebron, and Salfit—all amid a wave of incursions and arrests.

The Palestinian News Agency (Wafa) reported that Israeli forces demolished about 50 residential structures and livestock enclosures, as well as water tanks belonging to Palestinian families in Khirbet Samra in the Northern Jordan Valley.

The structures were razed to the ground, leaving the residents and their livestock without shelter—a situation compounded by the prohibition against establishing infrastructure that would help them cope with harsh weather conditions and settler violence.

In Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate, Wafa—citing local sources—reported that settlers torched 12 vehicles during simultaneous attacks on three villages, while also spray-painting racist slogans on the walls of homes.

According to the sources, the settlers burned seven vehicles in the northern part of the village of Kafr Malik, east of Ramallah, and tree vehicles in the village of Deir Abu Mash’al, northwest of the city, before fleeing.

Additionally, they set fire to two vehicles in the village of Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah causing significant material damage.

In Nablus, occupation forces raided the Balata refugee camp, searching homes and ransacking their contents. They also distributed inflammatory leaflets, though no arrests were made during the incursion.

‘Jewish terrorism’

The leader of the “Yashar” party, Gadi Eizenkot, described the burning of Palestinian property—including homes and vehicles—as “Jewish terrorism,” stating that it threatens the lives of civilians and undermines regional stability.

Eizenkot criticized the policies of the Minister of National Security, Itamar Ben-Gvir, and the Minister of Finance, Bezalel Smotrich, arguing that their actions have pushed the situation toward chaos.

He urged the government and the security establishment to employ all available measures—including administrative detention and operations by the Shin Bet (Israel’s internal security service)—to pursue the perpetrators and impose severe penalties upon them.

The Israeli occupation army announced the deployment of military forces and Border Police personnel to four villages in the West Bank, following reports and video footage showing burned vehicles and racist graffiti.

Bloomberg reported that Israeli police investigators will enter the sites of the attacks under military protection to collect evidence and continue their investigations into the incidents.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egypt leads Russian tourist bookings in November with 32% share
World.content:
Egypt continues to top the list of most attractive destinations for Russian tourists this November, accounting for approximately 32 percent of organized tour package sales.

This serves as a fresh indicator of the strength of the Russian market for Egyptian tourism and reflects the enduring preference among Russian tourists for Egypt’s beach destinations during the winter season.

The Deputy Chairman of the Chamber of Tourism Establishments in the Red Sea, Essam Ali, said that Egypt has maintained its prominent position in terms of Russian tourism demand throughout November.

With its share of organized tour package sales increasing compared to last year, Egypt has reaffirmed its competitiveness against several other major international destinations vying for the Russian market, Ali added.

The tourism expert emphasized that for Egypt to maintain its leading position in the Russian market, it must continue to strike a balance between pricing and service quality—a necessity made all the more pressing by growing competition from Asian destinations.

Several factors at play

A reservations manager at a tourism company that brings visitors from Russia, Mahmoud Arafa, noted that Egypt’s continued lead in the Russian market depends on several factors.

Foremost among these is the warm winter weather, which is highly attractive to Russian tourists looking to escape freezing temperatures.

Furthermore, Egypt offers year-round beach tourism, a wide array of hotels and resorts, and diverse price points.

The country also boasts numerous diving centers, marine activities, desert excursions, and various entertainment programs.

The relative proximity of Egypt to the Russian market—compared to many Asian destinations—along with the availability of direct flights to Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, and Marsa Alam, serves as an additional factor that strengthens Egypt’s competitive edge.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Expert reveals reasons for recent decline in gold prices
World.content:
An expert on the gold market, Saeed Imbaby, revealed the reasons behind the recent decline in the price of the precious metal.

He explained that the local market is directly linked to global prices, and that fluctuations in the price of gold in Egypt reflect changes in the price per ounce on international exchanges.

Imbaby referred to two primary factors driving the recent drop in gold prices — the first is the significant losses sustained by technology stocks and various other investments, which prompted several investors to liquidate a portion of their gold holdings to cover their losses.

The second factor, he added, relates to the US Federal Reserve’s move toward raising interest rates, which has enhanced the appeal of the US dollar as an income-generating asset, in contrast to gold, which does not provide periodic returns to its holders.

Gold Retreats to $3,500

Imbaby noted that these developments have caused the global price per ounce to fall from $ 4,000 to approximately $ 3,500.

This shift has impacted the Egyptian market, where prices have declined to around LE 5,500 per gram.

The gold market expert emphasized that gold remains a means of preserving the value of savings over the long term—rather than a tool for speculation or quick gains—and cautioned against making buying or selling decisions based on daily price fluctuations.

He pointed to the historical trajectory of gold prices in the local market, noting that the precious metal has previously reached levels of LE1,000, LE3,000, LE5,000, and LE7,500.

He added that the current decline does not rule out the possibility of prices returning to higher levels in the future.

Rising Demand for Gold

Imbaby revealed a notable increase in demand for the precious metal over the past 48 hours, coinciding with a sharp decline in prices.

He explained that this surge in buying interest has pushed the price per gram in the local market up by approximately LE 100 relative to the global price.

The expert welcomed this shift in consumer behavior—noting that people are now opting to purchase gold during price dips rather than when prices are rising—and expressed an expectation that the price gap between the local and global markets will narrow when trading resumes on Monday.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: GTA 6 shatters entertainment industry records: The Washington Post
World.content:
In an unprecedented achievement for the global entertainment industry, The Washington Post reported that Grand Theft Auto 6 – the long-awaited installment of the GTA video game franchise – has reached a record-breaking sales of US$ 3.79 billion within just 24 hours of its release on Thursday.

According to the developer, Rockstar Games this marks the largest entertainment product launch in history—surpassing films, music, and other video games—amidst widespread global celebration and renewed concerns regarding the impact of its violent content.

The newspaper noted that Rockstar Games on Friday announced that 32.5 million copies had been sold prior to the official launch, shattering the record for pre-orders.

The game, which took 13 years to develop and involved tens of thousands of people, generated $1.5 billion in pre-order revenue.

It noted that pre-sales approached half the sales volume of Michael Jackson’s “Thriller”—the best-selling album in music history—while the game earned a score of 99 out of 100 on the platform Metacritic, making it the highest-rated video game ever.

The game surpassed the record set by its predecessor, GTA V, which reached one billion dollars in sales within three days in 2013.

For comparison, the film Avengers: Endgame (2019) took five days to reach the one billion dollar mark, while Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey took three weeks to hit that same figure.

The founder and president of Rockstar Games, Sam Houser, said that the company is deeply grateful for the extraordinary response from players around the world.

The Washington Post noted how the game has evolved into a cultural phenomenon that has swept through American society.

This includes promotional campaigns featuring brands like Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) and Heineken, as well as the Miami Heat basketball team wearing jerseys bearing the name Vice City—the fictional, Miami-inspired metropolis where the game is set.

The game features over 33,000 non-player characters and offers a wide array of unconventional activities—such as managing character weight, renovating homes, purchasing clothing, birdwatching, and interacting with pets—alongside a simulation of daily life infused with political and social satire.

The game has drawn criticism within the US Congress and raised security concerns regarding the impact of virtual violence, while police in San Juan, Texas, have issued warnings against imitating criminal behaviors outside the game world.

World.title: COP31 Ends Without Political Deal as Disputes Over Fossil Fuels and Finance Persist
World.content:
Countries adopted decisions on adaptation and just transition in Antalya, but failed to agree on the conference’s overarching political outcome. Photo: UNFCCC

Summary

COP31 ended without agreement on the proposed Antalya Pact after disagreements over fossil fuels, climate finance and the direction of global climate action.

Governments adopted decisions on adaptation and just transition, but failed to agree on the Mitigation Work Programme and several other proposals.

Developing countries left Antalya without a clear pathway for delivering adaptation finance, while attention turns to Ethiopia’s hosting of COP32 in 2027.

By Aria Deemie

The United Nations climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Sunday without agreement on its proposed overarching political deal, after nearly two extra days of negotiations exposed deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and how governments should respond to rising global temperatures.



“I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome,” United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement following the conference.

“There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science.”

The failure to adopt the proposed Antalya Pact left the conference without a common political statement addressing some of the most contested questions in climate action. But it did not mean all negotiations failed. Governments adopted separate decisions on issues including the Global Goal on Adaptation and the Just Transition Work Programme , while other proposals, including the Mitigation Work Programme , did not secure agreement.

The proposed Antalya Pact consisted of two Presidency-led decisions, one under the United Nations climate convention and another under the Paris Agreement. Together, they were intended to provide an overarching political response to the climate crisis and set direction for the next phase of international climate action.



But countries could not agree on the language. A central dispute was whether the decisions should explicitly address the transition away from fossil fuels, the main source of greenhouse gas emissions.
