World.title: Rescuing maps from the adventures of factions
World.content:
Is it true that the era that placed certain maps into the hands of factions has come to an end? Is it true that what remains of their reckless practices resemble farewell battles rather than the battles of the future? Is it true that the factions that hijacked the decision-making of these countries will find no choice before them other than releasing their hostages, whether they are states or individuals? And is it true that Iran, which played a decisive role in nurturing the “small parallel armies,” may no longer possess the capacity to implement its agenda of keeping the maps in the grip of these factions?

It is difficult to find definitive answers to these questions. We are in the Middle East. Its land gives birth to sudden surges, explosions and collapses. Yet the general impression suggests that people who have experienced the era of factions have developed a deep-seated conviction that “factions unsettle, while states reassure” and that “factions violate rights, while states nurture and protect them.”

Is it the feeling among a majority of Iraqis that there is an urgent need for a fully constituted state, allowing Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to demand that the “Republic of Jurf Al-Sakhar” return to the Iraqi state? And is it the feeling among a majority of Lebanese that there is an urgent need for the return of the state, prompting President Joseph Aoun to address Hezbollah in clear terms, which the party was not accustomed to before he became president and Nawaf Salam became prime minister?

The era of factions with regional roles opened the door to perils, horrors and the draining of resources and hopes Ghassan Charbel

Aoun said that the weapons “fulfilled their duty in a previous era, with sacrifices and achievements, then exhausted their own community, environment, people and country in a later stage, inflicting heavy losses on them and on us when they came to serve non-Lebanese causes. You must acknowledge this and you must hand over the weapons.”

In all likelihood, Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem will receive Aoun’s remarks with fury. None of Aoun’s predecessors among the generals who assumed the presidency dared to use such language, or even come close to it. Emile Lahoud committed himself in the Axis of Resistance, settling for whatever scraps the party and the Assad regime left for the state. Michel Suleiman was pushed into political isolation when he criticized the “wooden formula” of the “army, people and resistance” equation. It was difficult for Michel Aoun to demand the return of what had been wrested from the state, as it was an agreement with Hezbollah that allowed him to become president.

Joseph Aoun was speaking on Lebanon’s Independence Day. His clarity in addressing Hezbollah was matched by his clarity in addressing Iran. He said that “completing our independence today faces two fundamental, concurrent, interconnected and mutually reinforcing obstacles: the Israeli occupation of parts of our land and foreign interference in our affairs, specifically from certain influential factions within the Iranian regime, through arms and decision-making outside the authority of the Lebanese state.”

Aoun stressed that the two crises are “interconnected and concurrent, as each invites the other, uses it as a pretext and gives it a pretext in return,” noting that “in both cases, Lebanon is the one paying the price, particularly the south and its people, who since 1969 have borne the cost of successive wars, generation after generation.”

Illusions of a regional role are a poisoned chalice that factions drink from the moment they accept the role of proxy Ghassan Charbel

Hezbollah’s leadership is expected to be angered by Aoun’s remarks. Yet anger does not exempt it from the need to calmly assess the transformations that have reshaped the region following Yahya Sinwar’s Al-Aqsa Flood Operation. Israeli occupation has returned to parts of Gaza and southern Lebanon, Bashar Assad is preparing to mark his second anniversary in Russian exile and an Iraqi majority is rallying behind the call to prioritize the logic of the state over the logic of factions.

The region has grown weary of factions and the world has grown weary of them too. The era in which factions carved out regional roles for themselves through the possession of missiles and drones opened the door to perils, horrors and the draining of resources and hopes.

Hezbollah does not need anyone to tell it that a majority of Lebanese firmly oppose the war it launched under the banner of supporting Gaza, as well as the one it waged in support of Iran. This majority is equally aware of the danger of the roles the party has played in Syria and elsewhere. Hezbollah has no choice but to return from its regional expedition, while fully recognizing that placing all weapons exclusively under state authority means closing the chapter on the “unity of arenas.” Contemplating upending the domestic order in Lebanon would expose the party, its base and the entire country to unprecedented peril.

Joseph Aoun concluded from regional and international stances that the path to restoring Lebanese sovereignty over southern Lebanon and launching reconstruction inevitably runs through placing all arms under state control.

In Baghdad, Al-Zaidi concluded that there can be neither stability nor investment if armed enclaves continue to launch missiles and drones at neighboring states. He chose to close this chapter. Jurf Al-Sakhar had acquired the reputation of a sealed fortress, rumored among Iraqis to house tunnels, missile and drone workshops, and field courts. Many assumed that Jurf Al-Sakhar, which the factions wrested from the grip of Daesh, was lost for good and that its strategic location prevented its return to its original inhabitants.

Al-Zaidi punctured the mystique of the “Republic of Jurf Al-Sakhar” when he spoke publicly about oil smuggling and pipeline tapping. He brought the issue directly to the Coordination Framework and the State Administration Coalition, putting everyone on the spot by demanding that weapons remain exclusively in the hands of the state. While the resulting settlement bears the imprint of Quds Force commander Esmail Ghaani, who inherited from his predecessor the mission of preserving factions rather than sovereign states, the crisis nonetheless demonstrated that dismantling these “armed mini republics” can indeed begin.

Illusions of a regional role are a poisoned chalice that factions drink from the moment they accept the role of proxy. It begins with the mirage of an alliance with a powerful patron, followed by the steady surrender of independent decision-making in exchange for a flow of weapons. The balance of power is merciless: this is no ally — he is your general, your manager and your guide. And the deeper factions plunge into regional adventures, the greater the suffering inflicted upon sovereign nations.

The experience of the Houthis in Yemen is stark proof of the grim fate toward which maps are driven when factions seize control of decisions, resources and arsenals. Maps must be saved from the illusions of factions.

World.title: Who is fueling the religious war narrative in Palestine?
World.content:
A Palestinian Christian priest, Father Issa Thaljieh, was denied a US visa this month, seemingly for no other reason than the fact he is Palestinian. “I believe the reason for the rejection is that I’m a Palestinian and live in this Holy Land,” he said.

Around the same time, the US welcomed with open arms former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, who is wanted on war crimes charges, allowing him to attend a conference in New York despite an outstanding arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court.

The contrast is striking. But to call it mere hypocrisy is to miss the deeper contradiction it exposes: the deliberate distortion of how the Middle East and its people are portrayed.

For decades, the US government, its political class and powerful media institutions have relentlessly depicted the region as a breeding ground for violence and religious fanaticism, where wars are supposedly eternal and bloodshed an inevitable expression of ancient religious hatred.

This framing serves several purposes. It obscures the role of US military interventions, destructive foreign policies and colonialism; it portrays the West as the rational defender of civilization against Arab and Muslim “fanaticism;” and it casts Israel as the perpetual victim of the Middle East’s supposed religious fundamentalists.

For decades, the Middle East has been depicted as a breeding ground for violence and religious fanaticism Dr. Ramzy Baroud

Palestinians have repeatedly rejected attempts to frame their national struggle as a religious war, warning instead against the religious confrontation championed by Israel and its increasingly fanatical political leadership.

While Israeli ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich are often blamed for inflaming religious tensions, the truth is that Zionism itself has, from its inception, drawn upon religious claims and biblical entitlement to justify its political ambitions.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s November 2023 message to Israeli soldiers, which stated, “Remember what Amalek did to you,” was an articulation of this worldview — one that presents Israel as the fulfillment of prophecy and its actions, including genocide, as expressions of divine will.

Behind Israel stands a vast apparatus of religious fundamentalists, particularly in the US, who reinforce a worldview in which international law and human rights are rendered virtually irrelevant.

When US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee declared in February that Israel was a land given by God to a chosen people, he was, at least in his own mind, expressing a perfectly defensible position. After all, this is the same man who once declared: “There’s really no such thing as a Palestinian.”

The same religious fanaticism is evident in the words of extremist Israeli politician Moshe Feiglin, who, in an October interview, argued that killing babies in Gaza was morally justified. “I don’t want to see babies killed,” he said, before adding: “Morally, that should have been done.”

Religious fanaticism stands in stark contrast to how Palestinians themselves understand and invoke religious identity Dr. Ramzy Baroud

Such religious fanaticism stands in stark contrast to how Palestinians themselves understand and invoke religious identity.

Since Israel defines virtually every aspect of its existence as Jewish, from its army and settlements to its bypass roads and institutional privileges, ordinary Palestinians have adopted the term largely as a corresponding reference to Israel’s self-definition. Palestinians also invoke Jewish identity to emphasize that many Jews around the world stand firmly with Palestine.

The numbers challenge the assumption that Jewish identity necessarily translates into support for Israel’s wars. A May 2026 Jewish Voters Resource Center survey found that 55 percent of American Jewish respondents opposed the way Israel conducted its war in Gaza. And while American politicians and media elites sought to demonize Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, a survey found that 60 percent of Jewish early voters who participated in the Senate race supported him.

As for Palestinian Christians, their place within Palestinian society has never been a question of religious affiliation but of shared history and national belonging. They are an ancient, deeply rooted community, sharing with Palestinian Muslims a common culture, history, national identity and even bloodlines.

Long before Israel was established on the ruins of historic Palestine, the Muslim-Christian Associations emerged as a major civil society platform resisting British and Zionist colonialism. Beginning in 1918, they spread across Palestinian cities and helped organize the first Palestinian Arab Congress in 1919.

Although these institutions were dismantled following the creation of Israel, Palestinians continued to embrace an inclusive national identity, one in which the struggle against oppression had room for all.

With few exceptions, the sinister framing of the Middle East as inherently fanatical has largely emerged from the West, allowing Western governments to claim the moral high ground and portray themselves as heroes rather than villains.

Yet these supposed saviors could not accommodate a Palestinian Christian priest seeking to deliver a message of peace and equality, which he ultimately conveyed through Zoom. His message was politically inconvenient precisely because it echoed long-standing warnings that Israel’s mounting pressure is driving Christians from the Holy Land.

Gallant, on the other hand, who oversaw Israel’s military campaign during much of the genocide in Gaza, was free to travel to the US and address American audiences without the slightest hindrance.

This might seem confusing to those accustomed to viewing the Middle East through the simplistic division between “us,” the supposed defenders of freedom and diversity, and “them,” the violent religious fanatics.

But this is the outcome of the West’s religious framing. It does not merely demonize Palestinians and, by extension, Arabs and Muslims. It distorts the very political questions we ask, turning the aggressor into the victim and aggression into liberation, supposedly carried out in God’s name.

It is time to tear away this screen of bigotry and hatred and listen to Palestinians themselves. Their struggle is not a religious war but an enduring fight for justice, freedom and lasting peace — a vision that Israel and its supporters, the true fanatics in this story, have consistently refused to embrace.

World.title: Iraq weighs 10m-barrel oil supply deal with Egypt
World.content:
RIYADH: Iraq is studying a proposal to supply Egypt with approximately 10 million barrels of oil as the two countries seek to expand economic cooperation during Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s visit to Cairo.

The proposed quantity remains under consideration, Iraqi Deputy Trade Minister for Administrative Affairs Sattar Al-Jabiri told the Iraqi News Agency. No delivery timeframe or financial terms have been announced.

The discussions also cover alternative routes for Iraqi oil exports to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, alongside efforts to diversify imports of construction materials and food and expand Iraqi exports.

Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to Egypt was scheduled for Nov. 23, with President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi expected to discuss bilateral relations and regional developments with him, Ahram reported, citing the Egyptian presidency.

Energy cooperation

Ahead of the visit, Egyptian Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi met Iraqi Ambassador Qahtan Taha Khalaf to discuss cooperation in the oil and gas sectors, according to Ahram Business.

Badawi said recent talks with his Iraqi counterpart had identified opportunities to broaden cooperation.

The Iraqi ambassador said Baghdad wanted to expand its economic and petroleum partnerships with Cairo.

The visit coincides with the fourth session of the countries’ Joint Higher Committee, which is preparing agreements covering economic, commercial and financial cooperation.

Al-Jabiri said the committee is prioritizing arrangements that could be implemented and monitored, rather than simply increasing the number of agreements.

Banking and investment

The negotiations also include the reactivation of the licence for the Cairo branch of Rafidain Bank, which operated from the 1980s before its licence was suspended in 2005.

Iraq is seeking to restore the previous licence rather than obtain a new one. Al-Jabiri said specialist committees had been formed and an Iraqi feasibility study submitted.

Baghdad has also issued a ministerial order establishing an Iraqi-Egyptian Business Council, with the necessary procedures on the Egyptian side still pending.

Preparations are under way for an economic, investment and trade forum in Cairo in mid-2027 to showcase Iraqi investment opportunities and products and strengthen business partnerships.

World.title: Saudi construction costs rise 2.3% in October: GASTAT
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s construction costs rose 2.3 percent year on year in October, with equipment and machinery rental recording the sharpest increases, adding to budget pressures for developers and contractors amid an expanding project pipeline.

The Kingdom’s Construction Cost Index reached 104.1 in October, compared with 104 in September and 101.7 a year earlier, according to the General Authority for Statistics.

Costs in the residential sector increased 2.2 percent, while non-residential construction costs climbed 2.7 percent.

The increase comes as construction markets across the Gulf face mounting pressure from material prices, labour shortages and supply-chain uncertainty.

JLL forecasts construction cost inflation in the Middle East at 5.7 to 7.7 percent in 2026, easing to 3.4 to 5.4 percent in 2027.

Saudi Arabia’s construction market is also operating against a substantial development pipeline.

Knight Frank valued projects planned or underway in the Kingdom at $2.07 trillion in the first half of 2026, including $1.13 trillion in construction and real estate developments.

The consultancy said rising construction costs, supply-chain disruption and regional tensions were adding pressure to project delivery and financial viability.

Construction activity expands

Despite the cost pressures, Saudi construction activity expanded for a sixth consecutive month in October, according to the Al Rajhi Capital Saudi Construction Index compiled by S&P Global.

The seasonally adjusted index eased to 52.3 from 54.4 in September but remained above the 50-point threshold separating expansion from contraction.

In its latest report, GASTAT said: “The increase (in residential sector) was attributed to a 1.8 percent rise in the cost of basic materials, due to the increase in the prices of timber and joinery by 3.4 percent.”

It added: “The costs of renting equipment and machinery also increased by 4 percent, driven by the increase in the costs of renting equipment and machinery with an operator by 5.4 percent.”

In the residential sector, labour costs rose by 1.6 percent in October compared with the same month in 2025, while energy costs increased by 3 percent.

Munir Al-Daraawi, founder and CEO of Orla Properties, told Arab News that the current CCI trend points to a market that is expanding in a measured and disciplined manner, allowing stakeholders to forecast costs with greater confidence and maintain project momentum.

“A gradual and predictable increase is far more manageable than periods of sharp volatility. The data demonstrates that Saudi Arabia’s construction sector continues to strike a healthy balance between growth and cost control,” said Al-Daraawi.

Non-residential sector

The rise in construction costs in the non-residential sector was driven by a 5.8 percent increase in equipment and machinery rental costs, including a 7.2 percent increase in the cost of renting equipment and machinery with an operator.

Labor costs rose by 2.1 percent and energy costs increased by 3 percent. Basic materials costs climbed by 2 percent, reflecting a 4.4 percent rise in other building materials and a 2.1 percent increase in timber and joinery prices.

Maurice Salem, partner at Arthur D. Little, said: “On projects already under construction, prices are largely agreed, so most of the increase is absorbed within existing contracts.

“The bigger effect is on projects still being priced, especially non-residential ones, where costs are up 2.7 percent.”

He added: “There I would expect tighter budgets and earlier booking of equipment and materials.”

Modest monthly increase

According to GASTAT, the CCI increased by 0.1 percent month on month in October, mainly due to a 0.1 percent rise in non-residential construction costs, while residential costs remained unchanged at the published one-decimal precision.

Al-Daraawi said the modest monthly increase of 0.1 percent was an encouraging indicator that the market was managing cost inflation relatively well despite sustained construction activity.

He added: “It suggests that while demand remains strong, the industry is gradually adapting through improved procurement practices, greater supply-chain coordination, and more efficient resource allocation.”

World.title: Qatar’s inward FDI climbs as country targets $100bn by 2030
World.content:
RIYADH: Qatar’s inward foreign direct investment stock increased 5.2 percent in the second quarter of 2026 to reach 180.6 billion Qatari riyals ($49.6 billion), marking its third consecutive quarterly record.

Data released by the National Planning Council showed that around 95 percent of Qatar’s inward FDI stock was concentrated in five economic activities.

Mining and quarrying accounted for the largest share at 41.3 percent, followed by financial and insurance activities at 36 percent and manufacturing at 11.7 percent.

Information and communication accounted for a further 3.8 percent, while professional, scientific and technical activities made up the remaining 1.9 percent.

Qatar sets $100bn FDI target for 2030

Qatar is targeting $100 billion in FDI by 2030 as part of its Ministry of Commerce and Industry Strategy, which also aims to achieve a compound annual growth rate of 3.4 percent in non-oil sectors by 2030.

The plan forms part of the country’s efforts to diversify its economy and strengthen its investment environment.

The country’s National Manufacturing Strategy for 2024–2030 also aims to raise the manufacturing sector’s value added to 70.5 billion riyals, increase non-hydrocarbon exports to 49 billion riyals and attract annual industrial investments of 2.75 billion riyals by 2030.

Qatar’s outward FDI stock declines

The newly released QNA statement said: “Regarding Qatari investments abroad, the survey results showed that the stock of outward FDI decreased by 2.5 percent compared with the first quarter of 2026, reaching 220.7 billion riyals.”

It added: “The results indicated that this stock represents investment abroad controlled by companies resident in the State of Qatar, noting that around 95 percent of this stock is concentrated in five economic activities: financial and insurance activities, at 36.2 percent, mining and quarrying, at 26.8 percent, information and communication, at 15.2 percent, accommodation and food service activities, at 9.1 percent, and transportation and storage at 7.3 percent.”

Survey methodology, coverage

The National Planning Council said the survey forms part of its efforts to strengthen national economic statistics and provide reliable data to support decision-making and track progress toward development targets.

The preliminary estimates cover inward and outward FDI positions among privately owned and selected public enterprises, while also incorporating Qatar Central Bank data covering monetary financial institutions, including banks, insurance companies and other financial institutions.

They exclude international financial transactions conducted by individuals and government entities.

The second quarter 2026 survey was based on a sample of approximately 210 enterprises operating in Qatar.

World.title: Razane Jammal scores brand ambassador role
World.content:
DUBAI: Lebanese British actress Razane Jammal has been named a regional brand ambassador for haircare brand Pantene Arabia.

The actress and children’s book author joins the Procter & Gamble-owned brand in its latest regional celebrity partnership.

She shared a photograph on Instagram to announce the news, followed by a video which she captioned, in part: “My hair has always been an extension of my personality, and as an actress, it plays such an important role in bringing my characters to life.”

Jammal is no stranger to the world of fashion and beauty endorsements. In 2022, she was appointed Middle East brand ambassador for French luxury house Dior, before expanding her relationship with the label to include its beauty division in January 2024. She also became a Middle East ambassador for Cartier in 2024.

Born and raised in Beirut, Jammal’s early film credits include Olivier Assayas’ “Carlos,” Kanye West’s experimental short film “Cruel Summer” and the Liam Neeson-led thriller “A Walk Among the Tombstones.”

She went on to build a profile across both Hollywood and Arab productions, appearing in Netflix’s Egyptian supernatural series “Paranormal” in 2020 before gaining international recognition for her portrayal of Lyta Hall in the streaming platform’s fantasy series “The Sandman” in 2022.

Closer to home, she starred opposite Syrian actor Bassel Khaiat in the popular Arabic drama “Al Thaman,” which premiered in 2023 and was adapted from the Turkish series “Bin Bir Gece.”

More recently, Jammal appeared in Egyptian filmmaker Mohamed Diab’s historical action drama “Asad,” alongside Mohamed Ramadan. Her performance also earned her the Best Actress in a Cinematic Role award at the Arab Satellite Festival in Cairo in September 2026.

Jammal also authored children’s book “Lulu and Blu,” published in 2025 by Turning Point Books.

The story was illustrated by Sasha Haddad, a Lebanese illustrator who graduated from Cambridge School of Arts in 2014. It follows the adventures of two young friends — a vegetarian lioness and a friendly fish — as they navigate themes of friendship, curiosity and self-discovery. The book draws on Jammal’s multicultural background and encourages children to embrace diversity, kindness and imagination.

Beyond acting, Jammal has become a regular presence at international fashion events and has appeared in campaigns for some of the industry’s most prominent luxury labels.

World.title: Lebanon denounces Israeli military official’s visit to school in south
World.content:
BEIRUT: Lebanese officials have denounced a visit by an Israeli military spokesperson to a school in a Christian village in an Israeli-occupied area of southern Lebanon.

On Sunday, as Lebanon marked its independence day, the Israeli military’s Arabic-language spokesperson Ella Waweya shared a video showing her outside a school in Debl and then standing in front of a classroom of children.

The village is located inside the “security zone” that Israel declared after the latest war erupted with Hezbollah in March and which covers a strip of southern Lebanon along the border around 10 kilometers (six miles) deep.

It is among a number of Christian-majority villages near the frontier where many residents have refused to leave despite Israeli military orders to evacuate.

Cut off from the rest of Lebanon, they are largely dependent on humanitarian aid.

#لبنان الأرز، لبنان #فيروز والرحابنة، لبنان الجبال والقرى الحلوة، لبنان اللي غنّتله فيروز بحبك يا لبنان…وطن بيستاهل السلام والأمان والحياة. بزيارتي الأخيرة لجنوب لبنان، شفت جمال الأرض، بس الأجمل كان الأمل بعيون الأطفال، وأحلامهن البسيطة بمستقبل آمن وأيام أحلى. بعيد الاستقلال، بتمنّى للبنان استقلال بكل معانيه: حرية، كرامة، سلام، وقرار حرب وسلم بإيد الدولة اللبنانية وحدها. لأن لبنان بيستاهل يكون وطن الأحلام، مش ساحة للحروب. وبيستاهل يسمع صوت فيروز. 🇱🇧🌲 مني أنا، اللفتنانت كولونيل إيلا واوية (كابتن إيلا) من القلب، كل عام ولبنان وأهله بألف خير. — Lieutenant Colonel Ella Waweya | إيلا واوية (@CaptainElla1) November 22, 2026

“During my last visit to south Lebanon, I was amazed by the beauty of the land and the villages which have paid a heavy price due to their exploitation... by a terrorist organization,” Waweya said, referring to the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group.

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam later denounced Israel for “dragging students into a military and propaganda display.”

“An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south,” he added.

Lebanese Education Minister Rima Karami condemned what she called an “attack on the Debl school and its students.”

The Debl municipality said the visit took place around a month earlier “without any prior coordination with the school’s administration.”

Since the video’s publication, the village and local officials have been targeted on social media with accusations of collaborating with Israel.

Such attacks are particularly incendiary in the area because Israel relied on local collaborators during its around two-decade-long occupation of southern Lebanon, which ended in 2000.

The municipality said that the choice by residents to remain was not “acceptance of the occupation” but rather “an expression of our attachment to our Lebanese land.”

Residents “for long months have lived in exceptional and difficult conditions under the Israeli military presence,” it said.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March with rocket fire at Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion.

Lebanon says Israeli attacks since then have killed more than 4,300 people.

World.title: Armenia proposes new constitution in step toward peace with Azerbaijan
World.content:
TBILISI: Armenia published a draft proposal of a new constitution on Monday, a major step toward signing a formal peace agreement with its neighbor and long-time foe Azerbaijan.

The charter’s unveiling puts pressure on Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to secure a deal with Baku after he won a new term in office in June in a vote widely viewed as a referendum on his handling of the peace process.

“I stake my entire political, human and moral credibility on this issue and say that after the adoption of the new Constitution, we will not only sign ‌and ratify ‌a peace agreement with Azerbaijan, but will also have ‌institutional, lasting and irreversible peace,” Pashinyan said in an address to the nation shortly after the draft was published on Monday, according to the Armenpress state news agency.

Armenia and Azerbaijan, neighbors in the South Caucasus, had been at intermittent war since the late 1980s, mostly over the mountainous region of Nagorno-Karabakh, controlled for decades by ethnic Armenians but recaptured by Azerbaijan in 2023 in a lightning offensive. The two countries signed a joint US-backed peace ‌declaration last August.

Since then they have ‌begun to rebuild trade links and say they are in a state of “real ‌peace.”

But for Azerbaijan, a central sticking point to signing a formal ‌deal has been the preamble of Armenia’s constitution, which contains a reference to another Soviet-era document calling for the reunification of Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh, then an autonomous region in Soviet Azerbaijan.

The proposed new constitution rewrites the preamble and removes the ‌reference to which Baku has objected.

High stakes for PM Pashinyan

Pashinyan has pledged to resign if the Armenian people vote against the new constitution in a referendum, a move that would trigger snap elections in which he has promised not to run. To reach the two-thirds majority needed to call a constitutional referendum, Pashinyan must convince at least six opposition legislators to join his ruling Civil Contract party. The new charter would also undergo a public debate.

Armenia’s main opposition parties have so far rejected the draft.

In the run-up to the June election, Pashinyan faced a wave of criticism from the opposition and some sections of the public. They accuse him of capitulating to Azerbaijan, particularly since Baku’s 2023 military operation when it retook Karabakh, which prompted nearly all of the territory’s ethnic Armenian population to flee to Armenia.

World.title: Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission outlines 10-year roadmap for peaceful nuclear reactor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission announced on Monday, November 23, 2026, that constructing a peaceful nuclear reactor will take roughly seven to ten years, confirming that authorities are preparing to launch immediate preparatory steps—including specialized workforce training, laboratory construction, and radiopharmaceutical projects—ahead of full-scale reactor operations.

In statements to the official newspaper, Murtadha Adhab, Iraq’s National Liaison Officer with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), emphasized that peaceful nuclear applications span agriculture, industry, education, and broader sectoral development.

He highlighted the practical role of radioactive materials in sterilizing medical supplies and preserving agricultural seeds over extended storage periods to prevent spoilage.

Rather than delaying progress until a reactor is fully built, Adhab explained that the commission is actively coordinating with relevant state institutions to bring near-term strategic projects into execution.

Foremost among these is a radiopharmacy initiative focused on producing medical radioisotopes. Under the commission’s phased roadmap, initial efforts will prioritize qualifying technical personnel, establishing specialized laboratories, and initiating radioisotope fractionation processes before transitioning to full domestic isotope production once the reactor comes online.

Adhab underscored that Iraq’s nuclear reactor and all associated atomic energy programs are strictly dedicated to peaceful purposes. He noted that this commitment is firmly enshrined in the Iraqi Constitution and governed by domestic legislation as well as the international treaties and IAEA safeguards agreements ratified by Baghdad.

World.title: US dollar drops noticeably to 168,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar recorded a notable drop across major domestic parallel markets on Monday morning, November 23, 2026, breaking well below the 170,000-dinar threshold as purchasing bids harmonized at 168,000 IQD per $100 across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

According to morning trading figures, physical banknote rates across Iraq’s three primary commercial hubs opened as follows.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 168,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,000 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted slightly lower retail selling rates at 168,300 IQD alongside matching buying bids of 168,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices mirrored Baghdad’s pricing, listing retail selling rates at 168,500 IQD and purchasing offers at 168,000 IQD per $100.

Despite the noticeable retreat toward the 168,000-dinar mark, parallel cash rates still maintain a spread of 16,300 to 16,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Al Zaidi arrives in Cairo for talks with El Sisi
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi arrived in the Egyptian capital, Cairo, on Monday, November 23, 2026, at the start of an official visit aimed at expanding bilateral economic, political, and regional cooperation, where he was received upon arrival by Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly.

According to an official statement from the Prime Minister’s Media Office, Al-Zaidi’s itinerary begins with a summit meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.

Following their bilateral talks, Al-Zaidi will co-chair a session of the Iraqi-Egyptian Joint Higher Committee alongside Madbouly, culminating in the signing of a package of bilateral memoranda of understanding and cooperation agreements spanning multiple economic and infrastructure sectors.

Beyond bilateral government sessions, Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit the headquarters of the League of Arab States in Cairo to meet with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy and deliver a formal address before the permanent representatives of Arab member states.

The Prime Minister’s agenda also includes field visits to key development sites and a dedicated roundtable with prominent Egyptian business leaders and investors to promote private-sector participation in Iraqi reconstruction and investment projects.

World.title: Asian tech back in the firing line as traders track Wall St rout
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stock markets struggled to recover from last week’s sell-off, with tech firms again in the firing line as investors tracked an eye-watering rout on Wall Street.

A healthy bounce in US futures was unable to inspire buying amid fears over the AI trade, the prospect of more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and tighter regulation under a Democrat-led Congress.

Scandal-hit Nvidia characterised the collapse in New York on Friday, plunging 14 percent and helping to drag the Nasdaq into negative territory for the year.

The index has lost almost a fifth of its value since hitting a record high just last month, with strong earnings from Nvidia and a blockbuster IPO from Claude-creator Anthropic unable to staunch the bloodletting.

The selling continued into Asia, with Seoul diving more than four percent as chip titans SK hynix and Samsung dropped four percent each.

“These are not peripheral players in the AI boom but two of its most important semiconductor suppliers,” said SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“Their continued weakness suggests investors are still more interested in reducing exposure than celebrating a few hours of improved sentiment in US futures.”

The losses have led authorities in some countries to introduce measures aimed at minimising the negative impact.

Taiwan was making it harder to short stocks, while China made it easier to borrow money to buy them and South Korea eyed a stabilisation fund not used since the global financial crisis.

Taipei flickered between gains and losses but Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Jakarta were all deep in negative territory.

Tokyo was closed for a holiday.

Meanwhile, the VIX Index — which is seen as the market’s fear gauge — spiked to its highest level since April last year, when Donald Trump unveiled his wide-ranging tariff bazooka.

Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department’s move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia’s powerful AI chips remotely.

Fiona Cincotta at Forex.com said “nerves have been showing in the AI trade, amid increased scrutiny over AI capital expenditure, the scale of investment, the returns on those investments and when they might materialise”.

“Furthermore, the Democrats taking control of Congress, which is expected to slow the AI buildout, combined with expectations of higher rates for longer, are fueling concerns about the sector.”

World.title: Miami blow past Thunder, Hawks down Pistons in NBA action
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Miami Heat romped past the injury-hit Oklahoma City Thunder 123-113 to extend their winning streak to seven games in the NBA on Sunday.

Miami, who started without the injured Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin strain), took full advantage of a depleted Thunder line-up to record a wire-to-wire win.

Bam Adebayo led Miami with a triple-double, finishing with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists with two steals and three blocks.

Pelle Larsson added 21 points while Nikola Jovic scored 15 from the bench as seven Miami players finished in double figures.

“Coming into the game, obviously one of your best players is out of the game, so the next player has to step up – and that was me,” Adebayo said, referring to Antetokounmpo’s absence.

“We took care of business. I didn’t like how we finished the fourth quarter, but a W (win) is a W,” Adebayo added.

“We’re getting stops, we’re running in transition, we’re sharing the ball and guys are making plays for one another.”

Miami improved to 10-6 for the season after the victory while Oklahoma City, who were without reigning NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, fell to 10-7.

The Atlanta Hawks meanwhile improved to 11-6 with a 107-97 defeat of the Detroit Pistons.

Nickeil Alexander-Walker rattled in six three-pointers to finish with 27 points as Atlanta erupted in the fourth quarter to extend their winning streak to four games.

Detroit trailed by 10 points midway through the second quarter, but rallied to lead by as many as 13 in the third quarter before taking an 11-point advantage into the final frame.

But Atlanta flipped the script in the fourth quarter, embarking on an 18-0 run to take the lead before outscoring the Pistons 33-12 to surge to victory.

Isaiah Joe led Detroit’s scoring with 19 off the bench but Cade Cunningham was restricted to just five points while serving up 15 assists.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt FMs prepare for Iraqi PM’s imminent visit to Cairo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met in the southern city of Aswan on Sunday to prepare for the Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Cairo and to coordinate on regional security.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the sixth Aswan Forum for Sustainable Peace and Development.

Both ministers focused on preparations for al-Zaidi’s scheduled visit to Cairo on Monday, alongside the fourth session of the Egyptian-Iraqi Joint Higher Committee.

Abdelatty emphasized Egypt’s commitment to boosting trade and investment, specifically targeting greater participation by Egyptian firms in Iraq’s infrastructure, energy, transport, and reconstruction projects.

The two diplomats exchanged views on ongoing regional crises and security challenges, calling for political and diplomatic resolutions to maintain close bilateral consultations.

The fourth session of the Joint Higher Committee aims to build on cooperation agreements signed previously, while both nations continue advancing regional integration through the Egypt-Iraq-Jordan trilateral cooperation mechanism.

Al-Zaidi, accompanied by a high-level government delegation, will meet with senior Egyptian officials—including President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi—to promote bilateral ties and expand Egyptian corporate participation in Iraqi infrastructure.

World.title: Pochettino demands response from ‘painful’ Man Utd debut
World.content:
Liverpool – Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card.

Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak.

United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick.

Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974.

“It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino.

“We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.”

Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro.

“I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino.

“At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.”

– ‘Changes the game completely’ –

A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes.

However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half.

“It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro.

“There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international.

“It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.”

Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory.

Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time.

“It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola.

“We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.”

World.title: Iraq offers $33 per barrel discount for December oil sales
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil is once again being offered at significant discounts for shipments that will be loaded in December 2026, as challenges related to crude oil exports from the country’s southern ports persist.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to offer Basra crude shipments with discounts reaching as much as $33 per barrel.

These offers cover both Basra Medium and Basra Heavy crude grades for loading in December, with buyers left to determine the specific quantities they wish to purchase.

These new discounts follow similar offers for October shipments—which reached as high as $37 per barrel—as Baghdad seeks to maintain its oil export flows amid rising shipping and insurance costs, as well as risks associated with navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO views the discounts on Iraqi oil as an opportunity to market shipments of Basra crude for this coming December, particularly with the ongoing crisis related to the restricted passage of tankers through the strategic waterway.

The offers include Basra Medium crude at a discount of $29.20 per barrel and Basra Heavy crude at a discount of $33 per barrel.

The discounts have narrowed by $5.30 per barrel for Basra Medium crude and by $4 per barrel for Basra Heavy crude compared to oil shipments in October.

World.title: 'We stand ready': China signals push to ease business visa process for Indians amid reported curbs
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports of a slowdown in visa issuance to Indian nationals."China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said in a written response to questions from news agency PTI."We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson added.The remarks come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business travellers.According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair provides a platform for businesses from around the world to showcase their products to Chinese consumers.Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, a service provider, from accepting visa applications, with Chinese diplomatic missions now handling them directly amid rising demand for visas, particularly business visas.Visa arrangements between the two countries have improved since India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years. The move was part of efforts to repair bilateral ties, which came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.The resumption of tourist visas was seen as a significant step towards normalising relations after years of strained ties.As part of efforts to ease travel, the two countries also resumed direct air connectivity between several cities, including the Beijing-New Delhi route.According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has come down to around seven per cent in recent months to encourage business and tourism-related travel to India.China, meanwhile, launched the "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December last year, allowing them to apply for visas online.Responding to a question on the status of bilateral relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September this year, the spokesperson said Beijing was ready to work with New Delhi to strengthen ties."The most important common understanding they (PM Modi and Xi) reached is that China and India need to be partners. Both sides are working to deliver on this important common understanding."China stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalisation, and contribute to world peace and prosperity," the spokesperson said.

World.title: SC directs West Bengal SIR tribunals to prioritise appeals challenging voter exclusion
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Monday directed the appellate tribunals hearing appeals related to the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to give preference to pleas filed by voters challenging their exclusion from the electoral rolls, while deferring those contesting the inclusion of names.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the tribunals to separate appeals challenging voter exclusions from those contesting inclusions, and give priority to the exclusions.

The bench further directed the tribunals to prioritise, within the exclusion-related appeals, cases involving voters under the jurisdiction of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, given that civic body elections are due to be held soon.

World.title: 'Stop acting like Baahubali': SC raps Bihar judicial officer for FIR against SP for disobeying directions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Monday pulled up a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a police officer over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR. The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and telling him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers.

The bench also suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy.

"Ask your client to stop acting like a 'Bahubali' while exercising judicial powers," Chief Justice Surya Kant said while hearing the judicial officer's plea against a Patna high court order staying his decision.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana criticised district and additional sessions judge-IV, Rohtas at Sasaram, Anil Kumar for convicting the police officer on the same day and treating the non-compliance as an offence committed in the face of the court.



"We are really surprised at your understanding of law. You must first understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 BNSS and Section 345 CrPC. If someone slaps someone or abuses the court, or refuses to leave the courtroom when directed, that is an offence committed in the face of the court. But if we direct someone to register an FIR and they do not, it does not amount to a crime committed in the face of the court," news agency PTI quoted the bench as saying.





"Your understanding of law is appalling. You also took such an aggressive stance, called the superintendent and convicted him on the same day," Justice Bagchi said.

Questioning the judge's objection to an inspecting judge's intervention, Justice Bagchi said, "Were you within your domain and jurisdiction when you called the district magistrate and superintendent of police, treated their non-appearance as an offence committed in the face of the court and convicted and sentenced him? You also stay your hands.

On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas, for wilfully disobeying court directions to register an FIR against a person who had allegedly given false evidence in a criminal case decided in 2023.

The judicial officer imposed a symbolic fine of Rs 1 on the SP and directed Bihar's director general of police (DGP) to enter the court's observations into the officer's service records. Key takeaways from PM Modi-Balen Shah meet

Saryu-Kamala Express to connect Ayodhya and Janakpur

Eight agreements signed across key sectors

Balen Shah highlights shared ties, climate cooperation

Balen Shah's first bilateral visit to India

NEW DELHI: India and Nepal on Monday signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development, following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.The two leaders also virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal, and jointly inaugurated several development projects during Balen Shahâs two-day state visit to India.At a joint press conference after the talks, Modi said the two countries had taken several important decisions to strengthen bilateral relations.âI am very pleased to welcome Balendra Shah ji to India on his first bilateral visit after becoming the Prime Minister of Nepal. A few months ago, when he addressed the United Nations as the worldâs youngest Prime Minister, we got a clear glimpse of his vision. Over the past few hours of our discussions, I have sensed his clear vision and commitment towards Nepalâs future and India-Nepal relations. The historic mandate given to him by the people of Nepal this year reflects the aspirations and hopes of the countryâs younger generation. India has always been a partner in the development journey of a strong and prosperous Nepal.In this spirit, today we have taken several important decisions to take our relations to new heights,â PM Modi said.The prime minister also announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepalâs reconstruction and long-term development, particularly in the wake of the devastating floods in August.âWe express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. Today, we announce a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees to give fresh impetus to Nepalâs reconstruction and long-term development. Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities, and further strengthen Nepalâs capacity to deal with future disasters,â he said.PM Modi also highlighted the shared religious and cultural ties between the two countries, referring to the launch of the train service connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur.âLord Ram and Mata Sita are symbols of our shared civilisation and faith. In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said that our pilgrimage sites are incomplete without Nepal, and our Lord Ram is incomplete without Nepal. In 2024, the consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla took place in Ayodhya. This historic occasion gave renewed strength to our shared faithâ¦With the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express train service today, we are giving a new dimension to this sacred bond,â he said.He said India had maintained supplies of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year, and expressed confidence in the future of bilateral ties.âWe will together write a golden chapter of India-Nepal relations,â PM Modi said.The Saryu-Kamala Express will connect Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, covering around 604 km in approximately 19 hours. The regular service will operate once a week in each direction from November 28, enabling pilgrims to travel between the two religious destinations without changing trains.The inaugural run on Monday operated as a special train (No. 04295), departing from Ayodhya Dham at 12.30 pm.The eight MoUs exchanged after the delegation-level talks cover satellite communication, policing, forensic sciences, civil service training, healthcare, traditional medicine, sustainable urban development, and livestock and fisheries development.In the space and communication sector, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Nepalâs Ministry of Information and Communication signed an MoU to establish a Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the utilisation of the South Asia Satellite.Two agreements aim to strengthen cooperation in policing and forensic sciences. One provides for academic and research collaboration between the National Forensic Sciences University in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and the Crime Investigation Department of Nepal Police. The other was signed between Indiaâs Rashtriya Raksha University and Nepalâs National Police Academy.For capacity building in public administration, the National Centre for Good Governance, under Indiaâs Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, signed an MoU with Nepalâs Administrative Staff College under the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration. The agreement provides for training programmes for Nepalese civil servants.In healthcare, Indiaâs Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Nepalâs Ministry of Health and Food Safety signed an MoU on cooperation in health and medicine. The two sides also signed a government-to-government agreement on cooperation in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.The remaining two agreements provide for technical cooperation in sustainable urban development and collaboration in livestock and fisheries development.At the joint press conference, Balen Shah described India-Nepal relations as being founded on mutual respect, trust and goodwill.âTies between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans,â he said.He expressed confidence that the agreements and initiatives announced during the visit would take bilateral relations to a new level, while stressing the need for cooperation on climate change.âI am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to build on the strong foundation of this enduring relationship and lay solid pillars for the future. Our Himalayas, the sources of clean water, sustain millions across this region. The pristine rivers flowing from the Himalayas into the Ganga remind us of our future and destiny, underscoring the need to address the challenges of climate change through collective action. Nepal and India have been bound by historical, cultural and civilisational ties since the sacred era of Lord Ram and Mata Janaki,â Balen Shah said.Balen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day state visit, his first to India since assuming office in March 2026.On Monday, PM Modi received him at Hyderabad House for the bilateral talks. Before the meeting, Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan and paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at the Raj Ghat memorial.Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post on X that the leaders would discuss various aspects of bilateral relations and explore new avenues to deepen cooperation.Jaiswal described the ceremonial welcome as reflecting âthe special warmth and enduring friendship between India and Nepalâ and Shahâs visit to Raj Ghat as âA tribute to the timeless legacy of Mahatma!â

World.title: Dhanraj murder verdict a strong message against political violence: HM Ramesh Chennithala
World.content:
Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said the court verdict in the C.V. Dhanraj murder case sends a strong message against political violence. He also asserted that there is no place for politics of murder in Keralam.

Speaking to media persons in Pathanamthitta, Mr. Chennithala said the murders of Dhanraj and Indian Union Muslim League worker Abdul Shukkoor were unacceptable in a democratic society and should have no place in the State. The government’s consistent stand was to support the victims of political violence, he added.

While three Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) - Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) workers were found guilty in the Dhanraj murder case, 17 other accused (including one who was murdered later) were acquitted.

Referring to the outcome of the case, the Home Minister said the possibility of an appeal would be considered after examining the judgment and consulting the victim’s family.

Mr. Chennithala also pointed out that the government’s position was to stand with the victims and their families, irrespective of political affiliations. “Whether in the case of Dhanraj or Shukkoor, the government would seriously consider an appeal if the families wanted one.” he said.

Minister for Higher Education of Keralam Roji M. John attended the ceremony as chief guest and delivered the convocation address. He emphasised the importance of innovation, research, technological advancement and social responsibility in the higher education sector.
